title_en: Americans Lost Nearly $18 Billion Last Year to Cyberscams. Is Washington Doing Enough to Help Them Get It Back?
excerpt_en: A Congressional investigation identifies gaps in federal efforts to help Americans recover billions of dollars lost to scammers online.

enrich.title_zh: 美国人去年因网络诈骗损失近180亿美元，华盛顿做得够多吗？
enrich.summary_zh: 这篇《时代》周刊美国栏目的报道聚焦网络诈骗造成的巨额损失：去年美国人被骗走近180亿美元。国会的一项调查指出，联邦政府在帮助受害者追回损失方面存在明显缺口，文章据此追问华盛顿的应对是否足够。

paragraphs.en: A Congressional investigation identifies gaps in federal efforts to help Americans recover billions of dollars lost to scammers online.
paragraphs.zh: 一项国会调查指出，联邦政府在帮助美国人追回被网络诈骗分子骗走的数十亿美元方面存在不足。

vocab.meaning_zh: 国会的；美国国会（Congress）的，注意首字母大写时特指美国国会
vocab.example_en: The congressional hearing drew sharp partisan lines.
vocab.example_zh: 这场国会听证会呈现出鲜明的党派对立。

vocab.meaning_zh: 调查，此处指官方性质的正式调查（如国会委员会调查）
vocab.example_en: The committee launched an investigation into the data breach.
vocab.example_zh: 该委员会对这起数据泄露事件启动了调查。

vocab.meaning_zh: 指出、确认（问题所在）；外刊中常与 gaps、problems、issues 搭配
vocab.example_en: Auditors identified serious weaknesses in the system.
vocab.example_zh: 审计人员指出了该系统中存在的严重缺陷。

vocab.meaning_zh: （能力、制度、覆盖上的）空白、缺口、不足
vocab.example_en: There is a widening gap between policy and practice.
vocab.example_zh: 政策与实践之间的差距正在扩大。

vocab.meaning_zh: 联邦（政府）的；美国语境下指华盛顿的中央政府，与州、地方层面相对
vocab.example_en: Federal agencies were slow to respond to the crisis.
vocab.example_zh: 联邦机构对这场危机反应迟缓。

vocab.meaning_zh: 诈骗者，行骗的人；动词 scam 指诈骗，名词 scam 指骗局
vocab.example_en: Scammers often pose as bank employees.
vocab.example_zh: 诈骗者常常冒充银行工作人员。

sentences.en: A Congressional investigation identifies gaps in federal efforts to help Americans recover billions of dollars lost to scammers online.
sentences.structure: 主干：A Congressional investigation（主语）identifies（谓语）gaps（宾语）。修饰：in federal efforts 作 gaps 的后置定语，说明是“哪方面的缺口”；to help Americans recover... 是修饰 efforts 的不定式定语；lost to scammers online 是过去分词短语作后置定语，修饰 billions of dollars。
sentences.analysis_zh: 这是一个信息密度很高的单句，主干只有三个词，其余全靠后置定语层层“挂”在主谓宾之后，这是英文新闻导语最典型的写法：先把核心判断（调查指出缺口）抛出，再用介词短语和分词短语补充细节。翻译时中文习惯把修饰成分前置或拆成短句，所以处理成“在帮助……方面存在不足”。注意 lost to 是被动含义“被……弄丢的”，scammers online 即“网络上的诈骗者”，介词 to 在此表示损失的对象或原因。

background.title: 美国国会调查权
background.text_zh: 美国国会两院各委员会有权就特定议题展开调查，方式包括发传票调取文件、传唤证人作证、发布调查报告。这类调查本身没有执法效力，但常成为推动立法的前奏，也是媒体获取官方数据的重要来源。文中“国会调查”很可能指某个委员会（如参议院常设调查小组委员会或众议院相关委员会）发布的报告。

background.title: 美国的诈骗损失追回机制
background.text_zh: 在美国，网络诈骗受害者的钱一旦转出，追回主要依赖银行、支付平台（如电汇、礼品卡、加密货币渠道）以及联邦机构（如联邦贸易委员会 FTC、联邦调查局 IC3 报案系统、消费者金融保护局）。这些机构分工不同、报案门槛各异，长期以来被批评为“报案渠道分散、跨境资金难追、受害者获赔率极低”，这正是摘要中“联邦努力存在缺口”的现实语境。

title_en: Why You Shouldn't Toss Your Old Halloween Pumpkins In The Trash
excerpt_en: Millions of pumpkins need to be disposed of after Halloween.

enrich.title_zh: 为什么你不该把万圣节用过的南瓜扔进垃圾桶
enrich.summary_zh: 万圣节一过，数以百万计的雕刻南瓜就成了待处理的垃圾。时代周刊气候栏目以这个标题提出主张：不要把它们直接丢进垃圾桶，而应另寻更环保的去处。编辑部配发的提要只点明问题规模——需要处理的南瓜以百万计——至于具体的环境代价与替代方案，仅凭这条提要大可不必臆测。

paragraphs.en: Millions of pumpkins need to be disposed of after Halloween.
paragraphs.zh: 万圣节过后，数以百万计的南瓜需要处理掉。

vocab.meaning_zh: 随手扔、随手丢（比 throw 更口语，含“漫不经心”的意味）
vocab.example_en: Many people simply toss their pumpkins into the nearest dumpster the morning after Halloween.
vocab.example_zh: 万圣节第二天早上，很多人干脆把南瓜随手丢进最近的垃圾箱。

vocab.meaning_zh: 处理掉、清除掉（垃圾、废弃物等）；介词 of 不可省
vocab.example_en: Cities are looking for ways to dispose of food waste without sending it to landfills.
vocab.example_zh: 各城市正在寻找不把厨余垃圾送进填埋场的处理办法。

vocab.meaning_zh: 数以百万计的、大量的（新闻标题与提要中常用来强调问题规模）
vocab.example_en: Millions of tonnes of food are wasted every year.
vocab.example_zh: 每年有数百万吨食物被浪费掉。

vocab.meaning_zh: （美式）垃圾、废弃物；in the trash 即“扔进垃圾桶、当垃圾丢掉”
vocab.example_en: Half the food we buy ends up in the trash.
vocab.example_zh: 我们买回来的食物有一半最后进了垃圾桶。

sentences.en: Millions of pumpkins need to be disposed of after Halloween.
sentences.structure: 主干：Millions of pumpkins（主语）+ need to be disposed of（谓语，被动不定式）／修饰：after Halloween 为时间状语，置于句末补充时间信息
sentences.analysis_zh: 全句只有一套主谓结构，意思是“数以百万计的南瓜需要被处理掉”。谓语用 need to be done 而非主动形式，是因为主语 pumpkins 是“被处理”的对象；这一结构也可换成 need disposing of（need + 动名词，主动形式表被动），但 need to be done 更常见、更清楚。要特别注意 dispose of 的介词 of 不能丢：dispose 单独用意为“布置、使倾向于”，与“丢弃”无关，这是中国学生的高频错误。时间状语 after Halloween 放在句末而不是句首，是因为句子的信息重心在“需要处理”这一判断上，时间只作补充说明。

background.title: 南瓜灯、万圣节与“节日后的垃圾”
background.text_zh: 南瓜灯（jack-o'-lantern）源自爱尔兰传说中的人物“吝啬鬼杰克”，爱尔兰移民到北美后改用当地更易雕刻的南瓜，此后南瓜逐渐成为万圣节的视觉符号。在英美国家，万圣节用的南瓜绝大多数是专门种植的雕刻品种，个头大、肉质粗、味道淡，并不适合食用，所以节日一过就大批被丢弃。若这些南瓜进入填埋场，会在缺氧环境下缓慢分解并释放甲烷这类温室气体；因此近年不少地方推行把南瓜送去堆肥、捐赠给动物园喂动物或集中回收的做法。这也正是气候类报道在每年十一月都会重提“别把南瓜扔进垃圾桶”的现实背景。

title_en: Why We Like to Be Scared
excerpt_en: The world has always been full of things that frighten us. One way we work through these fears is by watching horror, writes Coltan Scrivner.

enrich.title_zh: 我们为什么喜欢被吓到
enrich.summary_zh: 世界从来不缺让人害怕的东西。作者科尔坦·斯克里夫纳在本文中提出，我们消化、应对这些恐惧的方式之一，就是去看恐怖片。也就是说，人之所以愿意主动体验恐惧，是因为恐怖这类虚构的惊吓能帮我们处理现实中的不安。

paragraphs.en: The world has always been full of things that frighten us. One way we work through these fears is by watching horror, writes Coltan Scrivner.
paragraphs.zh: 这个世界从来都不缺少令我们恐惧的事物。科尔坦·斯克里夫纳写道，我们化解这些恐惧的方式之一，就是去看恐怖片。

vocab.meaning_zh: 使害怕、使惊恐；此处用主动形式 things that frighten us，强调外物给人的心理冲击
vocab.example_en: The sudden noise frightened the children.
vocab.example_zh: 突如其来的响声吓到了孩子们。

vocab.meaning_zh: 充满、到处都是；配合 always 使用，强调这是一种长期、普遍的状态
vocab.example_en: Her letters are full of small, telling details.
vocab.example_zh: 她的信里满是不起眼却很说明问题的细节。

vocab.meaning_zh: （逐步）处理、化解（情绪、问题等）；不是“穿过”，而是把某种难受的感受慢慢消化掉，是外刊谈心理时的常用表达
vocab.example_en: He is still working through his grief.
vocab.example_zh: 他仍在慢慢消化自己的悲伤。

vocab.meaning_zh: 恐惧、害怕；these fears 回指上一句所说的那些令人害怕的事物带来的具体恐惧
vocab.example_en: She has a deep fear of being alone.
vocab.example_zh: 她非常害怕独处。

vocab.meaning_zh: 此处指“恐怖题材作品”，即恐怖片、恐怖小说这一类型（不可数用法），而非“恐怖”这种情绪本身
vocab.example_en: He has been a fan of horror since he was a teenager.
vocab.example_zh: 他从十几岁起就是恐怖片的爱好者。

vocab.meaning_zh: 害怕的、受惊吓的（标题 be scared 指“被吓到”这种体验），与 frightening（令人害怕的）形成“感受者—施动者”的对照
vocab.example_en: I was scared stiff during the whole film.
vocab.example_zh: 整部电影我都吓得僵住了。

sentences.en: The world has always been full of things that frighten us.
sentences.structure: 主干：The world has been full of things（主—系—表）/ 修饰：that frighten us 是定语从句，修饰 things，that 在从句中作主语
sentences.analysis_zh: 句子本身很简单，但两个细节值得注意。一是时态：has always been 用现在完成时加 always，把“充满可怕之物”说成从过去延续到现在的常态，而不是某一时的判断，为下文“所以人类一直在找办法应对”铺路。二是定语从句用 that 而非 which，且不省略，因为 that 在从句里作主语；things that frighten us 这种“名词＋定语从句”的结构让抽象判断落在具体事物上，比说 The world is frightening 更有画面感。全句作为开篇，先把“恐惧”设定为人类处境的常量，第二句才好提出“看恐怖片是一种应对方式”。

sentences.en: One way we work through these fears is by watching horror, writes Coltan Scrivner.
sentences.structure: 主干：One way is by watching horror（主—系—表）/ 修饰：we work through these fears 是省略了 that 或 in which 的定语从句，修饰 One way；by watching horror 是介词短语作表语，说明“方式”；writes Coltan Scrivner 是引述插入语，置于句末并倒装
sentences.analysis_zh: 这句话的信息重心在表语 by watching horror 上：英语常用“One way … is by doing …”来给某现象归类，by 加动名词把抽象的“方式”具体化为一个动作。定语从句 One way we work through these fears 省略了关系词，这是先行词为 way 时的固定用法，读的时候要意识到 we 前面藏着一个 that。句末的 writes Coltan Scrivner 是新闻英语典型的引述方式：动词加主语倒装，不占句首位置，既交代观点归属，又不打断主句的陈述节奏。整句把“看恐怖片”从娱乐行为重新描述为一种心理应对机制，这正是标题“为什么我们喜欢被吓到”的答案雏形。

background.title: TIME 的 Ideas 栏目
background.text_zh: Ideas 是《时代》周刊的评论与观点版块，刊登由学者、作家或评论人署名（byline）的短篇文章，体裁接近报纸的 op-ed：由一个判断或发现切入，用作者自己的研究或观察支撑，而不是新闻报道式的多方引述。因此这类文章里的“writes Coltan Scrivner”意味着：以下观点属于作者本人，不代表杂志编辑部的立场。

background.title: Coltan Scrivner 与“娱乐性恐惧”研究
background.text_zh: 科尔坦·斯克里夫纳是一位行为科学家，长期研究“娱乐性恐惧”（recreational fear）——即人们为什么愿意花钱、花时间去体验害怕。他的研究领域包括恐怖片爱好者、极端 haunt 体验（鬼屋）参与者的心理特征，并曾提出这类人可能在压力情境下具有更强的心理韧性。了解这一背景，就能明白本文标题中的“喜欢被吓到”并非修辞上的矛盾，而是一个有实证研究支撑的心理学问题：恐惧在安全前提下可以被当作“练习”。（以上为文章之外的背景信息，摘要本身并未展开。）

title_en: Protests under way in Germany and France as minister warns against use of Halloween masks – Europe live
excerpt_en: France’s interior minister, Laurent Nuñez, has warned protesters that covering their faces with Halloween costumes could result in fines
body_en: 320,000 attend protests in France, according to government Turnout at the protests in France against the cost of living stood at 320,000 nationwide, the interior ministry said, lower than the 410,000 seen the previous Saturday and 550,000 on October 17 when riots erupted across the country.

Demonstrations were largely peaceful through the afternoon, though police fired tear gas in Lyon, France’s third-largest city, and Toulouse in the southwest, while tension also broke out at the end of the march in Marseille, Reuters reported.

Police cancel march in Cologne due to masked protesters Police in the German city of Cologne have called off the march organised by Gen Z regelt due to some protesters wearing masks and throwing smoke bombs.
“The demonstration will continue as a stationary rally,” a police spokesperson told German DPA news agency.
Some images on the newswires of protesters dressed for Halloween:
The demonstrations in France and Germany have so far passed without incident, although not everyone is happy with how it’s going.
“We expected it to be different,” one Berliner dressed in a black ski mask and hoody told Die Welt.

Police officers at Place de la Bastille in Paris, where protest organisers had originally planned to begin the march before authorities banned the route and ordered it to start at Porte de Bagnolet, on the eastern edge of the capital:
AP is reporting from the ground in Paris:
A few Halloween costumes stood out in the crowd, including a zombie Michael Jackson from “Thriller,” a pirate and a Spider-Man. Protesters waited calmly, chanting and singing through megaphones.

Corentin Cabreux, a 21-year-old student, said he lives in a state-run student residence where “there are damp stains all along the bottom of my walls, whole sections peeling off, cockroaches everywhere, rats.”
He said he hoped Saturday’s protest would be festive in honor of Halloween, to counter the image of violence that has attached itself to France’s protests.

France interior ministry says 15,000 people taking part in protests The French interior ministry said about 15,000 people were taking part in demonstrations across the country , adding that the situation remained “generally calm”.
The protests were unfolding “without any notable incidents”, the ministry added.
Police had made 27 arrests by 2pm local time, AFP reported.

So far, police in Germany have reported 2,700 protesters in Berlin , with 1,800 people participating in Munich , and about 1,000 in Frankfurt. Police in Cologne have not provided figures but said it was “significantly” lower than the 15,000 registered by organisers, according to the German newspaper Die Welt.
Marches under way in Germany Demonstrations have also begun across Germany, with marches taking place in Berlin, Hamburg, Frankfurt and Dresden , among other cities:
Protesters begin marching in French cities Protesters in Paris have begun marching from Porte de Bagnolet, with demonstrations also taking place in Lille and Lyon .

French student unions call for school and university blockade Crowds of people have gathered in Paris for the protests, where two French student unions have called for a blockade of schools and universities on Tuesday and Thursday.

“We will block access… and then take part in the demonstration this 5 November, in response to the call from workers who are calling for a strike,” Sabrine Kharbach, the spokesperson for the Union Etudiante ( Student Union), told protesters, according to Le Monde.
“If they want to ban demonstrations every week, if they want to ban the marches that have always taken place peacefully, we will show them that they are wrong.”
Manon Moret, general secretary of the National Union of Students of France (UNEF), added: “ So far, the government has still not provided a concrete response to the demands of young people.”

enrich.title_zh: 德法抗议持续进行，部长警告勿用万圣节面具
enrich.summary_zh: 德法两国爆发反对生活成本上涨的大规模抗议。法国内政部称全法32万人上街，人数较前两周下降；里昂、图卢兹警方发射催泪瓦斯，巴黎游行路线被当局更改。德国柏林、慕尼黑等城市亦有游行，科隆因有人戴面具、投掷烟雾弹而取消游行。法国学生工会号召封锁学校，批评政府未回应青年诉求。

paragraphs.en: 320,000 attend protests in France, according to government Turnout at the protests in France against the cost of living stood at 320,000 nationwide, the interior ministry said, lower than the 410,000 seen the previous Saturday and 550,000 on October 17 when riots erupted across the country.
paragraphs.zh: 据政府统计，法国有32万人参加抗议。法国内政部表示，全法反对生活成本上涨的抗议活动参与人数为32万人，低于上周六的41万人，也低于10月17日全国多地爆发骚乱时的55万人。

paragraphs.en: Demonstrations were largely peaceful through the afternoon, though police fired tear gas in Lyon, France’s third-largest city, and Toulouse in the southwest, while tension also broke out at the end of the march in Marseille, Reuters reported.
paragraphs.zh: 整个下午示威基本和平进行，但警方在法国第三大城市里昂和西南部的图卢兹发射了催泪瓦斯；据路透社报道，马赛的游行在结束时也出现了紧张局面。

paragraphs.en: Police cancel march in Cologne due to masked protesters Police in the German city of Cologne have called off the march organised by Gen Z regelt due to some protesters wearing masks and throwing smoke bombs.
paragraphs.zh: 科隆警方因抗议者戴面具而取消游行。德国科隆警方取消了由“Gen Z regelt”组织的游行，原因是部分抗议者戴面具并投掷烟雾弹。

paragraphs.en: “The demonstration will continue as a stationary rally,” a police spokesperson told German DPA news agency.
paragraphs.zh: “示威将以定点集会的形式继续举行，”一名警方发言人对德国DPA通讯社说。

paragraphs.en: Some images on the newswires of protesters dressed for Halloween:
paragraphs.zh: 新闻通讯社图片中一些为万圣节做了装扮的抗议者：

paragraphs.zh: 法国和德国的示威迄今未发生冲突事件，不过并非所有人都对事态的发展感到满意。

paragraphs.en: “We expected it to be different,” one Berliner dressed in a black ski mask and hoody told Die Welt.

paragraphs.zh: 人群中有几身万圣节装扮格外显眼，包括《颤栗》MV里的僵尸版迈克尔·杰克逊、一个海盗和一个蜘蛛侠。抗议者平静地等待，用扩音器喊口号、唱歌。

paragraphs.en: Corentin Cabreux, a 21-year-old student, said he lives in a state-run student residence where “there are damp stains all along the bottom of my walls, whole sections peeling off, cockroaches everywhere, rats.”
paragraphs.zh: 21岁的学生科朗坦·卡布勒（Corentin Cabreux）说，他住在公立学生宿舍，“我墙根全是水渍，整块墙皮往下掉，到处是蟑螂，还有老鼠。”

paragraphs.en: He said he hoped Saturday’s protest would be festive in honor of Halloween, to counter the image of violence that has attached itself to France’s protests.
paragraphs.zh: 他说，他希望周六的抗议能借万圣节之名办出节日气氛，以扭转法国抗议活动被贴上的暴力形象。

paragraphs.en: France interior ministry says 15,000 people taking part in protests The French interior ministry said about 15,000 people were taking part in demonstrations across the country , adding that the situation remained “generally calm”.
paragraphs.zh: 法国内政部称约1.5万人参加抗议。法国内政部表示，全国约有1.5万人正在参加示威，并称局势仍“总体平静”。

paragraphs.en: The protests were unfolding “without any notable incidents”, the ministry added.
paragraphs.zh: 该部补充说，抗议活动“未发生任何值得注意的事件”。

paragraphs.en: Police had made 27 arrests by 2pm local time, AFP reported.
paragraphs.zh: 据法新社报道，截至当地时间下午2点，警方已逮捕27人。

paragraphs.en: So far, police in Germany have reported 2,700 protesters in Berlin , with 1,800 people participating in Munich , and about 1,000 in Frankfurt. Police in Cologne have not provided figures but said it was “significantly” lower than the 15,000 registered by organisers, according to the German newspaper Die Welt.
paragraphs.zh: 德国警方目前报告称，柏林有2700名抗议者，慕尼黑有1800人参加，法兰克福约1000人。据德国《世界报》报道，科隆警方未提供数字，但表示人数“明显”低于组织方登记的1.5万人。

paragraphs.en: Marches under way in Germany Demonstrations have also begun across Germany, with marches taking place in Berlin, Hamburg, Frankfurt and Dresden , among other cities:
paragraphs.zh: 德国的游行正在进行。德国各地也开始示威，柏林、汉堡、法兰克福和德累斯顿等城市都有游行：

paragraphs.en: Protesters begin marching in French cities Protesters in Paris have begun marching from Porte de Bagnolet, with demonstrations also taking place in Lille and Lyon .
paragraphs.zh: 抗议者在法国多座城市开始游行。巴黎的抗议者已从巴尼奥莱门开始游行，里尔和里昂也在举行示威。

paragraphs.en: French student unions call for school and university blockade Crowds of people have gathered in Paris for the protests, where two French student unions have called for a blockade of schools and universities on Tuesday and Thursday.
paragraphs.zh: 法国学生工会呼吁封锁学校。大批民众聚集巴黎参加抗议，两个法国学生工会呼吁在周二和周四封锁中学和大学。

paragraphs.en: “We will block access… and then take part in the demonstration this 5 November, in response to the call from workers who are calling for a strike,” Sabrine Kharbach, the spokesperson for the Union Etudiante ( Student Union), told protesters, according to Le Monde.
paragraphs.zh: 据《世界报》报道，学生工会（Union Etudiante）发言人萨布琳·哈尔巴什（Sabrine Kharbach）对抗议者说：“我们将封锁入口……然后参加11月5日的示威，响应呼吁罢工的工人们的号召。”

paragraphs.en: “If they want to ban demonstrations every week, if they want to ban the marches that have always taken place peacefully, we will show them that they are wrong.”
paragraphs.zh: “如果他们想每周都禁止示威，如果他们想禁止那些一向和平进行的游行，我们就让他们看看他们错了。”

paragraphs.en: Manon Moret, general secretary of the National Union of Students of France (UNEF), added: “ So far, the government has still not provided a concrete response to the demands of young people.”
paragraphs.zh: 法国全国学生联合会（UNEF）总书记玛侬·莫雷（Manon Moret）补充说：“到目前为止，政府仍未对年轻人的诉求给出具体回应。”

vocab.meaning_zh: （数量、水平）达到、为……（用于统计数据）
vocab.example_en: Unemployment stood at 7.2% last month.
vocab.example_zh: 上个月失业率为7.2%。

vocab.meaning_zh: （骚乱、暴力）突然爆发；（火山）喷发
vocab.example_en: Riots erupted in several cities after the announcement.
vocab.example_zh: 消息公布后，多座城市爆发骚乱。

vocab.meaning_zh: 取消（已安排的活动）
vocab.example_en: The march was called off at the last minute for safety reasons.
vocab.example_zh: 出于安全考虑，游行在最后一刻被取消。

vocab.meaning_zh: 不动的、固定的；stationary rally 指原地不动的“定点集会”
vocab.example_en: Police allowed a stationary rally but banned the march.
vocab.example_zh: 警方允许举行定点集会，但禁止游行。

vocab.meaning_zh: 新闻通讯社供稿线路（如路透、美联的社会供稿），也指通讯社
vocab.example_en: Pictures of the scene moved on the newswires within minutes.
vocab.example_zh: 现场照片几分钟内就通过通讯社发出。

vocab.meaning_zh: 平安无事地过去、未发生冲突（新闻报道固定说法）
vocab.example_en: The demonstration passed without incident.
vocab.example_zh: 这次示威平安结束，未发生冲突。

vocab.meaning_zh: 显眼、突出，在人群中引人注目
vocab.example_en: A few colourful costumes stood out in the grey crowd.
vocab.example_zh: 一片灰暗的人群中，几身鲜艳的装扮格外显眼。

vocab.meaning_zh: （墙皮、漆面等）剥落、脱落
vocab.example_en: The paint is peeling off the ceiling.
vocab.example_zh: 天花板上的漆正在剥落。

vocab.meaning_zh: 封锁（此处指学生工会封锁校门、阻止师生进出）
vocab.example_en: Students announced a blockade of the university on Tuesday.
vocab.example_zh: 学生们宣布周二封锁这所大学。

vocab.meaning_zh: 对抗、抵消、反击（某种印象或说法）
vocab.example_en: The organisers tried to counter the image of violence.
vocab.example_zh: 组织者试图扭转暴力形象。

sentences.en: Turnout at the protests in France against the cost of living stood at 320,000 nationwide, the interior ministry said, lower than the 410,000 seen the previous Saturday and 550,000 on October 17 when riots erupted across the country.
sentences.structure: 主干：Turnout … stood at 320,000 nationwide。修饰：at the protests in France against the cost of living 为介词短语后置修饰 turnout；the interior ministry said 是插入式来源说明；lower than … 是形容词短语作补充说明（比较状语性），其中 seen the previous Saturday 是过去分词短语后置修饰 410,000；when riots erupted across the country 是定语从句修饰 October 17。
sentences.analysis_zh: 新闻体惯用的“数据句”：先给出核心数字，再用比较结构把当天的规模放进时间轴上比较，暗示“人数在下降”。比较结构里省略了重复名词（410,000 [people] seen…），seen 用过去分词是“被统计到的”意思，避免重复谓语。翻译时可把 lower than 单独拆成一小句，中文更顺。

sentences.en: Police officers at Place de la Bastille in Paris, where protest organisers had originally planned to begin the march before authorities banned the route and ordered it to start at Porte de Bagnolet, on the eastern edge of the capital:
sentences.structure: 这不是完整句，而是图片说明式的名词短语：中心词 Police officers，后接 at Place de la Bastille in Paris 定位；where 引导定语从句修饰地点，从句内部又嵌一个 before 引导的时间状语从句（authorities banned … and ordered …）；on the eastern edge of the capital 是同位语，补充说明 Porte de Bagnolet 的位置。
sentences.analysis_zh: 直播博客的图片说明常用“名词短语＋冒号”结构，省略主谓，信息密度极高。理解关键是拆层：主句只是“巴士底广场的警察”，后面 where 从句才是新闻点——路线被当局禁止、被迫改到城东的巴尼奥莱门。had originally planned 用过去完成时，表示“原计划”先于“被禁”发生；ordered it to start 中 it 指 the march。

sentences.en: “We will block access… and then take part in the demonstration this 5 November, in response to the call from workers who are calling for a strike,” Sabrine Kharbach, the spokesperson for the Union Etudiante (Student Union), told protesters, according to Le Monde.
sentences.structure: 直接引语（宾语）前置，主句为 Sabrine Kharbach … told protesters，同位语 the spokesperson for the Union Etudiante 说明身份，according to Le Monde 交代消息来源。引语内部主干：We will block access and then take part in the demonstration；in response to the call from workers 是原因状语；who are calling for a strike 是定语从句修饰 workers。
sentences.analysis_zh: 这是典型的“引语＋说话人＋出处”倒装式新闻引述：英语新闻常把长引语放最前，读者读到句子后半才知道谁说的。省略号“…”表示录音或原文有删节。翻译时中文习惯先把说话人提到前面。in response to 是外刊高频的“响应、应……之号召”，比 answer 更书面。

background.title: 法国的“示威文化”与两套人数统计
background.text_zh: 在法国，街头游行（manifestation）是工会和学生组织常用的常规施压手段，需事先向省政府（préfecture）申报；省政府有权以“妨碍公共秩序”为由禁止游行或更改路线——文中的巴士底广场改道巴尼奥莱门就是这种行政处置。内政部与工会各报一套数字是法国抗议报道的固定戏码：内政部统计通常明显偏低，主办方数字往往高出一倍以上，因此读这类新闻时要注意“according to”后面是谁在报数。

background.title: 德国为何对“蒙面”如此敏感
background.text_zh: 德国法律中有所谓“蒙面禁令”（Vermummungsverbot）：在公共集会中故意遮住面部、使人无法辨认身份，本身即属违法行为，警方可据此要求个人摘下面具、驱散人群甚至取消整场活动。所以在万圣节前后戴口罩、滑雪面罩参加游行，在德国会被视为具有对抗意味。这也是科隆警方取消游行的法律依据，以及报道标题中部长“警告不要使用万圣节面具”的现实背景——节日装扮与示威中的蒙面在法律上会撞车。

title_en: Britain’s housing crisis won’t be fixed without a new tax landscape
excerpt_en: We need policies that stop treating property as a store of wealth and that allow people to move home cheaply
body_en: John Healey’s critics on the right and left accused him of dodging the big questions in his first budget . The chancellor failed to announce reforms that might tackle some of Britain’s chronic problems, they say.
Healey’s scatter-gun budget, as the Resolution Foundation called it, was more about politics than economics, and unapologetically so.

Housing was one area of policy that took up a considerable chunk of his speech. And yet the measures amounted to very little, if a test of his policy changes was to ask how different will the UK be at the next election. Or, as that date is only two and a half years away, 10 years from now.
Housing is more than a single element of a complex economy. It is both its driving force and a disease eating its way through the body, from the inside out.

More than 80% of global investment is in property and the vast majority of that is in residential. Countries that once had a more communitarian approach, such as France and Germany, with a highly regulated mix of social, private rented and home ownership, have succumbed to building wealth through property.

It doesn’t seem to matter that Japan was ruined in the 1990s by a vicious property price crash. And China is still suffering domestically after Beijing allowed a property Ponzi scheme to develop that enriched the already super-wealthy and left tens of millions of middle-income earners in negative equity.

Nowhere is the situation worse than in the UK, where property prices have cooled somewhat, but remain at levels that deny younger generations the chance to find a home at a reasonable price and some financial security.

UK property has also become the method by which Gen Xers pay for social care for their parents and release housing deposits for their offspring. Then there is the debilitating leasehold /freehold split that is both a source of angry disputes and stymies investment in solar panels and insulation (who should pay?).

The lack of regulation and ill-thought-out subsidies affecting new private housing means developers are incentivised to enter an arm-twisting contest with local authorities. Without robust planning guidelines, developers champion building on flood plains or erecting tower blocks that are later dubbed ovens for their lack of ventilation in hot summers.
And all the while the tax system is working to make the situation worse.
The Oxford academic John Muellbauer has spent almost 40 years researching the UK’s housing system. He calls it “one of the most dysfunctional in the world”.

In an academic article published in September by the British Academy, he says: “Many of the UK’s current economic and social problems, including its housing affordability crisis, can be traced to decades of land and housing policy failures. The role of land markets is strongly dependent on institutions, including land use regulation, financial regulation and property taxation.”

The Treasury and Angela Rayner’s Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government have considered proposals from Muellbauer and others that remodel council tax, turning it into a fairer annual levy on households and using the reform to abolish stamp duty on transactions, which has calcified the housing market.

Rachel Reeves’s mansion tax is a good start . It is only a start though, because the former chancellor was persuaded to keep the council tax banding system when she should have applied a percentage to the 150,000-odd homes valued above £2m that will be captured by the new policy.

There was the potential for a database of homes valued above £2m to be the beginning of a revaluation process, carrying on until all homes were logged. With a percentage tax of, say, 0.5%, applied to all homes, a £150,000 property would pay an annual tax rate of £750 while a £3m home would pay £15,000.

Of course, the real problem is not the £3m homeowner for whom policymakers will have little sympathy – it’s the professionals occupying £1.5m homes in London, the south-east and affluent suburbs around other big cities, who will see council tax rates more than double to £7,500.

The professional classes will be the worst affected in the short term. Yet there will only be progress when this powerful lobby group of owner-occupiers – working and retired – are prepared to accept the trade-off with stamp duty, which would disappear for those who sell.

There are plenty of people in government who understand the need to resolve housing market issues in a more fundamental fashion. The Treasury minister Torsten Bell is one. His book, Great Britain?: How We Get Our Future Back, talks about “our housing omnishambles”.

However, they have had little influence on policy in this area so far. In his first budget Healey revamped a much-discredited help-to-buy scheme for new-build homes, which will only boost prices and line the pockets of developers. He also gave some more money towards council housebuilding, slapped an extra tax on landlords (that will probably push up rents) and promised to tackle homelessness.
Healey and Andy Burnham put all their revolutionary zeal into a long, and possibly tortuous, process of devolution from London to the regions to kickstart growth.

However, it is tax incentives that are causing the problems, not whether policy decisions are made locally or centrally. Bad policy decisions can be made locally just as much as centrally. What makes the difference is a permanently reformed tax landscape that discourages treating housing as a store of wealth, allows people to move home cheaply – especially older homeowners who want to downsize – and supports the building of more truly affordable homes to buy and rent.

enrich.title_zh: 没有新的税收格局，英国的住房危机无从解决
enrich.summary_zh: 文章批评英国首份预算案在住房问题上雷声大雨点小：购房援助、对房东加税等举措只是微调，反而可能推高房价与租金。作者援引牛津学者米尔鲍尔的观点，认为危机根源在土地与住房政策的长期失误，尤其是市政税档次僵化与交易印花税；主张对全部房产按比例征收年度房产税并废除印花税，才可能让年轻一代买得起房、让人们愿意搬迁。

paragraphs.en: John Healey’s critics on the right and left accused him of dodging the big questions in his first budget . The chancellor failed to announce reforms that might tackle some of Britain’s chronic problems, they say.
paragraphs.zh: 右翼和左翼的批评者都指责约翰·希利（John Healey）在其首份预算案中回避了重大问题。他们说，这位财政大臣没有宣布任何可能解决英国部分长期痼疾的改革。

paragraphs.en: Healey’s scatter-gun budget, as the Resolution Foundation called it, was more about politics than economics, and unapologetically so.
paragraphs.zh: 正如决议基金会（Resolution Foundation）所称，希利这份“散弹枪式”预算案（广撒网却缺乏重点）更多关乎政治而非经济，而且对此毫不掩饰。

paragraphs.en: Housing was one area of policy that took up a considerable chunk of his speech. And yet the measures amounted to very little, if a test of his policy changes was to ask how different will the UK be at the next election. Or, as that date is only two and a half years away, 10 years from now.
paragraphs.zh: 住房是他演讲中占据相当大篇幅的政策领域之一。然而，如果检验其政策变化的标准是问“到下届大选时英国会有多大不同”，那么这些措施可谓微不足道。或者换个说法：既然下届大选只剩两年半，那就问十年之后会怎样。

paragraphs.en: Housing is more than a single element of a complex economy. It is both its driving force and a disease eating its way through the body, from the inside out.
paragraphs.zh: 住房不只是一个复杂经济体中的单一要素。它既是经济的驱动力，又是一种从内部向外啃噬整个机体的病症。

paragraphs.en: More than 80% of global investment is in property and the vast majority of that is in residential. Countries that once had a more communitarian approach, such as France and Germany, with a highly regulated mix of social, private rented and home ownership, have succumbed to building wealth through property.
paragraphs.zh: 全球超过80%的投资落在房地产上，其中绝大多数是住宅地产。一些国家曾经更偏向社群主义路径，例如法国和德国，其社会住房、私人租赁住房与自有住房的混合体系受到高度监管，如今也都屈服于“靠房产积累财富”的模式。

paragraphs.en: It doesn’t seem to matter that Japan was ruined in the 1990s by a vicious property price crash. And China is still suffering domestically after Beijing allowed a property Ponzi scheme to develop that enriched the already super-wealthy and left tens of millions of middle-income earners in negative equity.
paragraphs.zh: 日本在1990年代因房价恶性崩盘而遭受重创，这似乎无关紧要。中国在允许一种房地产“庞氏骗局”发展起来之后，国内至今仍在承受后果——它让本已超级富有的人更加富有，却让数千万中等收入者陷入负资产。

paragraphs.en: Nowhere is the situation worse than in the UK, where property prices have cooled somewhat, but remain at levels that deny younger generations the chance to find a home at a reasonable price and some financial security.
paragraphs.zh: 没有哪里比英国的情况更糟：当地房价虽有所降温，但仍停留在这样一个水平——让年轻一代既无缘以合理价格置业，也无缘获得一定的财务保障。

paragraphs.en: UK property has also become the method by which Gen Xers pay for social care for their parents and release housing deposits for their offspring. Then there is the debilitating leasehold /freehold split that is both a source of angry disputes and stymies investment in solar panels and insulation (who should pay?).
paragraphs.zh: 英国房产还成了X世代为父母支付社会照护费用、为子女凑出购房首付的手段。此外还有令人身心俱疲的租赁产权／永久产权分割问题，它既是激烈纠纷的源头，也阻碍了对太阳能板和保温层的投资（该由谁来付钱？）。

paragraphs.en: The lack of regulation and ill-thought-out subsidies affecting new private housing means developers are incentivised to enter an arm-twisting contest with local authorities. Without robust planning guidelines, developers champion building on flood plains or erecting tower blocks that are later dubbed ovens for their lack of ventilation in hot summers.
paragraphs.zh: 针对新建私人住房的监管缺位与考虑不周的补贴，意味着开发商有动力与地方政府展开一场“掰手腕”式的较量。没有强有力的规划指引，开发商就热衷于在洪泛区盖房，或者竖起一栋栋高层住宅——它们后来因夏季通风不良而被讥为“烤箱”。

paragraphs.en: And all the while the tax system is working to make the situation worse.
paragraphs.zh: 而与此同时，税收体系还在不断把局面弄得更糟。

paragraphs.en: The Oxford academic John Muellbauer has spent almost 40 years researching the UK’s housing system. He calls it “one of the most dysfunctional in the world”.
paragraphs.zh: 牛津学者约翰·米尔鲍尔（John Muellbauer）研究英国住房体系近40年。他称之为“世界上最失灵的体系之一”。

paragraphs.en: In an academic article published in September by the British Academy, he says: “Many of the UK’s current economic and social problems, including its housing affordability crisis, can be traced to decades of land and housing policy failures. The role of land markets is strongly dependent on institutions, including land use regulation, financial regulation and property taxation.”
paragraphs.zh: 在9月由英国科学院（British Academy）发表的一篇学术文章中，他说：“英国当前许多经济和社会问题，包括住房可负担性危机，都可以追溯到数十年来的土地与住房政策失误。土地市场所起的作用高度依赖制度，包括土地使用监管、金融监管和房产税。”

paragraphs.en: The Treasury and Angela Rayner’s Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government have considered proposals from Muellbauer and others that remodel council tax, turning it into a fairer annual levy on households and using the reform to abolish stamp duty on transactions, which has calcified the housing market.
paragraphs.zh: 英国财政部和安吉拉·雷纳（Angela Rayner）领导的住房、社区与地方政府部，已研究过米尔鲍尔等人提出的方案：重塑市政税（council tax），使之成为对家庭征收的更公平的年度税，并借这项改革废除交易环节的印花税——印花税已让住房市场僵化。

paragraphs.en: Rachel Reeves’s mansion tax is a good start . It is only a start though, because the former chancellor was persuaded to keep the council tax banding system when she should have applied a percentage to the 150,000-odd homes valued above £2m that will be captured by the new policy.
paragraphs.zh: 蕾切尔·里夫斯（Rachel Reeves）推出的“豪宅税”是个好的开始。但它仅仅是开始，因为这位前财政大臣被说服保留了市政税的档次体系，而她本应对将被新政策覆盖的约15万套价值超200万英镑的住宅按统一比例税率征税。

paragraphs.en: There was the potential for a database of homes valued above £2m to be the beginning of a revaluation process, carrying on until all homes were logged. With a percentage tax of, say, 0.5%, applied to all homes, a £150,000 property would pay an annual tax rate of £750 while a £3m home would pay £15,000.
paragraphs.zh: 一份记录价值200万英镑以上房产的数据库，本有可能成为重新估值进程的起点，一直推进到所有住房都被登记在册。若对所有住房统一按比例征税，比如0.5%，那么一套15万英镑的房产每年缴税750英镑，而一套300万英镑的房产每年则缴1.5万英镑。

paragraphs.en: Of course, the real problem is not the £3m homeowner for whom policymakers will have little sympathy – it’s the professionals occupying £1.5m homes in London, the south-east and affluent suburbs around other big cities, who will see council tax rates more than double to £7,500.
paragraphs.zh: 当然，真正的问题不是那位300万英镑房产的业主——政策制定者对他不会有几分同情——而是在伦敦、东南部以及其他大城市周边富裕郊区拥有150万英镑房产的专业人士，他们的市政税将翻倍还多，达到7500英镑。

paragraphs.en: The professional classes will be the worst affected in the short term. Yet there will only be progress when this powerful lobby group of owner-occupiers – working and retired – are prepared to accept the trade-off with stamp duty, which would disappear for those who sell.
paragraphs.zh: 短期内受冲击最大的将是专业阶层。然而，只有当这个由自住业主（在职者和已退休者）组成的强大游说群体愿意接受与印花税的交换条件——对卖房者而言印花税将不复存在——才会有真正的进展。

paragraphs.en: There are plenty of people in government who understand the need to resolve housing market issues in a more fundamental fashion. The Treasury minister Torsten Bell is one. His book, Great Britain?: How We Get Our Future Back, talks about “our housing omnishambles”.
paragraphs.zh: 政府中有不少人明白，需要以更根本的方式解决住房市场问题。财政部部长托斯滕·贝尔（Torsten Bell）就是其中之一。他的著作《大不列颠？：如何找回我们的未来》谈到了“我们住房领域的一团乱麻”。

paragraphs.en: However, they have had little influence on policy in this area so far. In his first budget Healey revamped a much-discredited help-to-buy scheme for new-build homes, which will only boost prices and line the pockets of developers. He also gave some more money towards council housebuilding, slapped an extra tax on landlords (that will probably push up rents) and promised to tackle homelessness.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，到目前为止，他们对这一领域的政策影响甚微。在首份预算案中，希利改造了备受诟病的“购房援助”（help-to-buy）新建住房计划，而这只会推高房价、中饱开发商私囊。他还为社会住房建设追加了一些资金，对房东加征了一项额外税（这很可能推高租金），并承诺解决无家可归问题。

paragraphs.en: Healey and Andy Burnham put all their revolutionary zeal into a long, and possibly tortuous, process of devolution from London to the regions to kickstart growth.
paragraphs.zh: 希利和安迪·伯纳姆（Andy Burnham）把他们全部的变革热情，都投入到一个漫长且可能颇为曲折的进程中——把权力从伦敦下放到各地区，以启动经济增长。

paragraphs.en: However, it is tax incentives that are causing the problems, not whether policy decisions are made locally or centrally. Bad policy decisions can be made locally just as much as centrally. What makes the difference is a permanently reformed tax landscape that discourages treating housing as a store of wealth, allows people to move home cheaply – especially older homeowners who want to downsize – and supports the building of more truly affordable homes to buy and rent.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，真正造成问题的是税收激励，而非政策决定究竟由地方还是中央作出。糟糕的政策决定在地方和在中央一样会被作出。真正带来改变的是一个永久性改革的税收格局：它抑制把住房当作财富储存手段的做法，让人们能够低成本搬迁——尤其是想换小房子的年长业主——并支持建造更多真正负担得起的可购可租房。

vocab.meaning_zh: 回避，躲闪（问题、责任）
vocab.example_en: The minister was accused of dodging the tough questions on housing supply.
vocab.example_zh: 这位大臣被指责回避了有关住房供应的尖锐问题。

vocab.meaning_zh: 散弹枪式的；广撒网而缺乏重点的（政策、措施）
vocab.example_en: Critics described the package as a scatter-gun approach that spread money too thinly.
vocab.example_zh: 批评者称这套方案是广撒网式做法，资金摊得太薄。

vocab.meaning_zh: 屈服于，抵挡不住（某种趋势或做法）
vocab.example_en: Even countries with strong social housing traditions have succumbed to property speculation.
vocab.example_zh: 就连社会住房传统深厚的国家也抵挡不住房地产投机的诱惑。

vocab.meaning_zh: 负资产（房产市值低于所欠贷款）
vocab.example_en: Millions of buyers found themselves in negative equity after the crash.
vocab.example_zh: 崩盘之后，数以百万计的购房者发现自己陷入了负资产。

vocab.meaning_zh: 租赁产权／永久产权（英国房产的两种持有形式）
vocab.example_en: The leasehold system leaves flat owners paying ground rent to a freeholder.
vocab.example_zh: 租赁产权制度让公寓业主必须向永久产权人缴纳地租。

vocab.meaning_zh: 阻碍，使无法推进

vocab.example_zh: 模糊的产权规则阻碍了对节能改造的投资。

vocab.meaning_zh: 征收的税款，征费
vocab.example_en: An annual levy on property would replace transaction taxes.
vocab.example_zh: 每年征收的房产税将取代交易环节的税收。

vocab.meaning_zh: （使）僵化，固化成硬块
vocab.example_en: High stamp duty has calcified the housing market, freezing out first-time buyers.
vocab.example_zh: 高额印花税让住房市场僵化，把首次购房者挡在门外。

vocab.meaning_zh: 一团乱麻，全面失控的混乱局面（英式口语/政治用语）
vocab.example_en: His book calls the housing system an omnishambles of conflicting incentives.
vocab.example_zh: 他的书称住房体系是各种激励相互冲突的一团乱麻。

vocab.meaning_zh: （尤指子女离家后）换住更小的房子
vocab.example_en: Many retired owners would downsize if moving were cheaper.
vocab.example_zh: 如果搬家成本更低，许多退休业主会愿意换住小房子。

sentences.en: Countries that once had a more communitarian approach, such as France and Germany, with a highly regulated mix of social, private rented and home ownership, have succumbed to building wealth through property.
sentences.structure: 主干：Countries … have succumbed to building wealth through property（主语＋谓语＋宾语）。修饰：that once had a more communitarian approach 为定语从句修饰 countries；such as France and Germany 为同位举例；with a highly regulated mix of social, private rented and home ownership 为介词短语，补充说明这种“路径”的具体构成。
sentences.analysis_zh: 这句话信息密度很高，靠三层后置成分把“哪类国家、什么模式、结局如何”塞进一句。英语习惯先立主干再挂修饰，因此主语 countries 与谓语 have succumbed 之间隔了三十多个词；翻译时中文宜拆成“一些国家……如今也都屈服于……”的流水句，把修饰成分前置成定语，避免句子失衡。

sentences.en: The Treasury and Angela Rayner’s Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government have considered proposals from Muellbauer and others that remodel council tax, turning it into a fairer annual levy on households and using the reform to abolish stamp duty on transactions, which has calcified the housing market.
sentences.structure: 主干：The Treasury and … Ministry … have considered proposals（主谓宾）。修饰：from Muellbauer and others 为介词短语限定 proposals；that remodel council tax 为定语从句修饰 proposals；turning it into … and using the reform to abolish … 为两个并列的现在分词短语，说明方案的内容与目的；which has calcified the housing market 为非限制性定语从句，回指 stamp duty on transactions。
sentences.analysis_zh: 全句是典型的“名词＋定从＋分词状语＋非限定定从”四连挂。注意 that 从句的先行词是复数的 proposals，所以动词用 remodel 原形；turning 与 using 共享逻辑主语，即这些 proposals，两个动作各有宾语，形成平行节奏，是外刊常见的“先给结论、再用分词列出措施”的写法。

sentences.en: What makes the difference is a permanently reformed tax landscape that discourages treating housing as a store of wealth, allows people to move home cheaply – especially older homeowners who want to downsize – and supports the building of more truly affordable homes to buy and rent.
sentences.structure: 主干：What makes the difference is a permanently reformed tax landscape（主语从句＋系动词＋表语）。修饰：that discourages …, allows …, and supports … 为定语从句修饰 tax landscape，内含三个并列谓语；especially older homeowners who want to downsize 为插入的同位补充；to buy and rent 为不定式修饰 homes。
sentences.analysis_zh: 结尾句用 What 引导的主语从句提出判断，把“真正起作用的因素”前置强调，再用一个带三个并列动词的定语从句逐条落地，形成“总—分”结构。三个动词 discourage／allows／supports 分别为“抑制—允许—支持”，构成完整的政策逻辑链，也是作者全文主张的浓缩，翻译时应保留这种排比力度。

background.title: 市政税与印花税：英国房产税的两块老骨头
background.text_zh: council tax（市政税）是英格兰、苏格兰和威尔士的地方税，按房产价值划分档次（bands）征收。英格兰的档次自1991年（威尔士为2003年）确定估值以来从未全面重估，三十多年间房价剧烈变动，导致税负与真实房价严重脱节：高价房产往往按远低于市价的档次纳税。stamp duty（印花税）则是房产交易环节的一次性税，房价越高税率越高，被批评者认为抬高了搬家成本、抑制了市场流动性、把首次购房者挡在门外。所谓 mansion tax（豪宅税）是英国长期讨论的一个构想，即对高价值房产额外征税；文章提到的新政策把重点放在价值200万英镑以上的住宅上。

background.title: 租赁产权与永久产权之争
background.text_zh: leasehold（租赁产权）与 freehold（永久产权）是英国（尤其英格兰）特有的房产持有形式：独栋住宅多为永久产权，而公寓常以一份长达数十年至999年的租约出售，业主只拥有房屋内部，土地仍归 freeholder（永久产权人）。业主需缴纳地租（ground rent）和服务费，续租、改建、安装太阳能板或保温层都要取得永久产权人同意并可能分摊费用，因此常引发纠纷。近年英国一直在推进租赁产权改革，这也是文中“谁该为节能改造付钱”这一质问的制度背景。

title_en: ‘We freed Patrick Stewart!’ Star Trek’s Marina Sirtis on breaking in her beloved but very serious co-star
excerpt_en: She was scared of him but soon loosened the Shakespearean up – then watched him give Star Trek depth, even insisting scenes be rewritten for her. Captain Picard’s right-hand woman salutes her fabulous friend
body_en: I’d been warned about Patrick by friends who’d worked with him at the Royal Shakespeare Company. They said: “Marina, you can’t be you around Patrick Stewart. He’s all about the work. He takes it very seriously and he won’t abide you mucking about and trying to make people corpse.”

We had been cast together on Star Trek: The Next Generation and, because of what I’d heard, I was a bit scared, a bit intimidated. And let’s be honest – Patrick was very serious about the work. But there was a concerted effort by the rest of us to beat it out of him. We were from a younger generation and we wanted to shake up this Englishman who was so typical of his generation – stiff upper lip and a Yorkshireman to boot. You know, the kind of person who was not exactly renowned for showing their emotions. Early on Patrick told us all that we weren’t there to have fun, and you should have seen the looks he got. I’m a cockney: I’ve got a Spurs tattoo and we all looked at him in the same way I look at an Arsenal fan. But we did loosen him up. And – he’s said this himself – I think we actually freed him. We gave him a freedom that he said he’d never really felt before.
He told the writers he really had to look into my eyes – not Data’s – to reach the emotions he needed

Of course it went both ways. We learned so much from him, how could you not? We learned from his professionalism and his absolutely insane talent. He brought gravitas to the role. Star Trek was a bit of a punchline before Patrick came along – it’s not any more. Patrick gave it depth – here was this consummate Shakespearean actor playing the captain of a starship. It just shifted everything.

He had reservations about taking the role, and his friends – who loved him and were looking out for him – told him not to do it. They thought it would be the end of his career, whereas it was probably the best decision in showbusiness at that time. He handled fame with grace. He didn’t flaunt it. Never got too big for his boots. Early on, a review in a paper described him as an “unknown Shakespearean actor” and we blew it up and stuck it on his trailer door. Someone less self-deprecating might not have liked that but he left it up there for years. He knew it was all good fun.

Before meeting Patrick I was just a jobbing actor who did a bit of telly. I’d grown up dirt poor and had a difficult childhood, so we came from very similar backgrounds. I kept my cockney accent because I wanted people to know where I came from. Patrick was the same – not through his voice, but through his demeanour and actions. He was down to earth, a regular bloke. The fact that he supported Huddersfield Town shows you who he is – he didn’t go for Leeds or one of the glamour clubs.

We’d both experienced childhood trauma and came out with our stories after we had finished working together. We never sat down and went into it all. But when people have gone through something like that, there’s something in their demeanour, something that you can see in them, that you feel in them.

A month before Covid hit, my husband died. I was on my own in my house in Los Angeles for a year with just my dogs for company. Patrick was one of the very few people who invited me over for lunch, socially distanced in his garden. It had occurred to him that I was grieving and on my own – and he did something about that. It’s a mark of who he is.

He was always on my side. In one of the Star Trek movies we did there was a scene written for Picard and Data, where Picard tells the story of how his family were burned in a fire. Patrick went to the writers and producers and asked if they could rewrite the scene to have me be in it instead of Brent Spiner. He said that Brent’s character Data was an android, and that he really needed to look into my eyes in order to reach the emotions he needed. So our relationship on screen was a two-way street, which sounds ridiculous saying that out loud! I don’t know how I’ve got the cheek to say that when I’m talking about Patrick Stewart! But we did help each other.

It’s also because of Patrick that I am now in the annals of my football team. When Tottenham played Huddersfield in 2018, we both did interviews about the game and it was officially named in the match day programme as the Star Trek derby. That’s now a part of Tottenham history and, as anyone who knows me will tell you, that means more to me than winning an acting award!

It was the absolute privilege of my life and my career to work with him. We were very, very close and stayed in touch right to the end, even though it became difficult to speak to him on the phone because of his health. He went quickly in the end and it makes me very sad that I didn’t get a chance to say goodbye. To say: “Thank you Patrick. Thanks for everything, mate.”

I kept my cockney accent because I wanted people to know where I came from. Patrick was the same – not through his voice, but through his demeanour and actions. He was down to earth, a regular bloke. The fact that he supported Huddersfield Town shows you who he is – he didn’t go for Leeds or one of the glamour clubs.
paragraphs.zh: 在遇见帕特里克之前，我只是个接活儿的演员，演过一点电视剧。我在赤贫中长大，童年过得艰难，所以我们出身非常相似。我一直保留着伦敦东区口音，因为我想让人知道我来自哪里。帕特里克也一样——不是靠口音，而是靠他的举止和行事。他脚踏实地，就是个普通人。他支持哈德斯菲尔德镇队这件事就能说明他是怎样的人——他没去攀利兹，也没去攀哪个光鲜的豪门俱乐部。

paragraphs.en: We’d both experienced childhood trauma and came out with our stories after we had finished working together. We never sat down and went into it all. But when people have gone through something like that, there’s something in their demeanour, something that you can see in them, that you feel in them.
paragraphs.zh: 我们都经历过童年创伤，都是在合作结束之后才把各自的故事讲出来。我们从来没有坐下来把这些事细细谈过。但当一个人经历过那样的事情，他的举止里就有某种东西，某种你能在他身上看到、也能在他身上感受到的东西。

paragraphs.en: A month before Covid hit, my husband died. I was on my own in my house in Los Angeles for a year with just my dogs for company. Patrick was one of the very few people who invited me over for lunch, socially distanced in his garden. It had occurred to him that I was grieving and on my own – and he did something about that. It’s a mark of who he is.
paragraphs.zh: 新冠疫情暴发前一个月，我丈夫去世了。我一个人待在洛杉矶的家里，整整一年只有几只狗作伴。帕特里克是极少数邀请我去吃午饭的人之一，在他家花园里，保持着社交距离。他自己想到我正处在悲痛中、孤身一人——并且为此做了点什么。这一点正说明他是个什么样的人。

paragraphs.en: He was always on my side. In one of the Star Trek movies we did there was a scene written for Picard and Data, where Picard tells the story of how his family were burned in a fire. Patrick went to the writers and producers and asked if they could rewrite the scene to have me be in it instead of Brent Spiner. He said that Brent’s character Data was an android, and that he really needed to look into my eyes in order to reach the emotions he needed. So our relationship on screen was a two-way street, which sounds ridiculous saying that out loud! I don’t know how I’ve got the cheek to say that when I’m talking about Patrick Stewart! But we did help each other.
paragraphs.zh: 他总是站在我这边。在我们拍的一部《星际迷航》电影里，有一场戏是写给皮卡德和 Data 的，戏里皮卡德讲述他的家人如何在一场大火中被烧死。帕特里克去找编剧和制片人，问能不能把这场戏改一改，让我来演，而不是布伦特·斯派纳。他说布伦特演的角色 Data 是个机器人，而他真的需要看着我的眼睛，才能达到他需要的那种情绪。所以我们在银幕上的关系是双向的，这话说出口听起来很荒唐！我真不知道自己哪儿来的脸皮这么说，我谈的可是帕特里克·斯图尔特啊！但我们确实互相成就了对方。

paragraphs.en: It’s also because of Patrick that I am now in the annals of my football team. When Tottenham played Huddersfield in 2018, we both did interviews about the game and it was officially named in the match day programme as the Star Trek derby. That’s now a part of Tottenham history and, as anyone who knows me will tell you, that means more to me than winning an acting award!
paragraphs.zh: 也是因为帕特里克，我现在才被写进了我球队的史册。2018 年托特纳姆对哈德斯菲尔德那场，我们俩都就比赛接受了采访，比赛日手册里正式把那场命名为“星际迷航德比”。这如今已经是托特纳姆历史的一部分了，而认识我的人都会告诉你，这对我来说比拿表演奖还重要！

paragraphs.en: It was the absolute privilege of my life and my career to work with him. We were very, very close and stayed in touch right to the end, even though it became difficult to speak to him on the phone because of his health. He went quickly in the end and it makes me very sad that I didn’t get a chance to say goodbye. To say: “Thank you Patrick. Thanks for everything, mate.”
paragraphs.zh: 能和他共事，是我人生和职业生涯中莫大的荣幸。我们非常非常亲近，一直保持联系到最后，尽管因为他的身体状况，后来打电话给他变得越来越困难。他最后走得很匆忙，没能有机会跟他道别，让我非常难过。没能说上一句：“谢谢你，帕特里克。谢谢你的一切，老伙计。”

vocab.meaning_zh: （英式口语）笑场、笑得收不住；使别人笑场（字面义为“尸体”，这里是剧场行话）
vocab.example_en: Half the cast corpsed during the final take.
vocab.example_zh: 拍最后一条的时候，半个剧组都笑场了。

vocab.meaning_zh: （英国人的）坚忍克制、遇事不动声色的作风
vocab.example_en: He kept a stiff upper lip throughout the crisis.
vocab.example_zh: 整个危机期间，他一直不动声色地硬撑着。

vocab.meaning_zh: 而且，此外（置于句末加强语气）
vocab.example_en: She’s a brilliant actor and a fine writer to boot.
vocab.example_zh: 她是位出色的演员，而且还写得一手好文章。

vocab.meaning_zh: 庄重感、分量、威严（常形容公众人物的气场）
vocab.example_en: His gravitas made the whole show feel more serious.
vocab.example_zh: 他的那份厚重让整台节目都显得严肃起来。

vocab.meaning_zh: 笑话的“包袱”；引申为被人当成笑料的对象
vocab.example_en: The show was a punchline among critics before it was rebooted.
vocab.example_zh: 这部戏在重启之前，一直是评论界口中的笑柄。

vocab.meaning_zh: 炉火纯青的、技艺精湛的（形容专业人士）
vocab.example_en: She is a consummate storyteller.
vocab.example_zh: 她讲故事的本事炉火纯青。

vocab.meaning_zh: 打零工的、接活儿干的（jobbing actor 指没有固定剧团、靠一个个活儿吃饭的演员）
vocab.example_en: He spent ten years as a jobbing actor before his break.
vocab.example_zh: 他跑活儿跑了十年才等来出头之日。

vocab.meaning_zh: 自嘲的、贬低自己以显谦逊的
vocab.example_en: His self-deprecating humour puts everyone at ease.
vocab.example_zh: 他那种自嘲式的幽默让所有人都放松下来。

vocab.meaning_zh: 自以为了不起、翘尾巴、忘了自己是谁
vocab.example_en: A bit of fame and he got too big for his boots.
vocab.example_zh: 有了点名气，他就翘尾巴了。

vocab.meaning_zh: 史册、编年记录（the annals of … 常指某个领域被记载下来的历史）
vocab.example_en: That match has gone down in the annals of the club.
vocab.example_zh: 那场比赛已被写进俱乐部的史册。

sentences.en: We were from a younger generation and we wanted to shake up this Englishman who was so typical of his generation – stiff upper lip and a Yorkshireman to boot.
sentences.structure: 主干：We were from a younger generation // and we wanted to shake up this Englishman（两个并列分句）；修饰：who was so typical of his generation 是定语从句修饰 this Englishman；破折号后 stiff upper lip and a Yorkshireman to boot 是补充说明的同位成分（相当于 being ... ）
sentences.analysis_zh: and 连接两个并列分句，前一句交代背景（我们更年轻），后一句才是动作（想“晃一晃”他）。shake up 本义是“摇晃”，引申为“使某人的固有状态动摇、换个活法”。破折号后省略了 being，用两个名词短语把“他那一代典型英国人”具体化：stiff upper lip 是文化标签，a Yorkshireman to boot 再加一层地域标签，to boot 放句末起“而且还”的追加语气。整句用短促的口语补语收尾，符合人物回忆的谈话腔调。

sentences.en: It had occurred to him that I was grieving and on my own – and he did something about that.
sentences.structure: 主干：It had occurred to him ... and he did something about that（并列两句）；that I was grieving and on my own 是主语从句，it 为形式主语
sentences.analysis_zh: occur to sb 表示“（某个念头）出现在某人脑中”，主语用形式主语 it、真正内容放到 that 从句里，是英语里最自然的说法。用过去完成时 had occurred，暗示这个念头出现在他发出邀请之前，也就是“先想到，后行动”。破折号后的 and 分句是全句的重心：作者要夸的不是“他想到了”，而是“他为此做了点什么”——英语写人常用这种“想到 + 行动”的双拍结构来立人物。

sentences.en: In one of the Star Trek movies we did there was a scene written for Picard and Data, where Picard tells the story of how his family were burned in a fire.
sentences.structure: 主干：there was a scene；状语：In one of the Star Trek movies we did（we did 为省略关系词的定语从句修饰 movies）；修饰：written for Picard and Data 为过去分词短语后置修饰 scene；where 引导非限制性定语从句修饰 scene，其中 of how his family were burned in a fire 是介词 of 的宾语从句
sentences.analysis_zh: 口语叙述常用 there be 先把“有一场戏”抛出来，再把细节一层层往后挂：谁写的（written for ...）、戏里讲什么（where ...）。where 在这里等于 in which，指“在这场戏里”，不是地点状语。注意 written for Picard and Data 是过去分词被动式，逻辑主语就是 scene；后面 how 从句作 of 的宾语，说明 tells the story 的具体内容。

background.title: 《星际迷航：下一代》与三位当事人
background.text_zh: Star Trek: The Next Generation（1987—1994）是 60 年代原初系列之后的重启剧集，帕特里克·斯图尔特饰演企业号舰长让-吕克·皮卡德（Jean-Luc Picard），玛丽娜·瑟蒂斯饰演船上的顾问迪安娜·特洛伊（Deanna Troi），布伦特·斯派纳饰演机器人 Data。在斯图尔特加盟之前，原初系列在大众印象里常被当成“特效粗糙的太空肥皂剧”，这也是文中说它“曾经是个笑柄”的由来。斯图尔特出身皇家莎士比亚剧团（RSC），英国戏剧界把莎剧舞台看作演技的正统训练场，所以一位莎剧演员去演科幻剧舰长，在当时被视为提升剧集格调的大事——文中“他给这个角色带来了分量”正是指此。瑟蒂斯提到的“看着我的眼睛而不是 Data 的”，也只有在知道 Data 是机器人、没有人类情感这一设定后才读得懂。

background.title: 口音、地域与球迷身份：英国人的“出身暗号”
background.text_zh: 文中几个词都是英国社会的身份标记。cockney 指伦敦东区（尤其能听到“伦敦碗钟声”的范围）的工人阶级口音，瑟蒂斯特意保留它，等于公开宣告自己的出身；stiff upper lip 是外界对英国中上层“不轻易表露情绪”的刻板印象；Yorkshireman 则指向英格兰北部约克郡，常与直率、朴实、不装腔作势联系在一起。足球在这里也是身份标签：托特纳姆热刺（Spurs）是伦敦北部的俱乐部，阿森纳是同城的死敌，所以“像看阿森纳球迷那样看他”是极妙的一句调侃；哈德斯菲尔德镇队在约克郡，利兹联是同地区的传统强队，斯图尔特选择支持小城的哈德斯菲尔德而不是利兹或“光鲜的豪门”，在作者眼里恰恰证明他不攀附、不忘本。

title_en: ‘Bunch of baloney’: calls grow for Cop summit reforms as countries on track to fail nature targets
excerpt_en: Cop17, focused on protecting nature and restoring ecosystems, concludes on Saturday with critics saying system allows ‘one idiot’ to stall progress
body_en: Calls are growing for major reforms to UN biodiversity summits as countries fail to deliver on their promises to halt the destruction of the natural world, with governments likely on track to continue their record of never having met a target in the 34-year history of the convention.

Two weeks of negotiations at biodiversity Cop17 in Yerevan, Armenia, concluded on Saturday morning with countries vowing to redouble their efforts to meet this decade’s targets, which include commitments to protect 30% of the planet for nature, restore nearly a third of Earth’s degraded ecosystems and reform $500bn (£410bn) of environmentally damaging subsidies .

Agreed just four years ago by nearly every government on the planet, they aim to transform humanity’s relationship with nature . Despite progress in some areas, governments are way off track on meeting almost all of the targets. The UK is set to meet just three of the 23.

After talks that ran overnight from Friday into Saturday morning, countries signed off several measures, including a commitment to ramp up action on meeting existing targets and reaffirming a goal to increase biodiversity finance to $30bn a year by the end of the decade.

During the conference, environment ministers, activists and officials appealed for significant changes to the way the summits function to ensure governments follow through with meaningful action on the drivers of biodiversity loss.

Panama’s environment minister, Juan Carlos Navarro, a veteran conservationist, said the Cop process had been “designed to fail”, arguing that decisions should be taken by a majority as the consensus-based process allows “one idiot” to prevent agreement.

“A lot of what’s going on out here at the Cop is just a bunch of baloney and beautiful speeches and BS,” he told AFP earlier this week. “We cannot have – we cannot expect – a consensus between every nation on Earth on every topic. That’s ridiculous. Cops have been designed to fail, and they are not disappointing.”
He also argued that the UN should host a single environmental Cop each year to tackle the climate, biodiversity, plastics and other issues in one go.
“This just makes my blood boil, because while we fiddle, Rome burns,” he said.

The negotiations in the Armenian capital have seen Argentina, Saudi Arabia and Russia water down language on environmental ambition in the final agreement, while wealthier governments were divided on who would contribute more financial resources.

European nations would like to see additions to the list of donor states, as China and several of the Gulf states are still classified as developing countries in the UN process despite decades of rapid economic development. The final agreement in Yerevan left this issue open.

Key decisions on a fund to mobilise resources from firms that make money from digital forms of biodiversity, such as pharmaceutical companies, were postponed to the next summit in Ecuador in two years’ time. It had been hoped that the fund would generate £1bn a year for nature conservation, with a significant share going to Indigenous communities, but it has so far raised just over $10,000.
Related: Big pharma accused of ‘free-riding on nature’ as global fund attracts just $7,000

The calls for changes to the biodiversity Cop process echo an intervention by leading policy experts during climate Cop29 in Azerbaijan in 2024 who said the summit was “no longer fit for purpose” and needed to shift to focus on implementation.
Ruth Davis, the UK’s nature envoy, said she recognised that the meetings could be “extremely frustratiing”, but a huge amount of implementation was happening around the world.

“We’ve got to make the system actually deliver outcomes for people, otherwise they’ll lose confidence in it,” she said. “In the end, this is a process that is owned by governments who are parties to it. But I know we are going to find friends and allies in making the process work for the citizens of countries for whom this is really important, not least because they are the ones facing the impacts.”

Efforts to reform the UN’s sprawling environmental agenda are already under way. Inger Andersen, the executive director of the UN environment programme, said that the current systems were driving change, but they were moving too slowly.

“Right now, the environmental agenda is very cluttered. There are lots of meetings, important as each one is. Let’s begin with the easy stuff, like programmatic overlap between conventions, which has an energy-sapping effect,” said Andersen. “We identified the illegal wildlife trade back in the 70s as a problem, then we identified migratory species, then broader biodiversity, then wetlands.
“Each of these conventions came along at the right time, but we now have a plethora of them. Maybe we should think about that.”

enrich.title_zh: “一堆胡扯”：各国恐将再次错过自然保护目标，要求改革缔约方大会的呼声渐高
enrich.summary_zh: 联合国生物多样性 Cop17 在亚美尼亚埃里温落幕，各国仅承诺“加倍努力”落实本十年的 23 项自然目标，而多数国家进度严重落后。巴拿马环境部长批评协商一致的决策机制让峰会“被设计成失败”，呼吁每年只办一次统一的环境 Cop；关于数字生物多样性基金的设立也被推迟。联合国环境规划署承认环境议程过于杂乱，改革正在进行。

paragraphs.en: Calls are growing for major reforms to UN biodiversity summits as countries fail to deliver on their promises to halt the destruction of the natural world, with governments likely on track to continue their record of never having met a target in the 34-year history of the convention.
paragraphs.zh: 要求对联合国生物多样性峰会进行重大改革的呼声日益高涨，原因是各国未能兑现制止自然世界遭到破坏的承诺；各国政府很可能将延续一项纪录——在该公约 34 年的历史上，从未实现过任何一个目标。

paragraphs.en: Two weeks of negotiations at biodiversity Cop17 in Yerevan, Armenia, concluded on Saturday morning with countries vowing to redouble their efforts to meet this decade’s targets, which include commitments to protect 30% of the planet for nature, restore nearly a third of Earth’s degraded ecosystems and reform $500bn (£410bn) of environmentally damaging subsidies .
paragraphs.zh: 在亚美尼亚埃里温举行的生物多样性缔约方大会第十七次会议（Cop17）经过两周谈判，于周六上午结束。各国誓言加倍努力以实现本十年的目标，这些目标包括承诺将地球 30% 的面积划为自然保护地、恢复地球近三分之一的退化生态系统，以及改革 5000 亿美元（4100 亿英镑）对环境有害的补贴。

paragraphs.en: Agreed just four years ago by nearly every government on the planet, they aim to transform humanity’s relationship with nature . Despite progress in some areas, governments are way off track on meeting almost all of the targets. The UK is set to meet just three of the 23.
paragraphs.zh: 这些目标仅仅在四年前才由全球几乎所有政府一致通过，旨在彻底改变人类与自然的关系。尽管在某些领域取得了进展，但各国政府在实现几乎所有目标方面都严重偏离轨道。英国预计只能实现 23 个目标中的 3 个。

paragraphs.en: After talks that ran overnight from Friday into Saturday morning, countries signed off several measures, including a commitment to ramp up action on meeting existing targets and reaffirming a goal to increase biodiversity finance to $30bn a year by the end of the decade.
paragraphs.zh: 经过从周五持续到周六上午的通宵谈判，各国批准了若干措施，其中包括承诺加大力度落实现有目标，并重申到本十年末将生物多样性融资提高到每年 300 亿美元的目标。

paragraphs.en: During the conference, environment ministers, activists and officials appealed for significant changes to the way the summits function to ensure governments follow through with meaningful action on the drivers of biodiversity loss.
paragraphs.zh: 会议期间，环境部长、活动人士和官员呼吁对峰会的运作方式进行重大改革，以确保各国政府针对生物多样性丧失的驱动因素采取有意义的行动。

paragraphs.en: Panama’s environment minister, Juan Carlos Navarro, a veteran conservationist, said the Cop process had been “designed to fail”, arguing that decisions should be taken by a majority as the consensus-based process allows “one idiot” to prevent agreement.
paragraphs.zh: 巴拿马环境部长、资深自然保护主义者胡安·卡洛斯·纳瓦罗表示，缔约方大会的进程是“被设计成失败的”，他主张决定应以多数票通过，因为基于协商一致的进程会让“一个白痴”阻碍协议的达成。

paragraphs.en: “A lot of what’s going on out here at the Cop is just a bunch of baloney and beautiful speeches and BS,” he told AFP earlier this week. “We cannot have – we cannot expect – a consensus between every nation on Earth on every topic. That’s ridiculous. Cops have been designed to fail, and they are not disappointing.”
paragraphs.zh: “缔约方大会上发生的很多事情不过是一堆胡扯、漂亮的演讲和废话，”他本周早些时候对法新社说。“我们不可能——我们不能指望——地球上每个国家在每个议题上都达成共识。这太荒唐了。缔约方大会被设计成失败的，而它们也确实没有让人失望。”

paragraphs.en: He also argued that the UN should host a single environmental Cop each year to tackle the climate, biodiversity, plastics and other issues in one go.
paragraphs.zh: 他还主张，联合国应每年只举办一次统一的环境缔约方大会，一次性处理气候、生物多样性、塑料及其他问题。

paragraphs.en: “This just makes my blood boil, because while we fiddle, Rome burns,” he said.
paragraphs.zh: “这让我怒火中烧，因为当我们还在瞎忙活的时候，罗马已经烧起来了，”他说。

paragraphs.en: The negotiations in the Armenian capital have seen Argentina, Saudi Arabia and Russia water down language on environmental ambition in the final agreement, while wealthier governments were divided on who would contribute more financial resources.
paragraphs.zh: 在亚美尼亚首都举行的谈判中，阿根廷、沙特阿拉伯和俄罗斯淡化了最终协议中有关环境雄心的措辞，而较富裕的各国政府在谁应贡献更多财政资源的问题上意见不一。

paragraphs.en: European nations would like to see additions to the list of donor states, as China and several of the Gulf states are still classified as developing countries in the UN process despite decades of rapid economic development. The final agreement in Yerevan left this issue open.
paragraphs.zh: 欧洲国家希望捐助国名单能够扩大，因为中国和几个海湾国家尽管经历了几十年的快速发展，在联合国进程中仍被归类为发展中国家。埃里温最终协议将这一问题悬而未决。

paragraphs.en: Key decisions on a fund to mobilise resources from firms that make money from digital forms of biodiversity, such as pharmaceutical companies, were postponed to the next summit in Ecuador in two years’ time. It had been hoped that the fund would generate £1bn a year for nature conservation, with a significant share going to Indigenous communities, but it has so far raised just over $10,000.
paragraphs.zh: 关于设立一项基金、向利用数字化生物多样性信息获利的企业（如制药公司）筹集资金的关键决定，被推迟到两年后在厄瓜多尔举行的下一届峰会。人们原本希望该基金每年能为自然保护带来 10 亿英镑，其中相当大一部分将流向原住民社区，但该基金迄今只筹集到略高于 1 万美元。

paragraphs.en: Related: Big pharma accused of ‘free-riding on nature’ as global fund attracts just $7,000
paragraphs.zh: 相关报道：全球基金仅筹得 7000 美元，大型制药公司被指“免费搭车利用自然”

paragraphs.en: The calls for changes to the biodiversity Cop process echo an intervention by leading policy experts during climate Cop29 in Azerbaijan in 2024 who said the summit was “no longer fit for purpose” and needed to shift to focus on implementation.
paragraphs.zh: 要求改革生物多样性缔约方大会进程的呼声，与 2024 年在阿塞拜疆举行的气候缔约方大会第二十九次会议（Cop29）上一些主要政策专家的表态如出一辙，他们表示该峰会“已不再符合其宗旨”，需要转向以落实为重点。

paragraphs.en: Ruth Davis, the UK’s nature envoy, said she recognised that the meetings could be “extremely frustratiing”, but a huge amount of implementation was happening around the world.
paragraphs.zh: 英国自然事务特使露丝·戴维斯表示，她承认这些会议可能“极其令人沮丧”，但世界各地正在开展大量落实工作。

paragraphs.en: “We’ve got to make the system actually deliver outcomes for people, otherwise they’ll lose confidence in it,” she said. “In the end, this is a process that is owned by governments who are parties to it. But I know we are going to find friends and allies in making the process work for the citizens of countries for whom this is really important, not least because they are the ones facing the impacts.”
paragraphs.zh: “我们必须让这个体系真正为人们带来成果，否则他们就会对它失去信心，”她说。“归根结底，这是一个由作为缔约方的政府所掌控的进程。但我知道，在让这一进程服务于那些真正重视它的国家的公民方面，我们会找到朋友和盟友，尤其是因为他们正是承受影响的人。”

paragraphs.en: Efforts to reform the UN’s sprawling environmental agenda are already under way. Inger Andersen, the executive director of the UN environment programme, said that the current systems were driving change, but they were moving too slowly.
paragraphs.zh: 改革联合国庞杂环境议程的努力已经在进行中。联合国环境规划署执行主任英格·安德森表示，现行体系确实在推动变革，但进展太慢。

paragraphs.en: “Right now, the environmental agenda is very cluttered. There are lots of meetings, important as each one is. Let’s begin with the easy stuff, like programmatic overlap between conventions, which has an energy-sapping effect,” said Andersen. “We identified the illegal wildlife trade back in the 70s as a problem, then we identified migratory species, then broader biodiversity, then wetlands.
paragraphs.zh: “目前，环境议程非常杂乱。会议很多，每一个都很重要。让我们从容易的地方开始，比如各公约之间在项目安排上的重叠，这种重叠会消耗精力，”安德森说。“我们早在 70 年代就把非法野生动物贸易确定为一个问题，接着确定了迁徙物种，然后是更广泛的生物多样性，然后是湿地。”

paragraphs.en: “Each of these conventions came along at the right time, but we now have a plethora of them. Maybe we should think about that.”
paragraphs.zh: “这些公约每一个都出现在恰当的时候，但现在我们拥有的公约已经太多了。也许我们应该考虑一下这个问题。”

sentences.en: Calls are growing for major reforms to UN biodiversity summits as countries fail to deliver on their promises to halt the destruction of the natural world, with governments likely on track to continue their record of never having met a target in the 34-year history of the convention.
sentences.structure: 主干：Calls are growing for major reforms（主谓+介词短语）／修饰：as countries fail to deliver on... 原因状语从句；to halt the destruction... 修饰 promises；with governments likely on track to... 为 with 复合结构作伴随状语，说明原因带来的后果。
sentences.analysis_zh: 新闻英语典型的“结论先行”句式：先抛出“改革呼声高涨”，再用 as 从句交代原因，最后用 with 复合结构补充后果。注意 record of never having met a target：of 后接动名词完成式，表示“从未实现过目标”这一持续 34 年的纪录；be on track to continue that record 字面是“有望延续纪录”，实际意思是“有望继续失败”，带有讽刺意味。

sentences.en: Key decisions on a fund to mobilise resources from firms that make money from digital forms of biodiversity, such as pharmaceutical companies, were postponed to the next summit in Ecuador in two years’ time.
sentences.structure: 主干：Key decisions ... were postponed to the next summit（主谓+状语）／修饰：on a fund 修饰 decisions；to mobilise resources 修饰 fund；from firms 修饰 resources；that make money from digital forms of biodiversity 为定语从句修饰 firms；such as pharmaceutical companies 为插入的同位语。
sentences.analysis_zh: 主语中心词 decisions 与谓语 were postponed 之间隔了 20 多个词，是外刊常见的长距离主谓分离，阅读时先抓 Key decisions ... were postponed 这个骨架，再把层层后置修饰挂回去。digital forms of biodiversity 指“数字序列信息”（DSI），即基因序列数据；把这么长的修饰塞在主语后，是为了让“推迟”这一新闻点落到句末以突出重点。

sentences.en: But I know we are going to find friends and allies in making the process work for the citizens of countries for whom this is really important, not least because they are the ones facing the impacts.
sentences.structure: 主干：I know (that) we are going to find friends and allies／修饰：in making the process work... 作状语，说明在哪方面找到盟友；for whom this is really important 为定语从句修饰 countries；not least because... 引导原因状语，表示“尤其是因为”。
sentences.analysis_zh: 这句是引语中较绕的一句：make the process work for sb（让进程为某人服务）是“make + 宾语 + 动词原形”的使役结构；for whom 把介词提前，属于正式书面语。not least because 是外刊高频的“递进式原因”表达，意为“尤其因为/特别是由于”，比 especially because 更含蓄。

background.title: 昆明-蒙特利尔全球生物多样性框架与“30×30”
background.text_zh: 2022 年《生物多样性公约》第十五次缔约方大会（Cop15）在中国昆明（线下部分在加拿大蒙特利尔举行）通过了“昆明-蒙特利尔全球生物多样性框架”，共 23 个目标，要求到 2030 年保护地球 30% 的陆地和海洋（即“30×30”）、恢复 30% 的退化生态系统、每年减少 5000 亿美元有害补贴，并把每年流向发展中国家的生物多样性资金提高到 300 亿美元。文中所谓“this decade's targets”即指此框架。由于各国提交的国家行动计划普遍不足以达标，这才引出对峰会机制的质疑。

background.title: Calì 基金、数字序列信息与“共识”议事规则
background.text_zh: 所谓“digital forms of biodiversity”指数字序列信息（DSI），即药物研发中大量使用的基因序列数据：制药企业利用这些数据开发产品获利，却基本不向提供数据的原产国或原住民社区付费。2024 年哥伦比亚卡利举行的 Cop16 决定设立“卡利基金”（Calì Fund），鼓励受益企业自愿捐款，本文指出其实际到账仅一万余美元。另外，《生物多样性公约》长期按“协商一致”方式作出决定，任何一个代表团都可以阻止协议，这正是巴拿马部长批评“被设计成失败”“一个白痴就能挡住”的制度根源。

title_en: From gold rush to cosmic questions: a South Dakota mine and the search for the secrets of the universe
excerpt_en: A mile beneath the Black Hills, scientists are building giant detectors to analyse neutrino particles – and possibly find the answer to existence
body_en: For more than a century, the mining town of Lead, in the Black Hills of South Dakota, attracted workers with a taste for gold. Now, a flagship experiment being built in the old mine is drawing scientists in search of more intriguing riches: answers to the deepest mysteries of the universe.

Construction of the Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment (Dune) in the former Homestake mine is due to start on Monday. Engineers will begin assembling four giant detectors inside caverns blasted from rock a mile underground.

Once switched on, the detectors will quietly spark and flicker as ghostly particles called neutrinos hurtle through them. Some will arrive from the sun and distant supernovae, others in an intense beam sent through 800 miles (1,300km) of rock from a government laboratory near Chicago, Illinois.

Observing the neutrinos could uncover entirely new science and shed light on cosmic spectacles, such as the death of stars and the birth of black holes. Scientists are particularly hopeful of solving one of the most enduring puzzles in nature: why everything around us is made from matter and not its “evil twin”, antimatter. In other words, why we, and why anything, is here at all.

Interactive “It’s a super exciting time to be working on this,” said Dr Kate Shaw, an experimental particle physicist on Dune from the University of Sussex. “Neutrinos do not make sense yet and they could open a door to new physics.”

Neutrinos are the most abundant matter particles in the universe, outnumbered only by photons, the massless particles of light that illuminate the universe. They are produced in natural nuclear reactions, such as those that power the sun, in radioactive decay and in particle accelerators.

Even by physicists’ standards, neutrinos are oddballs. The chargeless particles barely interact with other matter: about a trillion pass unnoticed through your body each second. Neutrinos come in three varieties, all with minuscule but different masses. Weirdly, they change from one variety to another, a process called oscillation, as they travel. “It’s a very strange behaviour,” said Shaw. “It’s like me throwing you an apple and it turns into a banana.”

Lead has a history with these peculiar particles. In the 1960s, the physicist Ray Davis followed miners down the shaft and built a detector from a 100,000-gallon tank filled with dry-cleaning fluid. Shielded so deep beneath the ground, the detector became the first to record neutrinos from the sun as they struck chlorine atoms in the fluid and turned them into argon.

The mine closed in 2001 and transitioned, thanks to visionary forethought, into a dedicated subterranean laboratory, the Sanford Underground Research Facility (Surf). It is already home to the Lux-Zeplin (LZ) experiment which last month reported the first potential detection of dark matter.

“We’ve gone from mining the Earth to helping scientists explore the universe,” said Robin Lucero, Lead’s city administrator, whose family has lived locally for generations. “We’re incredibly proud and lucky that Dune is happening here, and Surf, which has other experiments like LZ. Having world-class science brings new opportunities, new people and new possibilities for our local businesses and especially our young people.”

Unlike Davis’s apparatus, the Dune experiment is enormous. Made from more than 4,000 tonnes of steel, the detectors will stand up to five-storeys high and hold a combined 70,000 tonnes of liquid argon that must be chilled to -200C. Assembling the detectors should take nearly three years. Filling them with liquid argon, another year.

“This is a heavy duty engineering operation,” and a partnership with the skilled local workforce, said Prof David Newbold, of the UK’s Science and Technology Facilities Council and a Dune spokesperson. “It’s like building a ship underground.” The UK is the largest international partner in the US-led experiment and is making core detector components, critical computing to reconstruct events in the detectors, and the graphite target needed to generate neutrinos at Femilab, a particle physics facility in Illinois.

Once operational, Dune will study an intense beam of neutrinos sent from Fermilab through 800 miles of the Earth’s crust and mantle. Most neutrinos will shoot straight through, but every so often one will strike an argon atom, creating a flicker of light and a pulse of electric charge. Analysing these will reveal intimate details about the mysterious particles.

One big question surrounds the masses of different neutrinos. Which is lightest and which heaviest? The answer could reveal fundamental new forces of nature. And in an attempt to answer the matter v antimatter question, Dune will look for subtle differences between neutrinos and their antimatter twins, antineutrinos.
Beyond the beams of particles sent from Fermilab, Dune will also study neutrinos arriving from space, carrying with them fresh information on stellar explosions and the formation of black holes.

Earlier this month, the Nobel prize for physics honoured the Belgian researcher Francis Halzen, who used a cubic kilometre of Antarctica to detect high-energy neutrinos from deep space. But detection is far from the end of the story. “This really is going to be a golden era,” Newbold said. “There’s a lot more of that to come.”

enrich.title_zh: 从淘金热到宇宙之问：南达科他州一座矿井与宇宙奥秘的探寻
enrich.summary_zh: 南达科他州黑山地区的矿业小镇利德曾因淘金而兴，如今当地废弃的霍姆斯塔克金矿正被改造成深地下中微子实验（Dune）的场址。工程即将动工，将在井下组装四台巨型液氩探测器，接收来自费米实验室的中微子束流以及来自太阳、超新星的中微子，以破解中微子质量次序、物质为何多于反物质等根本谜题。当地人与科学家都期待这场从采矿到基础科学的转型带来新的机遇。

Now, a flagship experiment being built in the old mine is drawing scientists in search of more intriguing riches: answers to the deepest mysteries of the universe.
paragraphs.zh: 一个多世纪以来，南达科他州黑山地区的矿业小镇利德（Lead）以淘金梦吸引着一批批工人。如今，一座建在这座老矿井里的旗舰级实验，正吸引科学家前来寻找更诱人的财富：宇宙最深奥之谜的答案。

paragraphs.en: Construction of the Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment (Dune) in the former Homestake mine is due to start on Monday. Engineers will begin assembling four giant detectors inside caverns blasted from rock a mile underground.
paragraphs.zh: 深地下中微子实验（Dune）将在这座昔日的霍姆斯塔克（Homestake）矿中动工，时间定在周一。工程师们将开始在一英里深的地下、由岩层炸出的洞室里组装四台巨型探测器。

paragraphs.en: Once switched on, the detectors will quietly spark and flicker as ghostly particles called neutrinos hurtle through them. Some will arrive from the sun and distant supernovae, others in an intense beam sent through 800 miles (1,300km) of rock from a government laboratory near Chicago, Illinois.
paragraphs.zh: 一旦启动，当被称为中微子的“幽灵粒子”疾驰穿过时，探测器会静静地闪出火花与微光。有些中微子来自太阳和遥远的超新星，另一些则来自伊利诺伊州芝加哥附近一座政府实验室发射的强束流——它们穿越了800英里（1300公里）的岩层。

paragraphs.zh: 观测中微子或许能带来全新的科学，并揭示恒星死亡、黑洞诞生这类宇宙奇观。科学家尤其希望能解开自然界最持久的谜题之一：为什么我们周围的一切都由物质构成，而不是由它的“邪恶双胞胎”——反物质构成。换句话说，为什么我们、为什么任何事物，竟然存在于此。

paragraphs.zh: “参与这项工作真是超级令人兴奋，”苏塞克斯大学实验粒子物理学家、Dune项目成员凯特·肖（Kate Shaw）博士说，“中微子至今仍说不通，而它们可能打开一扇通往新物理学的大门。”

paragraphs.en: Neutrinos are the most abundant matter particles in the universe, outnumbered only by photons, the massless particles of light that illuminate the universe. They are produced in natural nuclear reactions, such as those that power the sun, in radioactive decay and in particle accelerators.
paragraphs.zh: 中微子是宇宙中数量最多的物质粒子，只有光子比它们更多——光子是照亮宇宙的无质量光粒子。中微子产生于天然核反应（例如驱动太阳的那些反应）、放射性衰变以及粒子加速器之中。

paragraphs.zh: 即便以物理学家的标准来看，中微子也是怪胎。这种不带电的粒子几乎不与其他物质发生相互作用：每秒约有1万亿个中微子穿过你的身体而不被察觉。中微子有三种类型，质量都极小，却各不相同。奇怪的是，它们在飞行途中会从一种类型变成另一种，这一过程称为“振荡”。“这是非常奇怪的行为，”肖说，“就像我扔给你一个苹果，它却变成了香蕉。”

paragraphs.zh: 利德与这些奇特粒子早有渊源。20世纪60年代，物理学家雷·戴维斯（Ray Davis）跟随矿工下到竖井，用一只装满干洗液的10万加仑大罐建成了一台探测器。由于深藏地下、屏蔽良好，这台探测器成为首个记录到太阳中微子的装置——中微子击中液体中的氯原子，把它们变成了氩。

paragraphs.en: The mine closed in 2001 and transitioned, thanks to visionary forethought, into a dedicated subterranean laboratory, the Sanford Underground Research Facility (Surf). It is already home to the Lux-Zeplin (LZ) experiment which last month reported the first potential detection of dark matter.
paragraphs.zh: 这座矿于2001年关闭，并由于有远见的前瞻性规划，转型为一座专门的地下实验室——桑福德地下研究设施（Surf）。这里已经是Lux-Zeplin（LZ）实验的所在地，该实验上个月报告了首次可能探测到暗物质的结果。

paragraphs.en: “We’ve gone from mining the Earth to helping scientists explore the universe,” said Robin Lucero, Lead’s city administrator, whose family has lived locally for generations. “We’re incredibly proud and lucky that Dune is happening here, and Surf, which has other experiments like LZ. Having world-class science brings new opportunities, new people and new possibilities for our local businesses and especially our young people.”
paragraphs.zh: “我们从开采地球，转向帮助科学家探索宇宙，”利德市市政官罗宾·卢塞罗（Robin Lucero）说，她的家族已在此地生活了好几代。“Dune能在这里落地，还有拥有LZ等其他实验的Surf，我们无比自豪，也非常幸运。拥有世界级的科学，会给我们的本地企业、尤其是年轻人带来新机遇、新面孔和新可能。”
