paragraphs.zh: 与戴维斯的装置不同，Dune实验规模极其庞大。探测器由4000多吨钢材制成，高达五层楼，总共容纳7万吨液态氩，而液态氩必须冷却到-200℃。组装探测器预计要近三年时间，灌注液态氩还要再花一年。

paragraphs.en: “This is a heavy duty engineering operation,” and a partnership with the skilled local workforce, said Prof David Newbold, of the UK’s Science and Technology Facilities Council and a Dune spokesperson. “It’s like building a ship underground.” The UK is the largest international partner in the US-led experiment and is making core detector components, critical computing to reconstruct events in the detectors, and the graphite target needed to generate neutrinos at Femilab, a particle physics facility in Illinois.
paragraphs.zh: “这是一项重型工程作业”，而且需要与当地熟练劳动力合作，英国科学与技术设施理事会的戴维·纽博尔德（David Newbold）教授、同时也是Dune的发言人说。“这就像在地下造一艘船。”在这项由美国主导的实验中，英国是最大的国际合作伙伴，正在制造核心探测器部件、用于重建探测器内事件的关键计算系统，以及在伊利诺伊州粒子物理设施费米实验室（Fermilab）产生中微子所需的石墨靶。

paragraphs.en: Once operational, Dune will study an intense beam of neutrinos sent from Fermilab through 800 miles of the Earth’s crust and mantle. Most neutrinos will shoot straight through, but every so often one will strike an argon atom, creating a flicker of light and a pulse of electric charge. Analysing these will reveal intimate details about the mysterious particles.
paragraphs.zh: 投入运行后，Dune将研究中微子强束流——这些中微子由费米实验室发出，穿过800英里的地壳和地幔。大多数中微子会径直穿过，但偶尔会有一个击中氩原子，产生一瞬闪光和一束电荷脉冲。分析这些信号，将揭示有关这些神秘粒子的详尽细节。

paragraphs.en: One big question surrounds the masses of different neutrinos. Which is lightest and which heaviest? The answer could reveal fundamental new forces of nature. And in an attempt to answer the matter v antimatter question, Dune will look for subtle differences between neutrinos and their antimatter twins, antineutrinos.
paragraphs.zh: 一个大问题围绕不同中微子的质量展开：哪一种最轻，哪一种最重？答案可能揭示自然界中全新的基本作用力。而为了回答“物质对反物质”的问题，Dune将寻找中微子与其反物质伙伴——反中微子之间的细微差异。

paragraphs.en: Beyond the beams of particles sent from Fermilab, Dune will also study neutrinos arriving from space, carrying with them fresh information on stellar explosions and the formation of black holes.
paragraphs.zh: 除了费米实验室发出的粒子束，Dune还将研究来自太空的中微子，它们携带着关于恒星爆发和黑洞形成的新信息。

paragraphs.en: Earlier this month, the Nobel prize for physics honoured the Belgian researcher Francis Halzen, who used a cubic kilometre of Antarctica to detect high-energy neutrinos from deep space. But detection is far from the end of the story. “This really is going to be a golden era,” Newbold said. “There’s a lot more of that to come.”
paragraphs.zh: 本月早些时候，诺贝尔物理学奖授予比利时研究者弗朗西斯·哈尔岑（Francis Halzen），他借助南极洲一立方公里（的冰体）探测来自深空的高能中微子。但探测远非故事的终点。“这确实将是一个黄金时代，”纽博尔德说，“后面还有更多精彩。”

vocab.meaning_zh: 旗舰级的、最重要、最具代表性的（项目、机构等）
vocab.example_en: The lab is home to a flagship experiment in fusion energy.
vocab.example_zh: 该实验室承担着一项旗舰级的聚变能实验。

vocab.meaning_zh: 炸开、爆破（岩石等）；文中用过去分词 blasted 作定语
vocab.example_en: The tunnels were blasted out of solid granite.
vocab.example_zh: 这些隧道是从坚硬的花岗岩中爆破开凿出来的。

vocab.meaning_zh: （以极快速度）飞驰、猛冲
vocab.example_en: Particles hurtle through the detector at nearly the speed of light.
vocab.example_zh: 粒子以接近光速飞驰穿过探测器。

vocab.meaning_zh: 使……变得清楚，阐明，揭示
vocab.example_en: The findings could shed light on how galaxies first formed.
vocab.example_zh: 这些发现或有助于揭示星系最初是如何形成的。

vocab.meaning_zh: 振荡；（中微子）在三种“味”之间来回转变的现象
vocab.example_en: Neutrino oscillation proved that the particles have mass.
vocab.example_zh: 中微子振荡证明了这种粒子具有质量。

vocab.meaning_zh: 怪人、异类；文中指“与众不同的怪家伙”
vocab.example_en: Among the known particles, the neutrino is the oddball.
vocab.example_zh: 在已知粒子中，中微子是个异类。

vocab.meaning_zh: 极小的、微乎其微的
vocab.example_en: The differences in mass are minuscule but scientifically crucial.
vocab.example_zh: 这些质量差异极其微小，但在科学上至关重要。

vocab.meaning_zh: 屏蔽、遮蔽（使免受辐射、干扰等）
vocab.example_en: The rock above shields the detector from cosmic rays.
vocab.example_zh: 上方的岩层为探测器屏蔽了宇宙射线。

vocab.meaning_zh: （熟词僻义）详尽的、深入的、细微的（细节、了解）
vocab.example_en: The data gives an intimate picture of what happens inside the nucleus.
vocab.example_zh: 这些数据详尽地呈现了原子核内部发生的过程。

vocab.meaning_zh: 在数量上超过
vocab.example_en: Photons far outnumber every other particle in the universe.
vocab.example_zh: 在宇宙中，光子的数量远远超过其他任何粒子。

sentences.en: Shielded so deep beneath the ground, the detector became the first to record neutrinos from the sun as they struck chlorine atoms in the fluid and turned them into argon.
sentences.structure: 主干：the detector became the first（主—系—表）；修饰：句首过去分词短语 Shielded... 作原因/条件状语；to record... 作后置定语修饰 the first；as they struck... and turned... 为时间状语从句，主语 they 指 neutrinos。
sentences.analysis_zh: 这句的主干只有“探测器成为第一个”三层意思，其余全靠分词短语和时间状语从句挂上去。句首的 Shielded so deep... 既是原因也交代了实验的关键设计——深埋地下以屏蔽宇宙射线本底，这是这类中微子实验的必要条件，作者把它前置，避免了“主句之后再来一串解释”的拖沓。as 引导的从句里两个并列谓语 struck 和 turned 说明了探测原理：中微子把氯原子变成氩原子，戴维斯正是靠数氩原子来“数”中微子。

sentences.en: The mine closed in 2001 and transitioned, thanks to visionary forethought, into a dedicated subterranean laboratory, the Sanford Underground Research Facility (Surf).
sentences.structure: 主干：The mine closed... and transitioned into a laboratory（并列谓语）；修饰：thanks to visionary forethought 为插入的原因状语（用逗号隔开）；the Sanford Underground Research Facility (Surf) 是 laboratory 的同位语，起命名作用。
sentences.analysis_zh: 主句并不复杂，难点在于插入语把 transitioned 和它的介词宾语 into... 拆开了，读者容易在 thanks to 处断句而丢掉后面的 into。英文常用这种插入式状语来加评论，中文则习惯先说原因再说结果，所以译成“由于……而转型为”。同位语放在句末是英文给机构“命名”的常规做法，翻译时用破折号或“即”引出最自然。

sentences.en: Once operational, Dune will study an intense beam of neutrinos sent from Fermilab through 800 miles of the Earth’s crust and mantle.
sentences.structure: 主干：Dune will study a beam（主—谓—宾）；修饰：Once operational 是省略式状语从句（= Once it is operational）；of neutrinos 修饰 beam；sent from Fermilab through 800 miles... 为过去分词短语后置修饰 neutrinos。
sentences.analysis_zh: Once operational 是“连词+形容词”的省略结构，比 when it is operational 更书面、更简洁，外刊科技报道里很常见。真正的信息量在后面的过去分词短语：sent from... 交代来源，through 800 miles of the crust and mantle 交代中微子要穿透的路程——这既是实验的物理条件（中微子会在这段路程中发生振荡），也暗中解释了为什么要把探测器建在800英里之外，而不是紧挨着加速器。

background.title: DUNE、费米实验室与桑福德地下实验室
background.text_zh: DUNE（Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment，深地下中微子实验）是一项由美国能源部下属的费米国家加速器实验室（Fermilab，位于芝加哥附近的伊利诺伊州巴达维亚）主导的大型国际合作项目。它的核心设计是“长基线”实验：在费米实验室产生一束高强度的中微子，让其穿过约1300公里（800英里）的地壳和地幔，打到南达科他州利德市地下一英里深的巨型液氩探测器里，通过比较“发出时”和“到达时”中微子的种类比例，研究中微子振荡、质量次序以及物质与反物质的不对称。之所以要深埋，是为了用岩层挡住宇宙射线和其他本底噪声。承接实验的桑福德地下研究设施（Sanford Underground Research Facility, SURF）就建在已关闭的霍姆斯塔克金矿中，同一地点还运行着寻找暗物质、无中微子双贝塔衰变等实验。

background.title: 霍姆斯塔克金矿与雷·戴维斯的太阳中微子实验
background.text_zh: 霍姆斯塔克矿曾是北美最深、产量极高的金矿之一，也正是“利德（Lead，读作 leed）”与邻近的戴德伍德（Deadwood）在19世纪70年代淘金潮中兴起的原因。1960年代，布鲁克黑文国家实验室的物理学家雷·戴维斯（Ray Davis）在这座矿井里灌满10万加仑全氯乙烯（干洗液），利用中微子把氯-37转化为氩-37的反应来“捕捉”太阳中微子，这就是著名的“太阳中微子之谜”的起点：实测数量只有理论预期的约三分之一，直到中微子振荡被发现才得以解释。戴维斯因此获得2002年诺贝尔物理学奖。文中提到的LZ（Lux-ZEPLIN）是同一实验室中的液氙暗物质探测实验；而第16段提到的弗朗西斯·哈尔岑，则是“冰立方”（IceCube）中微子天文台（建在南极冰层下）的负责人，2025年诺贝尔物理学奖得主。

title_en: War Is Hell—And The Mosquito Bowl Won’t Let Us Forget It
excerpt_en: Peter Berg's World War II movie is awash in violence. But when it comes to depicting war, less is often more

enrich.title_zh: 战争是地狱——而《蚊子碗》不肯让我们忘记这一点
enrich.summary_zh: 这是《时代》娱乐版对彼得·伯格执导的二战题材影片《蚊子碗》的一句短评式提要。提要先用“充斥着暴力”概括影片的直观观感，随后笔锋一转，抛出全片的评价立场：就战争题材的呈现而言，含蓄克制往往比一味铺陈更有力量。短短两句话把“影片很暴力”与“但不该这么暴力”并置，暗示评论者对这部作品并不完全买账。

paragraphs.en: Peter Berg's World War II movie is awash in violence. But when it comes to depicting war, less is often more
paragraphs.zh: 彼得·伯格的这部二战电影充斥着暴力。但就描绘战争而言，少往往即是多。

vocab.meaning_zh: 充斥、淹没于（某物之中）；本义指“被水冲刷、浸泡”，外刊中大量用作引申义，形容数量多到泛滥的程度
vocab.example_en: The market is awash in cheap imported goods.
vocab.example_zh: 市场上充斥着廉价进口商品。

vocab.meaning_zh: 描绘、刻画、表现（尤指用文字或影像再现某情景）
vocab.example_en: The novel depicts life in a small mining town.
vocab.example_zh: 这部小说描绘了一座矿业小镇的生活。

vocab.meaning_zh: 谈到、涉及……时；用于把话题收窄到某个特定方面，后接名词或动名词，是外刊评论、议论文的高频过渡语
vocab.example_en: When it comes to tackling climate change, rhetoric is cheap.
vocab.example_zh: 在应对气候变化这件事上，空谈最不值钱。

vocab.meaning_zh: “少即是多”；常用来表达克制、留白反而效果更好，出自现代主义建筑大师密斯·凡·德·罗的设计理念，后被广泛借用于艺术评论
vocab.example_en: His latest album proves that, in music as in film, less is more.
vocab.example_zh: 他的新专辑证明：音乐与电影一样，少即是多。

vocab.meaning_zh: 暴力、暴力场面；在影视评论中通常指作品呈现的打斗、血腥等画面内容
vocab.example_en: The film's graphic violence caused an uproar among critics.
vocab.example_zh: 影片中露骨的血腥暴力场面在评论界引起哗然。

vocab.meaning_zh: 电影（美式说法，英式多用 film）；注意本文在同一个句子里 movie 与 depicting 形成“前者口语化、后者书面化”的语体落差
vocab.example_en: The movie is based on a true story.
vocab.example_zh: 这部电影改编自真实事件。

sentences.en: Peter Berg's World War II movie is awash in violence.
sentences.structure: 主干：Peter Berg's World War II movie（主语）+ is（系动词）+ awash in violence（表语）；无从句、无多余修饰，是一句典型的“主系表”短句。
sentences.analysis_zh: 句子的全部重量都压在表语短语 awash in 上。如果只说 is violent，只是陈述“有暴力”；而用 awash in（字面“被水淹着”）就把暴力写成了数量上的泛滥、扑面而来的浸泡感，一个隐喻替掉了一整句描写，这正是电影评论常见的写法——最短的句子干最重的活。主语用作者+国籍式的 Peter Berg's World War II movie 来限定，属于信息前置：读者一进来就知道是谁的什么片子。

sentences.en: But when it comes to depicting war, less is often more
sentences.structure: 主干：less（主语）+ is（系动词）+ often（状语）+ more（表语）；when it comes to depicting war 是状语成分，由介词短语 when it comes to + 动名词组成，前置在句首，用来划定“少即是多”这条判断的适用范围。
sentences.analysis_zh: 这句的妙处在于转折与收窄同时完成。but 把上文“影片充斥着暴力”的客观描述立刻翻成评价立场；when it comes to depicting war 又把这个评价框进“战争题材”这一具体领域，避免读者把“less is more”误解成对所有电影的普遍主张。主干选用了 less is more 这个固定说法，而插入 often 是关键的软化处理：作者留下“往往如此”而非“必然如此”的余地，评论语气由此从断言变成行家的经验之谈。整句只有七个词作主干，却完成了“断言＋限定“两层意思，正是提要型写作的密度所在。

background.title: 《蚊子碗》指的是什么
background.text_zh: Mosquito Bowl 原指 1944 年圣诞前在太平洋瓜达尔卡纳尔岛举行的一场橄榄球赛：当时美军两支海军陆战队（分别来自第 6 团与第 29 团）在等待下一场战役期间对阵，参赛者中许多人是战前大学橄榄球明星，队中还有后来的职业球员。此役之后的冲绳战役中，这些球员大量阵亡。记者 Buzz Bissinger 2022 年出版的同名纪实作品让这段往事广为人知，彼得·伯格的影片即据此改编。这里只是标题来源的背景，不涉及本文评论的具体内容。

background.title: 彼得·伯格其人与战争片传统
background.text_zh: Peter Berg 是美国导演、演员，代表作包括《胜利之光》《孤独的幸存者》《深海浩劫》等，擅长处理真实事件与男性群像，也常因镜头语言直接、动作场面猛烈而受讨论。好莱坞战争片长期存在一条争论线：是像《拯救大兵瑞恩》开头那样以极度写实的血腥震撼观众，还是像《现代启示录》《全金属外壳》那样用留白与荒诞感处理暴力——“less is more”正是这条脉络上的老话题，也是理解这条提要评价落点的关键。

title_en: The True Story of Tragedy and Perseverance Behind Everest: The Other Side
excerpt_en: When tragedy struck during the filming of a mountaineering documentary, the filmmakers and subject faced a decision about whether to continue.

enrich.title_zh: 《珠峰：另一面》背后关于悲剧与坚持的真实故事
enrich.summary_zh: 这篇报道聚焦一部登山纪录片的拍摄过程：拍摄期间发生了悲剧性事故，摄制团队与片中的拍摄对象随即面临一个艰难抉择，是就此中止拍摄，还是继续把片子做完。摘要只点出这一核心冲突，并未交代事故的具体情形与最终决定，正文应当围绕「灾难之后还要不要继续拍摄」这一伦理与情感难题展开。

paragraphs.en: When tragedy struck during the filming of a mountaineering documentary, the filmmakers and subject faced a decision about whether to continue.
paragraphs.zh: 一部登山纪录片的拍摄过程中发生了悲剧，摄制人员和片中的拍摄对象因此面临一个抉择：拍摄是否还要继续下去。

vocab.meaning_zh: （灾难、疾病、不幸等）突然降临、袭来；此处 tragedy struck 即「悲剧突然发生」
vocab.example_en: Just as the expedition set off, disaster struck: an avalanche buried the base camp.
vocab.example_zh: 探险队刚出发，灾难就降临了：一场雪崩掩埋了大本营。

vocab.meaning_zh: （影片的）拍摄、摄制过程
vocab.example_en: Filming was suspended for two weeks after the accident.
vocab.example_zh: 事故发生后，拍摄暂停了两周。

vocab.meaning_zh: 登山运动；（专业性、挑战性的）高山攀登
vocab.example_en: He has written several books on mountaineering in the Himalayas.
vocab.example_zh: 他写过好几本关于喜马拉雅登山运动的书。

vocab.meaning_zh: 纪录片
vocab.example_en: The documentary follows three climbers through a single season.
vocab.example_zh: 这部纪录片跟踪拍摄了三名登山者一个登山季的经历。

vocab.meaning_zh: （熟词僻义）拍摄对象、被记录/研究对象；此处指纪录片所跟拍的那个人
vocab.example_en: The director spent a year gaining the trust of her subject.
vocab.example_zh: 导演花了一年时间赢得拍摄对象的信任。

vocab.meaning_zh: 面临抉择（外刊高频搭配，强调不得不做、且不好做的决定）
vocab.example_en: The company now faces a decision: cut costs or close down.
vocab.example_zh: 公司现在面临抉择：要么削减成本，要么关门。

sentences.en: When tragedy struck during the filming of a mountaineering documentary, the filmmakers and subject faced a decision about whether to continue.
sentences.structure: 主干：the filmmakers and subject（并列主语）faced（谓语）a decision（宾语）。修饰：When... 引导时间状语从句，交代背景；about whether to continue 是介词短语，作后置定语修饰 decision。
sentences.analysis_zh: 这句话只有一个主句，但信息密度很高。前半句用 When 从句把「悲剧发生」压缩成背景，主语用 filmmakers and subject 把「拍的人」和「被拍的人」并列，暗示两方都被卷入同一困境；宾语 a decision 后面用 about whether to continue 这个「介词 + whether 不定式」结构点出抉择内容。全句不交代悲剧是什么、结果如何，是典型的报道式悬念写法：用一句话抛出核心冲突，把细节留给正文。

background.title: 登山纪录片的拍摄风险
background.text_zh: 在高海拔地区拍片，摄制组本身就是登山队：他们要背着摄影器材适应海拔、穿越冰裂缝与雪崩区，工作环境与登山者完全相同。因此一旦山上出事，镜头记录下的往往不只是被拍摄者的事故，也包括摄制团队自身亲历的危险，这也是此类纪录片常被讨论的伦理问题。

background.title: 「拍还是不拍」的纪录片伦理
background.text_zh: 纪录片界长期争论一个问题：当拍摄对象遭遇不幸时，导演应当停机施救、陪伴，还是继续拍摄？继续拍常被批评为「消费他人苦难」，但停止拍摄也可能让当事人的经历失去被记录、被见证的机会。摘要中「faced a decision about whether to continue」正指向这一矛盾。

title_en: Breaking Down the Supernatural Ending of Dead-End Job
excerpt_en: In this Squid Game-like fantasy horror, Lee Jae-wook stars as a jobless 30-something who takes a strange and fearsome job out of desperation.

enrich.title_zh: 《Dead-End Job》的超自然结局解析
enrich.summary_zh: 这篇《时代》周刊娱乐版文章解析韩剧《Dead-End Job》的结局。该剧是一部类似《鱿鱼游戏》的奇幻恐怖作品，主角是李宰旭饰演的三十多岁无业男子，他在走投无路之下接受了一份诡异而可怕的工作。摘要只交代了设定，未透露结局细节。

paragraphs.en: In this Squid Game-like fantasy horror, Lee Jae-wook stars as a jobless 30-something who takes a strange and fearsome job out of desperation.
paragraphs.zh: 在这部类似《鱿鱼游戏》的奇幻恐怖作品中，李宰旭饰演一名三十多岁、没有工作的男子，他因走投无路而接下了一份诡异又可怕的工作。

sentences.en: In this Squid Game-like fantasy horror, Lee Jae-wook stars as a jobless 30-something who takes a strange and fearsome job out of desperation.
sentences.structure: 主干：Lee Jae-wook stars as a jobless 30-something（主谓+as 引导的宾语补足成分）／修饰：In this Squid Game-like fantasy horror 作句首状语，交代作品类型与语境；who takes a strange and fearsome job out of desperation 是定语从句，修饰 30-something。
sentences.analysis_zh: 句子用「状语+主干+定语从句」的典型外刊提要结构：先一句点明类型坐标（Squid Game-like fantasy horror），让读者立刻有参照系；再把人物身份（jobless 30-something）与情节动机（out of desperation）串联在同一个名词短语和一个定语从句里，信息密度高又不冗长。star as 是影视报道里的固定说法，意为「主演、饰演」。定语从句用一般现在时，是因为叙述的是剧情设定而非已发生的事实。

background.title: 《鱿鱼游戏》与韩国「生存游戏」题材
background.text_zh: 《鱿鱼游戏》（Squid Game）是 2021 年 Netflix 推出的韩剧，讲述负债累累的普通人被诱导参加一场以生命为赌注的儿童游戏竞赛，最终只有一人能活下来拿走巨额奖金。该剧在全球爆红后，成为此类「走投无路的人被卷入残酷游戏」的叙事代名词，英语媒体常用「Squid Game-like」一词快速描述同类作品。需要注意的是，这只是记者给出的类比，用来帮助读者定位类型，并非说两部作品有剧情关联。

background.title: Lee Jae-wook（李宰旭）
background.text_zh: 李宰旭是韩国新生代男演员，1998 年出生，曾出演《还魂》《死期将至》等剧，以冷峻气质和奇幻、动作类角色为人熟知。英语外刊在提到亚洲演员时通常直接使用罗马字姓名，不加解释，读者若不了解其作品背景，容易低估这条选角信息的新闻价值。

title_en: ‘Apologies for any confusion!’: how to write the perfect passive-aggressive email
excerpt_en: In a survey, ‘just to be clear’ came out as the most loathed phrase. But I think I can do better
body_en: A new contender for the most passive-aggressive email phrase has emerged. “Just to be clear” was chosen by 52% of desk jockeys in a survey by email verification company ZeroBounce, closely followed by the perennial pass-ag fave, “per my last email” (40%), which tied with the identical-in-intent “as previously discussed”. Further down the list came “for future reference” and “kindly note”.

If you ask me, these all verge on actual aggressive. Imagine saying “just to be clear” out loud to another person: that’s a conversational poke in the ribs, isn’t it? It’s the kind of thing you unleash 10 minutes into an ill-tempered wrangle with your home insurance company about inflated renewal premiums. “Kindly note” is even worse – it’s a phrase from an angry message on the office kitchen wall about microwave abuse.

No, we can do better than that, or at least I – a person whose own spouse frequently describes her as unpleasantly passive-aggressive – can. Let me explain: an exchange of professional passive-aggressive emails is a ritual as intricately coded as a Belle Epoque duel and it demands the appearance of great politeness. Your message needs to read, on its surface, as exquisitely helpful and friendly, while leaving every cc and bcc on the thread in no doubt as to it what it really is: an epistolary shanking.

A good pass-agg email starts with a simulacrum of warmth and gratitude. I can usually generate the appearance of warmth by harnessing the dizzying rush of anger generated by whatever stupid message has prompted me to press “reply all”. “Hi X!” I usually start perkily, then I pause to hold up both middle fingers to the screen. Next comes gratitude: “Great to hear from you,” (it wasn’t) “and thank you so much for your message”. Thanks, that is, for giving me a chance to show everyone you’re out of line. I say “everyone”, because I like to deploy a cc on this kind of email.
I follow this Trojan Shetland pony of an intro with a selection of my preferred zingers:
“My understanding was … apologies if this was incorrect?”
I understood perfectly. I am correct. I am sorry for nothing. The question mark is a mere disingenuous flourish.

The import of this little phrase is clear: I have kept the receipts and I want you to know that. This email will be followed near-instantaneously by a second email, forwarding the evidence that I am right. The body of that second email will just read “FYI”, which is passive-aggressive for “checkmate, loser”.
“ Apologies for any confusion” or “apologies if this was unclear”
It, and I, was entirely clear. I am only sorry you are a dolt. Some pass-ag practitioners drop in a bland, smiling emoji here, but I am a purist.
I hope this leaves you seething with the same fury your message inspired in me.
By saying I don’t expect you to respond it will make you look petty when you do; it also subtly implies you’ve already gone home. Your move.

Still, as much as I get satisfaction from the perfect turn of passive-aggressive phrase, I always realise later that it’s a hollow pleasure. What am I doing fighting, albeit with elegant restraint, a fellow worker when the real enemy is capitalism? Why are we emailing at all when we could be contemplating the beauty of a sunset, shoulder to shoulder? For future reference: I think we’d all be happier taking a deep breath, pressing backspace, and walking away.

enrich.title_zh: “如有混淆，敬请见谅！”：如何写出完美的消极对抗式邮件
enrich.summary_zh: 邮件验证公司 ZeroBounce 的一项调查评出了职场最“消极对抗”的邮件用语，“Just to be clear”居首，“per my last email”紧随其后。作者认为这些说法其实已近于直接攻击，真正高级的消极对抗邮件应当表面礼貌热情、实则字字带刺：先来一段虚假的问候与感谢，再抛出“我的理解是……如有出入请见谅”之类的句式，抄送一圈人，随后补发证据邮件。不过作者最后承认，这种胜利是空洞的——真正的敌人是资本主义，不如深呼吸、按下退格键走开。

paragraphs.en: A new contender for the most passive-aggressive email phrase has emerged. “Just to be clear” was chosen by 52% of desk jockeys in a survey by email verification company ZeroBounce, closely followed by the perennial pass-ag fave, “per my last email” (40%), which tied with the identical-in-intent “as previously discussed”. Further down the list came “for future reference” and “kindly note”.
paragraphs.zh: 最具“消极对抗”色彩（passive-aggressive）的邮件用语出现了新的竞争者。在邮件验证公司 ZeroBounce 的一项调查中，52% 的办公室白领把票投给了“Just to be clear（先把话说清楚）”，紧随其后的是常年霸榜的消极对抗式最爱——“per my last email（如我上一封邮件所述）”（40%），它与意思如出一辙的“as previously discussed（如前所述）”并列。再往下排是“for future reference（供日后参考）”和“kindly note（敬请知悉）”。

paragraphs.en: If you ask me, these all verge on actual aggressive. Imagine saying “just to be clear” out loud to another person: that’s a conversational poke in the ribs, isn’t it? It’s the kind of thing you unleash 10 minutes into an ill-tempered wrangle with your home insurance company about inflated renewal premiums. “Kindly note” is even worse – it’s a phrase from an angry message on the office kitchen wall about microwave abuse.
paragraphs.zh: 要我说，这些话已经接近于真正的攻击了。你不妨想象一下，当着别人的面说出一句“先把话说清楚”——那简直是谈话里往人肋骨上捅一肘子，不是吗？这种话，是你在跟家庭保险公司为虚高的续保保费吵了十分钟、火气上来时才会甩出去的。“Kindly note”更糟——那是贴在办公室茶水间墙上、控诉有人滥用微波炉的愤怒告示才会用的措辞。

paragraphs.en: No, we can do better than that, or at least I – a person whose own spouse frequently describes her as unpleasantly passive-aggressive – can. Let me explain: an exchange of professional passive-aggressive emails is a ritual as intricately coded as a Belle Epoque duel and it demands the appearance of great politeness. Your message needs to read, on its surface, as exquisitely helpful and friendly, while leaving every cc and bcc on the thread in no doubt as to it what it really is: an epistolary shanking.
paragraphs.zh: 不，我们完全可以做得比这更高明——至少我这个人可以，我自己的配偶就常说我“消极对抗得让人难受”。让我解释一下：职场里一来一往的消极对抗邮件，是一套编码极其繁复的仪式，精细程度不亚于“美好年代”的一场决斗，而它要求你摆出十足礼貌的样子。你的邮件表面上必须读起来极其体贴、极其友好，同时又要让抄送（cc）和密送（bcc）在这串邮件里的每一个人都毫不怀疑它到底是什么：一记书信里的捅刀。

paragraphs.en: A good pass-agg email starts with a simulacrum of warmth and gratitude. I can usually generate the appearance of warmth by harnessing the dizzying rush of anger generated by whatever stupid message has prompted me to press “reply all”. “Hi X!” I usually start perkily, then I pause to hold up both middle fingers to the screen. Next comes gratitude: “Great to hear from you,” (it wasn’t) “and thank you so much for your message”. Thanks, that is, for giving me a chance to show everyone you’re out of line. I say “everyone”, because I like to deploy a cc on this kind of email.
paragraphs.zh: 一封好的消极对抗邮件，开头是一份温暖与感激的仿制品。我通常能凭空制造出温暖的样子——办法是利用那股令人眩晕的怒火，它来自那封让我按下“回复全部”的蠢邮件。“嗨，某某！”我通常轻快地这样开头，然后停下来冲屏幕竖起双手中指。接下来是感谢：“很高兴收到你的来信”（才没有），“非常感谢你的邮件”。所谓感谢，是谢谢你给了我一个机会，让所有人都看到你有多不像话。我说“所有人”，是因为这种邮件我总喜欢抄送一圈。

paragraphs.en: I follow this Trojan Shetland pony of an intro with a selection of my preferred zingers:
paragraphs.zh: 在这场“特洛伊设得兰矮种马”式的开场白之后，我会挑几句我最爱的扎心话接上去：

paragraphs.en: “My understanding was … apologies if this was incorrect?”
paragraphs.zh: “我的理解是……如有理解错误，我在此致歉？”

paragraphs.en: I understood perfectly. I am correct. I am sorry for nothing. The question mark is a mere disingenuous flourish.
paragraphs.zh: 我理解得完全正确。我是对的。我没有任何需要抱歉的。那个问号不过是装傻式的花边装饰。

paragraphs.en: The import of this little phrase is clear: I have kept the receipts and I want you to know that. This email will be followed near-instantaneously by a second email, forwarding the evidence that I am right. The body of that second email will just read “FYI”, which is passive-aggressive for “checkmate, loser”.
paragraphs.zh: 这句小话的用意很清楚：我留着证据，而且我要让你知道这一点。这封邮件发出后几乎立刻会有第二封跟上来，转发能证明我是对的材料。第二封邮件的正文只写两个字：“FYI（供参考）”——在消极对抗的词典里，它的意思是“将死了，输家”。

paragraphs.en: “ Apologies for any confusion” or “apologies if this was unclear”
paragraphs.zh: “如有任何混淆，敬请见谅”，或“如有不清楚之处，我深表歉意”。

paragraphs.en: It, and I, was entirely clear. I am only sorry you are a dolt. Some pass-ag practitioners drop in a bland, smiling emoji here, but I am a purist.
paragraphs.zh: 那件事、还有我，都清楚得不能再清楚。我唯一感到抱歉的是你是个笨蛋。有些消极对抗的练习者会在这里塞一个平淡的笑脸表情，但我是纯粹主义者。

paragraphs.en: I hope this leaves you seething with the same fury your message inspired in me.
paragraphs.zh: 我希望这封邮件让你怒火中烧，正如你的邮件在我心里点燃的那把火。

paragraphs.en: By saying I don’t expect you to respond it will make you look petty when you do; it also subtly implies you’ve already gone home. Your move.
paragraphs.zh: 说出“我不指望你回复”，会让你一旦真的回复就显得小气；它还隐约暗示你已经下班回家了。该你走了。

paragraphs.en: Still, as much as I get satisfaction from the perfect turn of passive-aggressive phrase, I always realise later that it’s a hollow pleasure. What am I doing fighting, albeit with elegant restraint, a fellow worker when the real enemy is capitalism? Why are we emailing at all when we could be contemplating the beauty of a sunset, shoulder to shoulder? For future reference: I think we’d all be happier taking a deep breath, pressing backspace, and walking away.
paragraphs.zh: 不过，尽管一句完美的消极对抗措辞能让我很有快感，我事后总会意识到那是一种空洞的快乐。真正的敌人是资本主义，我为什么要跟同为打工人的人斗——哪怕斗得姿态优雅、克制有度？我们本可以并肩而立，静静欣赏日落之美，为什么还要发这些邮件？供日后参考：我觉得我们都深呼吸一下、按下退格键、转身走开，会快乐得多。

vocab.meaning_zh: 接近于，近乎（某种通常不好的性质）

sentences.en: Your message needs to read, on its surface, as exquisitely helpful and friendly, while leaving every cc and bcc on the thread in no doubt as to it what it really is: an epistolary shanking.
sentences.structure: 主干：Your message needs to read as helpful and friendly（主 + 系动词 + 表语）。修饰：on its surface 为插入语，限定“表面上”；while leaving... 为现在分词短语作伴随/对比状语；leave sb in no doubt as to sth 是固定搭配“使某人对某事确信无疑”；冒号后 an epistolary shanking 是对 what it really is 的解释。
sentences.analysis_zh: 这句话是全篇的“方法论”核心：一个句子同时装下“表里两层”。read as 是“读起来像是”，on its surface 提前插入，先把“表面”钉死；while 引导的分词状语则把“实质”推出来，形成表面对照。leave ... in no doubt as to 这种双重否定式表达（不留任何怀疑余地）比 tell everyone clearly 更含蓄、也更符合本文讽刺的语气。冒号收尾干脆利落，用一个名词短语完成“揭示”，这正是外刊常见的“冒号 punchline”写法。注意原文 as to it what 有笔误，规范写法是 as to what it really is。

sentences.en: I can usually generate the appearance of warmth by harnessing the dizzying rush of anger generated by whatever stupid message has prompted me to press “reply all”.
sentences.structure: 主干：I can generate the appearance of warmth。修饰：by harnessing ... 为方式状语；generated by ... 为过去分词短语后置修饰 anger；whatever stupid message has prompted me ... 是 by 的宾语从句，其中 whatever stupid message 作从句主语。
sentences.analysis_zh: 句子用了三层“套娃”：主句（制造温暖）→ 方式（利用怒火）→ 怒火来源（那封蠢邮件）。generate ... by harnessing ... generated by ... 三个同源动词层层递进，读起来像一条因果链，最后落在口语化的 press “reply all” 上，反差制造笑点。dizzying rush 把愤怒写成生理性的上涌感，比 very angry 具体得多。whatever 引导名词性从句表“无论哪一封……”，暗含“这种事经常发生”。

sentences.en: Still, as much as I get satisfaction from the perfect turn of passive-aggressive phrase, I always realise later that it’s a hollow pleasure.
sentences.structure: 主干：I always realise that it's a hollow pleasure（that 引导宾语从句）。修饰：as much as ... 引导让步状语从句，意为“尽管、虽然”（= although），置于句首；from the perfect turn of ... 为介词短语修饰 satisfaction。
sentences.analysis_zh: as much as 在这里不是比较“和……一样多”，而是让步连词，相当于 although，是外刊高频的书面表达，值得记住。the perfect turn of phrase 中 turn 是“措辞、说法”，turn of phrase 为固定搭配。前半句给足自我满足，后半句用 hollow 一词反转，later 又暗示这种醒悟总是迟到——一句话把整篇文章从“教你使坏”扭向自嘲与反思。

background.title: ZeroBounce 是什么公司
background.text_zh: ZeroBounce 是一家提供邮件地址验证与送达率（email deliverability）服务的美国公司，主要帮企业清洗营销名单、剔除无效和风险邮箱。这类公司做“职场邮件用语”问卷调查，本质上是一种内容营销：调查结论轻松、易传播，媒体也乐于引用，因此常被写成“研究显示……”的新闻。文中 52%、40% 等数字均出自该调查，样本与统计方法文章并未交代，阅读时宜把它当作谈资而非严谨研究。

background.title: “消极对抗”与英美职场邮件政治
background.text_zh: passive-aggressive（消极对抗／被动攻击）指不直接表达不满，而用拖延、冷处理、表面客气实则带刺的方式表达敌意。在英美职场里，邮件是这种文化的主要舞台：cc（抄送）意味着“让上级或相关方都看见”，bcc（密送）则是暗中留证；“reply all（回复全部）”常被视为施压手段；“per my last email”之所以刺人，是因为它暗示“你根本没看我之前写的”。文中提到的 Belle Epoque（美好年代，约 1871–1914 的法国）决斗，指的是那种讲究礼节、有见证人、按规矩行事却真会流血的荣誉之争——作者以此比喻邮件往来的繁复规矩与真实杀伤力。

title_en: Canada and EU announce new alliance open to like-minded countries
excerpt_en: Alliance for the Future, unveiled at Montreal summit and open to other countries, conceived for world ‘shaken by new storms’
body_en: Canada and Europe have announced a new alliance of like-minded nations to serve as both a “protective canopy under which our citizens can thrive” and a powerful hedge against the unpredictable nature of geopolitics, while welcoming other countries to join.

Speaking to reporters on Friday from Montreal, the prime minister, Mark Carney, and the European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen, called the new partnership the Alliance for the Future and said the “deepest possible partnership between Canada and the 27-member bloc had the potential to offer unprecedented stability and opportunity”.

“Our societies have been shaken by new storms,” Carney told reporters, referring to the damaging effects of the climate emergency but also the “erosion of democratic norms” and “the weaponization of trade”.

As they concluded their two-day summit, Canada agreed to contribute to a €90bn support loan for Ukraine. Leaders also said future discussions would lead to a more integrated market worth tens of billions of dollars, reduced trade and travel restrictions, and new educational opportunities for both sides.

While a trade war between Canada and the United States has seen Carney go hunting for new geopolitical partners, an over-reliance on American companies – especially for defence – has also given Canada pause.
Last week, Elon Musk throttled the speeds of Starlink and Starshield over Ukraine in mid-October, severely disrupting Ukrainian military and defense operations.

Carney has repeatedly raised the concern that Canada’s defense technologies could be at the whim of political actors or companies with opposing interests. Musk, a dual Canadian citizen, is a critic of Canada’s governing Liberal party and has advocated for provinces to separate.

Carney pointed to a planned merger between the Canadian artificial intelligence company Cohere Inc and Germany’s Aleph Alpha GmbH as a step to lessening reliance on American AI giants. The tie-up will see the newly formed company have dual headquarters in Berlin and Toronto, and Canada’s federal government has announced a stake in Cohere worth up to C$1.6bn.
“We are not waiting for the future of AI to be decided somewhere else by those we don’t know, or by whom we don’t trust,” Carney said on Thursday.
Brussels and Ottawa also announced an agreement on Friday that would bringing Canada into Europe’s supercomputing network, giving Canadian access to European machines to train AI models.

In addition to lofty promises of helping to reshape the global order, or giving safe harbour to like-minded nations looking to weather uncertainty, Canadian and EU leaders also pitched their new, deeper relationship as one that addressed key sources of anxiety for residents, including the cost of living.

“When trade becomes a tool of economic pressure, it’s the families that pay the price, from the supermarket shelf to the cost of a new car,” Von der Leyen said, noting that previously trusted suppliers of energy, critical minerals or semiconductors “are increasingly turned into instruments of pressure”.
“More competition, more choice,” Carney said earlier in the day, suggesting the alliance could find ways to build certainty around supply chains and “withstand shocks, together”.

The leaders once again brought up the prospect of Canada becoming an associate member. The designation is uncharted territory, said Von der Leyen, who added: “We have the ambition, trust, and creativity to shape it together.
“This [associate membership] is a partnership not against anyone else, but for our common strength.”

While the leaders committed to the idea of associate membership, they said a clearer scope of the role would come at a 2027 summit. Some EU members had bristled at the idea of Canada being given a legally meaningless designation that they fear confuses other nations looking for membership. Germany and other states had worked behind the scenes to remove the phrase from a draft of the summit statement. But Von der Leyen, who first floated the term, and Carney both again referred to “associate membership” at the summit.

European Council president Antonio Costa, meanwhile, said earlier that Canada was “by far the most European of the non-European countries”, a sentiment that reflected a belief that despite geography, there was a collective sense of shared values.
Costa said the two sides would pursue “the most closer, the most deepest, the most stronger association ever between European Union and a non-European country”.

Still, the mere fact of the summit has caused friction in the province of Quebec, where the separatist Parti Québécois was recently elected to a minority government. The premier, Paul St-Pierre Plamondon, skipped the event after Ottawa’s refusal to let him speak publicly at it.

“The federal government would have us believe that the premier of Quebec being granted permission to serve shrimp cocktails at a reception constitutes an acceptable and sufficient form of influence for representing Quebec’s interests,” St-Pierre Plamondon wrote in a social media post earlier in the week.

He said an invitation to sit at the head table was the federal government asking Quebec “to get back in line, with the vassalization and invisibilization of Quebec which that implies, in exchange for obtaining better seats to watch the party”.

enrich.title_zh: 加拿大与欧盟宣布组建新联盟，向志同道合国家开放
enrich.summary_zh: 加拿大与欧盟在蒙特利尔举行为期两天的峰会，宣布组建“未来联盟”，宣称要为志同道合的国家提供“保护伞”与抵御地缘政治不确定性的对冲手段。加拿大同意参与900亿欧元对乌贷款，并与欧洲在人工智能、超级计算和供应链上加深合作。双方还重提加拿大“准成员”身份，但该提法在欧盟内部引发争议，也在魁北克激起地方与联邦的摩擦。

paragraphs.en: Canada and Europe have announced a new alliance of like-minded nations to serve as both a “protective canopy under which our citizens can thrive” and a powerful hedge against the unpredictable nature of geopolitics, while welcoming other countries to join.
paragraphs.zh: 加拿大与欧洲宣布组建一个由志同道合国家构成的新联盟，它既是“庇护我们公民得以繁荣发展的保护伞”，也是对抗地缘政治不可预测性的有力对冲手段，同时欢迎其他国家加入。

paragraphs.en: Speaking to reporters on Friday from Montreal, the prime minister, Mark Carney, and the European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen, called the new partnership the Alliance for the Future and said the “deepest possible partnership between Canada and the 27-member bloc had the potential to offer unprecedented stability and opportunity”.
paragraphs.zh: 周五，加拿大总理马克·卡尼与欧盟委员会主席乌尔苏拉·冯德莱恩在蒙特利尔向记者发表讲话，将这一新伙伴关系称为“未来联盟”，并表示加拿大与这个拥有27个成员国的集团之间“尽可能深入的伙伴关系，有可能带来前所未有的稳定与机遇”。

paragraphs.en: “Our societies have been shaken by new storms,” Carney told reporters, referring to the damaging effects of the climate emergency but also the “erosion of democratic norms” and “the weaponization of trade”.
paragraphs.zh: “我们的社会已被新的风暴撼动，”卡尼对记者说，他指的是气候紧急状态造成的破坏性影响，也包括“民主规范的侵蚀”和“贸易的武器化”。

paragraphs.en: As they concluded their two-day summit, Canada agreed to contribute to a €90bn support loan for Ukraine. Leaders also said future discussions would lead to a more integrated market worth tens of billions of dollars, reduced trade and travel restrictions, and new educational opportunities for both sides.
paragraphs.zh: 在为为期两天的峰会收尾时，加拿大同意为一项900亿欧元的对乌克兰支持贷款出资。双方领导人还表示，未来的讨论将推动形成一个价值数百亿美元的更一体化市场、减少贸易与旅行限制，并为双方创造新的教育机会。

paragraphs.en: While a trade war between Canada and the United States has seen Carney go hunting for new geopolitical partners, an over-reliance on American companies – especially for defence – has also given Canada pause.
paragraphs.zh: 加美之间的贸易战促使卡尼四处寻找新的地缘政治伙伴；与此同时，对美国公司的过度依赖——尤其是在防务领域——也让加拿大有所警醒。

paragraphs.en: Last week, Elon Musk throttled the speeds of Starlink and Starshield over Ukraine in mid-October, severely disrupting Ukrainian military and defense operations.
paragraphs.zh: 上周有消息称，埃隆·马斯克在10月中旬下调了“星链”（Starlink）和“星盾”（Starshield）在乌克兰上空的服务速度，严重干扰了乌克兰的军事与防务行动。

paragraphs.en: Carney has repeatedly raised the concern that Canada’s defense technologies could be at the whim of political actors or companies with opposing interests. Musk, a dual Canadian citizen, is a critic of Canada’s governing Liberal party and has advocated for provinces to separate.
paragraphs.zh: 卡尼已多次表达担忧：加拿大的防务技术可能受制于利益相左的政治人物或公司的一时之意。拥有加拿大国籍（同时持有他国国籍）的马斯克是加拿大执政党自由党的批评者，并曾主张各省分离。

paragraphs.en: Carney pointed to a planned merger between the Canadian artificial intelligence company Cohere Inc and Germany’s Aleph Alpha GmbH as a step to lessening reliance on American AI giants. The tie-up will see the newly formed company have dual headquarters in Berlin and Toronto, and Canada’s federal government has announced a stake in Cohere worth up to C$1.6bn.
paragraphs.zh: 卡尼以加拿大人工智能公司Cohere Inc与德国Aleph Alpha GmbH计划合并为例，称此举是减少对美国AI巨头依赖的一步。合并后的新公司将在柏林和多伦多设立双总部，加拿大联邦政府已宣布入股Cohere，投资额最高达16亿加元。

paragraphs.en: “We are not waiting for the future of AI to be decided somewhere else by those we don’t know, or by whom we don’t trust,” Carney said on Thursday.
paragraphs.zh: “我们不会坐等人工智能的未来由我们所不了解、或不信任的人在其他地方决定，”卡尼周四说。

paragraphs.en: Brussels and Ottawa also announced an agreement on Friday that would bringing Canada into Europe’s supercomputing network, giving Canadian access to European machines to train AI models.
paragraphs.zh: 布鲁塞尔与渥太华周五还宣布达成一项协议，将加拿大纳入欧洲超级计算网络，使加方能够使用欧洲的机器训练人工智能模型。

paragraphs.en: In addition to lofty promises of helping to reshape the global order, or giving safe harbour to like-minded nations looking to weather uncertainty, Canadian and EU leaders also pitched their new, deeper relationship as one that addressed key sources of anxiety for residents, including the cost of living.
paragraphs.zh: 除了“帮助重塑全球秩序”“为寻求抵御不确定性的志同道合国家提供安全港湾”这类宏大承诺之外，加欧领导人还把这一更深入的新关系包装成能够回应民众主要焦虑——包括生活成本问题——的方案。

paragraphs.en: “When trade becomes a tool of economic pressure, it’s the families that pay the price, from the supermarket shelf to the cost of a new car,” Von der Leyen said, noting that previously trusted suppliers of energy, critical minerals or semiconductors “are increasingly turned into instruments of pressure”.
paragraphs.zh: “当贸易成为经济施压的工具时，付出代价的是普通家庭——从超市货架到一辆新车的价格，”冯德莱恩说。她指出，过去值得信赖的能源、关键矿产或半导体供应方“正日益变成施压的工具”。

paragraphs.en: “More competition, more choice,” Carney said earlier in the day, suggesting the alliance could find ways to build certainty around supply chains and “withstand shocks, together”.
paragraphs.zh: “更多竞争，更多选择，”卡尼当天早些时候说，并暗示该联盟可以设法为供应链构筑确定性，并“共同抵御冲击”。

paragraphs.en: The leaders once again brought up the prospect of Canada becoming an associate member. The designation is uncharted territory, said Von der Leyen, who added: “We have the ambition, trust, and creativity to shape it together.
paragraphs.zh: 两位领导人再次提到加拿大成为“准成员”（associate member）的可能性。冯德莱恩称这一名分属于前所未有的新领域，并补充说：“我们有雄心、信任和创造力共同塑造它。”

paragraphs.en: “This [associate membership] is a partnership not against anyone else, but for our common strength.”
paragraphs.zh: “这一（准成员身份）伙伴关系不针对任何其他方，而是为了我们的共同实力。”

paragraphs.en: While the leaders committed to the idea of associate membership, they said a clearer scope of the role would come at a 2027 summit. Some EU members had bristled at the idea of Canada being given a legally meaningless designation that they fear confuses other nations looking for membership. Germany and other states had worked behind the scenes to remove the phrase from a draft of the summit statement. But Von der Leyen, who first floated the term, and Carney both again referred to “associate membership” at the summit.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管领导人表态支持“准成员”的构想，但他们表示，这一身份更明确的范围将在2027年的峰会上确定。一些欧盟成员国曾对这一想法感到恼火，认为给加拿大一个在法律上毫无意义的称谓，可能会混淆其他正在寻求入盟的国家。德国等国曾在幕后推动，把这一表述从峰会声明草案中删去。但最早提出这一措辞的冯德莱恩和卡尼都在峰会上再次提到了“准成员身份”。

paragraphs.en: European Council president Antonio Costa, meanwhile, said earlier that Canada was “by far the most European of the non-European countries”, a sentiment that reflected a belief that despite geography, there was a collective sense of shared values.
paragraphs.zh: 欧洲理事会主席安东尼奥·科斯塔早些时候则表示，加拿大“是迄今为止最欧洲的非欧洲国家”。这一说法反映出一种信念：尽管地理上相隔遥远，双方仍有一种共同的价值观认同。

paragraphs.en: Costa said the two sides would pursue “the most closer, the most deepest, the most stronger association ever between European Union and a non-European country”.
paragraphs.zh: 科斯塔说，双方将追求“欧盟与非欧洲国家之间历来最紧密、最深入、最牢固的联系”。（原话存在语法错误，此处按其本意译出）

paragraphs.en: Still, the mere fact of the summit has caused friction in the province of Quebec, where the separatist Parti Québécois was recently elected to a minority government. The premier, Paul St-Pierre Plamondon, skipped the event after Ottawa’s refusal to let him speak publicly at it.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管如此，仅仅是这场峰会本身就在魁北克省引发了摩擦。主张分离主义的魁北克人党最近在该省赢得少数政府。由于渥太华拒绝让魁北克省长保罗·圣皮埃尔·普拉蒙东在会上公开发言，他缺席了此次活动。

paragraphs.en: “The federal government would have us believe that the premier of Quebec being granted permission to serve shrimp cocktails at a reception constitutes an acceptable and sufficient form of influence for representing Quebec’s interests,” St-Pierre Plamondon wrote in a social media post earlier in the week.
paragraphs.zh: 圣皮埃尔·普拉蒙东本周早些时候在社交媒体发帖写道：“联邦政府想让我们相信，准许魁北克省长在招待会上端虾仁鸡尾酒，就算是一种可接受且足以代表魁北克利益的影响力形式。”

paragraphs.en: He said an invitation to sit at the head table was the federal government asking Quebec “to get back in line, with the vassalization and invisibilization of Quebec which that implies, in exchange for obtaining better seats to watch the party”.
paragraphs.zh: 他说，邀请他坐上主桌，是联邦政府在要求魁北克“重新归队，而这隐含着魁北克的附庸化与隐形化，换来的只是观看这场派对时更好的座位”。

vocab.meaning_zh: 志同道合的、想法相近的；外刊谈结盟、集团政治时的高频词
vocab.example_en: The two countries formed a bloc of like-minded governments on climate policy.
vocab.example_zh: 两国在气候政策上结成了一个由立场相近政府组成的集团。

vocab.meaning_zh: 顶篷、华盖；（比喻义）起庇护作用的“保护伞”
vocab.example_en: The treaty was presented as a protective canopy over small economies.
vocab.example_zh: 该条约被描述为罩在小国经济头上的一把保护伞。

vocab.meaning_zh: （金融、政治语境）对冲、防范手段，用来降低风险的东西
vocab.example_en: Diversifying suppliers is a hedge against sudden export bans.
vocab.example_zh: 供应商多元化是应对突然出口禁令的一种对冲手段。

vocab.meaning_zh: 凭……的一时兴起、受……任意摆布
vocab.example_en: No country wants its defence systems at the whim of a single executive.
vocab.example_zh: 没有哪个国家愿意让自己的防务系统受某一个人的随意摆布。

vocab.meaning_zh: 对……感到恼火、反感而准备反击
vocab.example_en: Several member states bristled at the proposal to fast-track membership.
vocab.example_zh: 几个成员国对快速入盟的提议十分恼火。

vocab.meaning_zh: 提出（想法、方案）以试探反应，是“抛出一个说法”的常用表达
vocab.example_en: The commission first floated the idea in a closed-door meeting.
vocab.example_zh: 欧盟委员会最初是在一次闭门会议上抛出这个想法的。

vocab.meaning_zh: （企业间的）联合、合并、合作
vocab.example_en: The tie-up will create a rival to the big American AI firms.
vocab.example_zh: 这次合并将造就一个能与美国大型人工智能公司抗衡的对手。

vocab.meaning_zh: （官方给予的）称号、名分、身份认定
vocab.example_en: The designation carries no legal rights inside the bloc.
vocab.example_zh: 这一名分在该集团内部并不附带任何法定权利。

vocab.meaning_zh: （本义）调节油门；引申为限制速度、压制、卡住
vocab.example_en: The operator throttled bandwidth for the entire region.
vocab.example_zh: 运营商限制了整个地区的带宽。

vocab.meaning_zh: 附庸化，使一方沦为从属地位；魁北克独立派常用此词指控联邦政府
vocab.example_en: The premier denounced what he called the vassalization of the province.
vocab.example_zh: 省长谴责了他所谓的该省被附庸化。

sentences.en: Canada and Europe have announced a new alliance of like-minded nations to serve as both a “protective canopy under which our citizens can thrive” and a powerful hedge against the unpredictable nature of geopolitics, while welcoming other countries to join.
sentences.structure: 主干：Canada and Europe have announced a new alliance（主谓宾）。修饰：of like-minded nations 作定语后置说明联盟构成；to serve as both A and B 是目的/功能状语，说明联盟的定位；under which our citizens can thrive 为定语从句修饰 canopy；against... 修饰 hedge；while welcoming other countries to join 为现在分词短语，补充说明“同时对别国开放”。
sentences.analysis_zh: 全句只用一个主谓宾，其余全是“这个联盟是什么”的层层附加信息，这是外刊导语段常见的写法：先抛出事件，再一口气交代定性、定位与开放性。注意 both A and B 的 A、B 结构不对称——A 是带定语从句的隐喻名词短语，B 是“名词+介词短语”的抽象概念，中文直译容易失衡，所以译文把隐喻保留、把 hedge 转为“对冲手段”，并补出“既……也是……”来维持平衡。

sentences.en: In addition to lofty promises of helping to reshape the global order, or giving safe harbour to like-minded nations looking to weather uncertainty, Canadian and EU leaders also pitched their new, deeper relationship as one that addressed key sources of anxiety for residents, including the cost of living.
sentences.structure: 主干：Canadian and EU leaders also pitched their new, deeper relationship as one（主谓宾+宾补）。修饰：In addition to... 为句首介词短语作让步/递进状语；of helping to reshape... or giving safe harbour... 修饰 promises；looking to weather uncertainty 为现在分词作后置定语修饰 nations；that addressed key sources of anxiety... 为定语从句修饰 one（代指 relationship）；including the cost of living 补充说明 anxiety 的具体内容。
sentences.analysis_zh: 句子真正的主干被压到后半句，前半句用 In addition to 挂了一长串“宏大承诺”，形成“宏大叙事 vs 民生焦虑”的对照，这是记者刻意的修辞：先承认联盟的宏大话语，再点出它同样是安抚国内选民的工具。pitch A as B（把 A 包装成 B）是本句的语义核心，也带轻微贬义色彩；a source of anxiety for residents（对居民的焦虑来源）宜译作“民众的主要焦虑”，而非逐字译成“居民的焦虑来源”。

sentences.en: Some EU members had bristled at the idea of Canada being given a legally meaningless designation that they fear confuses other nations looking for membership.
sentences.structure: 主干：Some EU members had bristled at the idea（主谓+介词宾语）。修饰：of Canada being given a legally meaningless designation 为动名词复合结构作 idea 的同位说明；that they fear confuses other nations 为定语从句修饰 designation，其中 they fear 是插入式主谓，插在引导词 that 与谓语 confuses 之间；looking for membership 为现在分词作后置定语修饰 nations。
sentences.analysis_zh: 难点在 that they fear confuses：that 是定语从句的主语，confuses 是从句谓语，they fear 只是插入成分（“他们担心”），不是从句的主谓，别误读成“他们害怕 designation 会……”之外还有别的结构。另外 had bristled 用过去完成时，因为作者是在峰会（已发生）之后回述峰会前的反对，时态承担了“幕后的反对早于公开的团结”这层叙事功能：公开场合重申“准成员”，私下却删过文稿，反差正是本段的信息点。

background.title: “准成员”（associate membership）为什么敏感
background.text_zh: 欧盟条约体系里，对外关系的正式身份只有成员国的“加入”（accession）以及各类协定伙伴（联系国、战略伙伴等），“准成员”并非有法律定义的地位。它之所以被反复提起又不敢写死，是因为一旦给加拿大一个介于“伙伴”与“成员”之间的模糊名分，那些排队多年、把入盟写进国策的国家（如西巴尔干、乌克兰、摩尔多瓦、土耳其）就会质疑：欧盟的门槛是否被稀释。加拿大不需要接受欧盟法律、预算分摊和人员自由流动，却可能拿到政治象征上的“准入门槛内”，这是德国等国要求从草案中删句的现实原因。文本给出的时间表是2027年峰会再明确范围。

background.title: 魁北克独立运动与魁北克人党
background.text_zh: 魁北克是加拿大的法语省份，独立运动在20世纪后期达到高峰，魁北克人党（Parti Québécois，PQ）正是主张主权独立、以法语共同体认同为核心诉求的政党，曾在1980年和1995年两次推动公投（均告失败后，1995年那次以极微弱差距落败）。在加拿大联邦制下，省政府在外交上没有独立发言权，国际场合由渥太华代表，因此“省长能否在峰会公开发言”被视为联邦与省的权限之争，而不只是礼宾问题。文中省长用“端虾仁鸡尾酒”“主桌座位”这类礼节性待遇来嘲讽联邦政府的安排，正是把礼宾细节转化为主权象征的政治修辞。

title_en: Sinkholes, scarred land and scapegoats: the scourge of illegal gold mining in Johannesburg
excerpt_en: There is no end in sight for the drivers of illegal mining, while police action appears ineffective
body_en: Cora Bailey has been encountering illegal miners ever since she first started treating injured animals in the townships around Roodepoort, west of Johannesburg, in 1991. But as the price of gold has soared, so too has activity in the abandoned mine shafts that mark the area.

In late September, dozens of zama zamas – the name given to illegal miners in South Africa, meaning roughly “to take a chance” in Zulu – arrived to dig for gold across the dirt road from her charity, Claw (Community Led Animal Welfare).

Soon, they were taking water for their panning and processing from the organisation’s two 25,000-litre water tanks, which are filled irregularly by the city government for the 100 or so rescued and injured animals on site.

“We’ve asked them really nicely and haven’t ever refused them water to drink … But, for the first time ever, we closed the gate at 12 [midday], because we literally had about two buckets of water left,” Bailey said in mid-October.

Police told her that the scale of the illegal mining was too big for them to do anything about, she said at the time. About a week later, officers sheared away the grass that had partly hidden the zama zamas . But within a few days a smaller group had returned, although Bailey said they were now taking Claw’s water only for drinking.
South Africa’s police regularly trumpet their success in tackling illegal mining. On 19 October, they said they had arrested 71 suspected zama zamas across the country in the previous week.

However, researchers put the number of illegal miners in the tens of thousands. In 2019, Marcena Hunter, a researcher at the Global Initiative against Transnational Organised Crime, estimated that a tenth of South Africa’s gold production , worth about $1bn, was being exported illegally .
Police operations have also led to tragedy. In 2025, 93 bodies were pulled from a mine shaft in Stilfontein , after officers blocked food and water from being delivered underground.

Meanwhile, there is no end in sight to the dynamics driving illegal mining, including the high price of gold, poverty, unemployment, corrupt politicians and police profiting, and the failure of mining companies to fulfil their legal obligation to seal mining shafts when they cease operating.

South Africa’s modern history is tied to mining. In 1884, gold was found on a farm, sparking a gold rush that led to the creation of Johannesburg. Gold production peaked in the 1970s , but South Africa was the world’s largest producer, a title it held for more than a century, until 2007.

In 2009, Morris Viljoen, a geology professor at the University of the Witwatersrand, estimated that the reef that gave the university its name had produced more than a third of the gold ever mined globally. Claw is housed in the old offices of the Durban Deep mine, which shut at the turn of the century, having once lent its name to an Elton John song .
The city government claims there is still 40,000 tonnes of gold underground in the region. But, with the remainder lying ever deeper, the costs of recovering it have risen.

Mining companies are supposed to seal up old mine shafts and rehabilitate the environment around them. However, in 2025 there were “6,100 derelict and ownerless mines and 1,170 unsafe mine openings”, the mining minister, Gwede Mantashe, said in response to a parliamentary question.

Zama zamas have stepped into those voids left in the earth. While there is no comprehensive data on them, experts agree that a majority are from neighbouring countries, principally Lesotho, Mozambique and Zimbabwe.
The skyline south of Johannesburg is punctuated by the pale yellow ridges of mine dumps. Increasingly, the ground is also caving open.

For politicians seeking votes in local elections on 4 November, the culprit is clear: illegal miners. In May, Kenny Kunene, the Johannesburg council member responsible for transport, took journalists on a tour of sinkholes that he claimed were the fault of zama zamas , including a section of Wemmer Pan Road that had completely collapsed .

The road was once the main artery linking the city’s central business district to the south-eastern suburbs. In one section it has completely disappeared, now raw earth pitted with the holes where illegal miners have been digging.
However, when it comes to sinkholes, experts say zama zamas are being scapegoated.

Rosalind Morris, an anthropology professor at Columbia University, who has worked extensively with illegal miners, noted that the porous dolomitic rock to Johannesburg’s south and west becomes unstable when water is removed.
“The biggest culprit of sinkholes in South Africa is formal industrial mining, which dewaters at a scale of hundreds of millions of gallons of water removed from underground every day,” she said.

“There are areas where there is a lot of residual gold, which are being very intensely mined by zama zamas , and some of that definitely causes structural collapse, there’s no doubt about it. But the idea that this was invented or caused for the first time by zama zamas is completely fallacious.”

Zama zamas are also frequently blamed for violence in mining areas, including a September mass shooting in Wedela township, west of Johannesburg. However, David van Wyk, the lead researcher at Bench Marks Foundation, said culpability laid with the often-feuding gangs that controlled access to the shafts.

enrich.title_zh: 塌陷、疮痍与替罪羊：约翰内斯堡非法采金的祸患

paragraphs.en: Cora Bailey has been encountering illegal miners ever since she first started treating injured animals in the townships around Roodepoort, west of Johannesburg, in 1991. But as the price of gold has soared, so too has activity in the abandoned mine shafts that mark the area.
paragraphs.zh: 科拉·贝利（Cora Bailey）自1991年开始在约翰内斯堡以西鲁德普特（Roodepoort）周边乡镇救治受伤动物以来，就一直与非法采矿者打交道。但随着金价飙升，遍布该地区的废弃矿井里的活动也愈发猖獗。

paragraphs.en: In late September, dozens of zama zamas – the name given to illegal miners in South Africa, meaning roughly “to take a chance” in Zulu – arrived to dig for gold across the dirt road from her charity, Claw (Community Led Animal Welfare).
paragraphs.zh: 9月下旬，数十名“扎马扎马”（zama zama，南非对非法采矿者的称呼，在祖鲁语中大致意为“赌一把”）来到她所创办的慈善机构 Claw（社区主导动物福利组织）对面的土路上挖金。

paragraphs.en: Soon, they were taking water for their panning and processing from the organisation’s two 25,000-litre water tanks, which are filled irregularly by the city government for the 100 or so rescued and injured animals on site.
paragraphs.zh: 很快，他们开始从该机构两个容量2.5万升的水箱里取水，用于淘洗和加工矿石。这两个水箱由市政府不定期注水，供现场约100只获救和受伤的动物饮用。

paragraphs.en: “We’ve asked them really nicely and haven’t ever refused them water to drink … But, for the first time ever, we closed the gate at 12 [midday], because we literally had about two buckets of water left,” Bailey said in mid-October.
paragraphs.zh: “我们好言相劝，也从未拒绝给他们饮用水……但这是头一回，我们中午12点就关上了大门，因为我们真的只剩大约两桶水了，”贝利在10月中旬说。

paragraphs.en: Police told her that the scale of the illegal mining was too big for them to do anything about, she said at the time. About a week later, officers sheared away the grass that had partly hidden the zama zamas . But within a few days a smaller group had returned, although Bailey said they were now taking Claw’s water only for drinking.
paragraphs.zh: 她说，当时警方告诉她，非法采矿的规模太大，他们无能为力。大约一周后，警员割掉了部分遮挡扎马扎马的草丛。但没过几天，一小群人又回来了——不过贝利说，他们现在只取 Claw 的水用于饮用。

paragraphs.en: South Africa’s police regularly trumpet their success in tackling illegal mining. On 19 October, they said they had arrested 71 suspected zama zamas across the country in the previous week.
paragraphs.zh: 南非警方经常大肆宣扬自己在打击非法采矿方面的成果。10月19日，他们表示，此前一周已在全国逮捕了71名扎马扎马嫌疑人。

paragraphs.en: However, researchers put the number of illegal miners in the tens of thousands. In 2019, Marcena Hunter, a researcher at the Global Initiative against Transnational Organised Crime, estimated that a tenth of South Africa’s gold production , worth about $1bn, was being exported illegally .
paragraphs.zh: 然而，研究者估计非法采矿者数以万计。2019年，“打击跨国有组织犯罪全球倡议”的研究员马塞娜·亨特（Marcena Hunter）估计，南非黄金产量的十分之一——价值约10亿美元——正被非法出口。

paragraphs.en: Police operations have also led to tragedy. In 2025, 93 bodies were pulled from a mine shaft in Stilfontein , after officers blocked food and water from being delivered underground.
paragraphs.zh: 警方的行动也酿成了悲剧。2025年，在斯蒂尔方丹（Stilfontein），93具遗体从一处矿井中被运出，此前警方阻止了食物和饮水送入井下。

paragraphs.en: Meanwhile, there is no end in sight to the dynamics driving illegal mining, including the high price of gold, poverty, unemployment, corrupt politicians and police profiting, and the failure of mining companies to fulfil their legal obligation to seal mining shafts when they cease operating.
paragraphs.zh: 与此同时，推动非法采矿的各种因素短期内看不到尽头：高企的金价、贫困、失业、腐败政客与警察从中获利，以及矿业公司在停止运营后未能履行封堵矿井的法律义务。

paragraphs.en: South Africa’s modern history is tied to mining. In 1884, gold was found on a farm, sparking a gold rush that led to the creation of Johannesburg. Gold production peaked in the 1970s , but South Africa was the world’s largest producer, a title it held for more than a century, until 2007.
paragraphs.zh: 南非的现代史与矿业密不可分。1884年，一座农场里发现了黄金，由此引发的淘金热催生了约翰内斯堡。黄金产量在20世纪70年代达到顶峰，但南非曾是世界最大产金国，这一头衔保持了一个多世纪，直到2007年。

paragraphs.en: In 2009, Morris Viljoen, a geology professor at the University of the Witwatersrand, estimated that the reef that gave the university its name had produced more than a third of the gold ever mined globally. Claw is housed in the old offices of the Durban Deep mine, which shut at the turn of the century, having once lent its name to an Elton John song .
paragraphs.zh: 2009年，金山大学（威特沃特斯兰德大学，University of the Witwatersrand）地质学教授莫里斯·维尔容（Morris Viljoen）估计，这所大学因其得名的那条矿脉，曾产出人类有史以来开采出的黄金总量的三分之一以上。Claw 的办公地点就设在杜班迪普（Durban Deep）矿的旧办公楼里；该矿于世纪之交关闭，其名字曾被埃尔顿·约翰用作一首歌的歌名。

paragraphs.en: The city government claims there is still 40,000 tonnes of gold underground in the region. But, with the remainder lying ever deeper, the costs of recovering it have risen.
paragraphs.zh: 市政府声称，该地区地下仍有4万吨黄金。但随着剩余矿藏埋藏得越来越深，开采成本也水涨船高。

paragraphs.en: Mining companies are supposed to seal up old mine shafts and rehabilitate the environment around them. However, in 2025 there were “6,100 derelict and ownerless mines and 1,170 unsafe mine openings”, the mining minister, Gwede Mantashe, said in response to a parliamentary question.
paragraphs.zh: 矿业公司本应封堵旧矿井并修复周边环境。然而，矿业部长格韦德·曼塔谢（Gwede Mantashe）在回答议会质询时表示，2025年南非有“6100座废弃无主矿山和1170处不安全的矿井开口”。

paragraphs.en: Zama zamas have stepped into those voids left in the earth. While there is no comprehensive data on them, experts agree that a majority are from neighbouring countries, principally Lesotho, Mozambique and Zimbabwe.
paragraphs.zh: 扎马扎马正是钻进了这些留在地下的空洞。虽然关于他们没有全面的数据，但专家们一致认为，其中大多数来自邻国，主要是莱索托、莫桑比克和津巴布韦。

paragraphs.en: The skyline south of Johannesburg is punctuated by the pale yellow ridges of mine dumps. Increasingly, the ground is also caving open.
paragraphs.zh: 约翰内斯堡南部的天际线上，点缀着一道道淡黄色的矿渣堆。而地面也越来越多地塌陷开裂。

paragraphs.en: For politicians seeking votes in local elections on 4 November, the culprit is clear: illegal miners. In May, Kenny Kunene, the Johannesburg council member responsible for transport, took journalists on a tour of sinkholes that he claimed were the fault of zama zamas , including a section of Wemmer Pan Road that had completely collapsed .
paragraphs.zh: 对于想在11月4日地方选举中拉票的政客来说，罪魁祸首一目了然：非法采矿者。今年5月，约翰内斯堡市议会负责交通的委员肯尼·库内内（Kenny Kunene）带记者们参观了几处地陷，声称这些都是扎马扎马造成的，其中包括韦默潘路（Wemmer Pan Road）一段完全垮塌的路面。

paragraphs.en: The road was once the main artery linking the city’s central business district to the south-eastern suburbs. In one section it has completely disappeared, now raw earth pitted with the holes where illegal miners have been digging.
paragraphs.zh: 这条路曾是连接该市中央商务区与东南郊的主要干道。其中一段已彻底消失，如今只剩裸露的泥土，上面布满非法采矿者挖掘留下的坑洞。

paragraphs.en: However, when it comes to sinkholes, experts say zama zamas are being scapegoated.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，专家表示，就地陷而言，扎马扎马正在被当成替罪羊。

paragraphs.en: Rosalind Morris, an anthropology professor at Columbia University, who has worked extensively with illegal miners, noted that the porous dolomitic rock to Johannesburg’s south and west becomes unstable when water is removed.
paragraphs.zh: 哥伦比亚大学人类学教授罗莎琳德·莫里斯（Rosalind Morris）长期与非法采矿者打交道，她指出，约翰内斯堡南部和西部的多孔白云岩一旦失水就会变得不稳定。

paragraphs.en: “The biggest culprit of sinkholes in South Africa is formal industrial mining, which dewaters at a scale of hundreds of millions of gallons of water removed from underground every day,” she said.
paragraphs.zh: “南非地陷的最大元凶是正规的工业化采矿，它们每天从地下抽走数亿加仑的水，抽排规模极其巨大，”她说。

paragraphs.en: “There are areas where there is a lot of residual gold, which are being very intensely mined by zama zamas , and some of that definitely causes structural collapse, there’s no doubt about it. But the idea that this was invented or caused for the first time by zama zamas is completely fallacious.”
paragraphs.zh: “确实有一些地区残留大量黄金，正被扎马扎马高强度地开采，其中一些活动无疑会造成结构坍塌，这一点毫无疑问。但认为地陷是扎马扎马首创或首次造成的，这种说法完全是谬误。”

paragraphs.en: Zama zamas are also frequently blamed for violence in mining areas, including a September mass shooting in Wedela township, west of Johannesburg. However, David van Wyk, the lead researcher at Bench Marks Foundation, said culpability laid with the often-feuding gangs that controlled access to the shafts.
paragraphs.zh: 扎马扎马也常常被指责要为矿区的暴力事件负责，包括9月约翰内斯堡以西韦德拉（Wedela）镇发生的一起大规模枪击案。但基准标记基金会（Bench Marks Foundation）首席研究员戴维·范维克（David van Wyk）表示，罪责在于那些经常火并、控制矿井通道的帮派。
