sentences.en: But as the price of gold has soared, so too has activity in the abandoned mine shafts that mark the area.
sentences.structure: 主干：activity … has soared（主谓）。让步/伴随：as the price of gold has soared（as 引导时间—原因状语从句）；倒装：so too has activity（“so + 助动词 + 主语”表示“后者也一样”）；定语：that mark the area 修饰 the abandoned mine shafts。
sentences.analysis_zh: 正常语序是 activity in the abandoned mine shafts has soared too。作者用 so too has… 把 activity 这个长主语后置，让前面的 as 从句和后面的 soared 形成首尾呼应，节奏更紧、书面感更强。that mark the area 是“使这一地区具有特征”的定语从句，比 which are in the area 更有画面感。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, there is no end in sight to the dynamics driving illegal mining, including the high price of gold, poverty, unemployment, corrupt politicians and police profiting, and the failure of mining companies to fulfil their legal obligation to seal mining shafts when they cease operating.
sentences.structure: 主干：there is no end in sight to the dynamics（there be 句型；no end in sight to sth 为固定表达）。修饰：driving illegal mining 为现在分词短语后置修饰 dynamics；including … 列举五个并列成分；the failure of mining companies to fulfil their legal obligation 中 of 短语与不定式分别限定 failure；to seal … 修饰 obligation；when they cease operating 为时间状语从句。
sentences.analysis_zh: 这是典型的英文外刊“清单式长句”：先用一个抽象名词 dynamics 概括，再用 including 引出五项具体动因，最后一项故意写得最长最重，把“矿企不封井”这一制度性责任压在句尾，形成强调。翻译时中文宜拆成“包括……以及……”，并保持列举的平行。

sentences.en: But the idea that this was invented or caused for the first time by zama zamas is completely fallacious.
sentences.structure: 主干：the idea … is completely fallacious（主系表）。同位语从句：that this was invented or caused for the first time by zama zamas，解释 idea 的具体内容；从句内部为被动语态，by zama zamas 是施动者，for the first time 作状语。
sentences.analysis_zh: 英文常用 the idea that… / the claim that… / the fact that… 这类“抽象名词+同位语从句”的结构来转述他人观点，然后加以评价（is completely fallacious）。中文更习惯说“认为……的说法完全是谬误”，把 that 从句提前译成“说法”的定语。注意 invented 与 caused 并列，用“发明”一词略带讽刺，暗指把地陷说成是非法矿工凭空造出来的。

background.title: 威特沃特斯兰德金矿带与约翰内斯堡的兴衰
background.text_zh: 约翰内斯堡并非因河流或港口而生，而是1886年前后在威特沃特斯兰德（Witwatersrand，意为“白色水域之脊”）发现金矿后，由矿工营地迅速膨胀成的城市。这条金矿带在20世纪长期支撑南非成为全球头号产金国。金矿越挖越深后，开采成本上升，大型矿业公司在20世纪末陆续关停或出售矿井，留下大量未妥善封闭的竖井、斜井与地下巷道，以及高耸的黄色矿渣堆。南非的“废弃无主矿山”问题正源于此：原业主消失或破产，政府缺乏资金全面封堵，这些地下空间便成了非法采矿者的入口。

background.title: 白云岩地质与“天坑”的真正成因
background.text_zh: 约翰内斯堡南部和西部地表下是厚层的白云岩（dolomite）。这类碳酸盐岩易被地下水溶解，形成溶洞和裂隙，本身就像一块多孔的“海绵”。当矿井排水或城市大量抽取地下水时，地下水位下降，原本支撑溶洞的水压消失，上覆土层失去支撑便会突然塌落，形成 sinkhole（地陷、天坑）。因此地质学界普遍认为，南非地陷的主因是工业化采矿的长期大规模抽排地下水，而非小规模手工挖掘——这也解释了文中专家为何认为把地陷归咎于非法矿工是找错了对象。

title_en: Sudanese diaspora and human rights groups denounce UAE nominee for UN top job
excerpt_en: Critics cite Lana Nusseibeh’s denial of accusations the UAE is fuelling Sudan war by supporting paramilitary RSF
body_en: Members of the Sudanese diaspora and international human rights monitors have denounced the candidature of an Emirati diplomat for the top job at the UN, citing her denial of accusations that the United Arab Emirates is fuelling the war in Sudan by supporting the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces.
The UAE nominated Lana Nusseibeh last week to replace the UN secretary general, António Guterres, as he finishes his second five-year term ⁠this year, upending a race that had become gridlocked.

Rights groups and others have for years documented evidence of UAE support for the RSF, which has been accused of atrocities during the course of its war against the Sudanese army, including an attack on the city of El Fasher in October 2025 that the UN said had “hallmarks of genocide” .
Nusseibeh, the UAE’s representative to the UN until 2024, has repeatedly reflected the UAE’s blanket denials of the accusations.

The Sudanese pro-democracy and women’s rights activist Hala al-Karib, the regional director of the Strategic Initiative for Women in the Horn of Africa, said Nusseibeh had “no track record of acting independently of her country’s role in Sudan” and that endorsement by the security council would amount “essentially [to] a denial of the genocidal acts committed in El Fasher by the RSF”.
There was also strong criticism of Nusseibeh’s candidature at a virtual briefing by the Avaaz human rights advocacy group on Tuesday.

Ibrahim Alduma, who grew up in El Fasher and is the co-founder of the human rights organisation Sudan Action Hub, told the briefing that success for Nusseibeh would result in people losing faith in the UN.

“If this candidate [succeeds], how would we tell people on the ground that the United Nations is not an obstruction of the [rights of] the people of Sudan?” said Alduma. “How could the people – not only in Sudan, but other victims of wars and international criminals – trust that the UN will achieve some kind of justice?”

Husam Mahjoub, a Sudanese advocate and co-founder of independent media Sudan Bukra TV, said: “Electing [the UAE’s] senior diplomat as secretary general would hand leadership of (UN) institutions to that government’s chief defender, at the very moment Sudanese civilians most need the ‌UN to hold powerful states accountable.”

Kenneth Roth, a former executive director of Human Rights Watch, told the briefing: “She has been asked about the UAE’s role in arming and supporting the RSF, and she just blatantly denies it without regard to the facts. That is not what we need as UN secretary-general.”

On Wednesday, Bruno Stagno Ugarte, the chief advocacy officer at Human Rights Watch, said Nusseibeh’s dismissal of UN reports documenting the UAE’s links to the RSF had “seriously undermined justice and accountability for the victims”.

In a statement on Tuesday Nusseibeh said that if she got the top UN job she would support the work of UN fact-finding missions for accountability and transitional justice over the war in Sudan, and described the RSF’s crimes as “atrocious”.

She added that she had taken a leave of absence from her ministerial post in the UAE government to be “mindful of the obligations of independence” the UN role would entail, adding that “the horrific conflict in Sudan will be the litmus test of the success of an incoming secretary general”.

To become the next UN security general, a candidate must secure a minimum of nine affirmative votes out of the 15 security council members, and avoid a veto from the US, the UK, China, France or Russia, its permanent members.

An informal security council poll earlier his month had ‌placed the former Costa Rican vice-president Rebeca Grynspan as the narrow frontrunner in the race. But she and all other candidates received two or more opposing votes from the permanent council members. The next straw poll could take place as soon as Friday, but the format and exact timing are still being negotiated by the diplomats.

At Tuesday’s briefing, Roth said: “It’s fair to say the RSF would not have been able to be nearly as successful militarily as it was and has been without that support from the UAE. And with that support, it didn’t just fight the Sudan armed forces. This wasn’t just a civil war. It committed mass atrocities.”
He added: “It amazes me that she’s being put forward. This is a completely unsuitable candidate.”

Kate Ferguson, co-founder and co-executive director of Protection Approaches, a charity working to prevent identity-based violence, said at the briefing: “There is not, as far as I have seen, sufficient evidence that this candidate is independent from the state from which she comes. And we must not be naive nor hide behind the pretence of naivety.
“This is autocratic capture of our most significant multilateral institution.”

enrich.title_zh: 苏丹侨民与人权组织谴责阿联酋提名的联合国秘书长人选
enrich.summary_zh: 阿联酋提名前常驻联合国代表拉娜·努赛贝竞逐下任联合国秘书长，苏丹侨民团体与国际人权组织强烈反对，指她一再否认阿联酋支持快速支援部队，而这支部队在苏丹包括法希尔犯下暴行；批评者称这等于让应被问责的国家主导联合国。努赛贝回应称将支持实况调查与过渡司法。

paragraphs.en: Members of the Sudanese diaspora and international human rights monitors have denounced the candidature of an Emirati diplomat for the top job at the UN, citing her denial of accusations that the United Arab Emirates is fuelling the war in Sudan by supporting the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces.
paragraphs.zh: 苏丹侨民群体成员和国际人权监督人士谴责一名阿联酋外交官竞逐联合国最高职位，理由是她否认了有关指控——即阿联酋通过支持准军事组织快速支援部队（RSF）在助燃苏丹战争。

paragraphs.en: The UAE nominated Lana Nusseibeh last week to replace the UN secretary general, António Guterres, as he finishes his second five-year term ⁠this year, upending a race that had become gridlocked.
paragraphs.zh: 上周，阿联酋提名拉娜·努赛贝（Lana Nusseibeh）接替联合国秘书长安东尼奥·古特雷斯——后者将于今年结束第二个五年任期——从而打乱了原本已陷入僵局的这场角逐。

paragraphs.en: Rights groups and others have for years documented evidence of UAE support for the RSF, which has been accused of atrocities during the course of its war against the Sudanese army, including an attack on the city of El Fasher in October 2025 that the UN said had “hallmarks of genocide” .
paragraphs.zh: 多年来，人权组织和其他方面一直在记录阿联酋支持RSF的证据。RSF在与苏丹政府军交战期间被控犯下暴行，包括2025年10月对法希尔市的袭击——联合国称这次袭击“带有种族灭绝的特征”。

paragraphs.en: Nusseibeh, the UAE’s representative to the UN until 2024, has repeatedly reflected the UAE’s blanket denials of the accusations.
paragraphs.zh: 努赛贝在2024年之前一直担任阿联酋常驻联合国代表，她多次转达了阿联酋对这些指控一概否认的立场。

paragraphs.en: The Sudanese pro-democracy and women’s rights activist Hala al-Karib, the regional director of the Strategic Initiative for Women in the Horn of Africa, said Nusseibeh had “no track record of acting independently of her country’s role in Sudan” and that endorsement by the security council would amount “essentially [to] a denial of the genocidal acts committed in El Fasher by the RSF”.
paragraphs.zh: 苏丹民主运动与妇女权利活动人士、非洲之角妇女战略倡议组织地区主任哈拉·卡里卜（Hala al-Karib）表示，努赛贝“没有任何独立于本国在苏丹所扮演角色之外行事的记录”，安理会若认可其候选资格，“实质上等同于否认RSF在法希尔犯下的种族灭绝行为”。

paragraphs.en: There was also strong criticism of Nusseibeh’s candidature at a virtual briefing by the Avaaz human rights advocacy group on Tuesday.
paragraphs.zh: 周二，人权倡导组织Avaaz举行的一场线上简报会上，也有人对努赛贝的候选资格提出强烈批评。

paragraphs.en: Ibrahim Alduma, who grew up in El Fasher and is the co-founder of the human rights organisation Sudan Action Hub, told the briefing that success for Nusseibeh would result in people losing faith in the UN.
paragraphs.zh: 在法希尔长大的易卜拉欣·阿尔杜马（Ibrahim Alduma）是人权组织“苏丹行动中心”（Sudan Action Hub）的联合创始人。他在简报会上说，努赛贝若成功当选，将导致人们失去对联合国的信任。

paragraphs.en: “If this candidate [succeeds], how would we tell people on the ground that the United Nations is not an obstruction of the [rights of] the people of Sudan?” said Alduma. “How could the people – not only in Sudan, but other victims of wars and international criminals – trust that the UN will achieve some kind of justice?”
paragraphs.zh: “如果这位候选人[成功当选]，我们怎么向当地民众解释，联合国不是苏丹人民[权利]的阻碍？”阿尔杜马说，“民众——不只是苏丹民众，还有其他战争受害者和国际罪犯——怎么能相信联合国会实现某种正义？”

paragraphs.en: Husam Mahjoub, a Sudanese advocate and co-founder of independent media Sudan Bukra TV, said: “Electing [the UAE’s] senior diplomat as secretary general would hand leadership of (UN) institutions to that government’s chief defender, at the very moment Sudanese civilians most need the ‌UN to hold powerful states accountable.”
paragraphs.zh: 苏丹维权人士、独立媒体“苏丹明日电视台”（Sudan Bukra TV）联合创始人胡萨姆·马赫朱卜（Husam Mahjoub）说：“在苏丹平民最需要联合国追究强权国家责任之际，把[阿联酋]这位资深外交官选为秘书长，等于把（联合国）机构的领导权交给该国政府的首席辩护人。”

paragraphs.en: Kenneth Roth, a former executive director of Human Rights Watch, told the briefing: “She has been asked about the UAE’s role in arming and supporting the RSF, and she just blatantly denies it without regard to the facts. That is not what we need as UN secretary-general.”
paragraphs.zh: 人权观察前执行主任肯尼斯·罗斯（Kenneth Roth）在简报会上说：“有人问过她阿联酋在武装和资助RSF方面所起的作用，而她只是公然否认，全然不顾事实。这不是我们所需要的联合国秘书长。”

paragraphs.en: On Wednesday, Bruno Stagno Ugarte, the chief advocacy officer at Human Rights Watch, said Nusseibeh’s dismissal of UN reports documenting the UAE’s links to the RSF had “seriously undermined justice and accountability for the victims”.
paragraphs.zh: 周三，人权观察首席倡导官布鲁诺·斯塔尼奥·乌加特（Bruno Stagno Ugarte）表示，努赛贝对记录阿联酋与RSF关联的联合国报告的驳斥，“严重损害了为受害者伸张正义和追究责任的努力”。

paragraphs.en: In a statement on Tuesday Nusseibeh said that if she got the top UN job she would support the work of UN fact-finding missions for accountability and transitional justice over the war in Sudan, and described the RSF’s crimes as “atrocious”.
paragraphs.zh: 在周二的一份声明中，努赛贝表示，如果她获得联合国最高职位，她将支持联合国实况调查团就苏丹战争开展追责与过渡司法方面的工作，并把RSF的罪行称为“残暴”。

paragraphs.en: She added that she had taken a leave of absence from her ministerial post in the UAE government to be “mindful of the obligations of independence” the UN role would entail, adding that “the horrific conflict in Sudan will be the litmus test of the success of an incoming secretary general”.
paragraphs.zh: 她还说，她已从阿联酋政府的部长职务上请假，以便“顾及”联合国这一职位所要求的“独立义务”；她并补充说：“苏丹这场可怕的冲突，将成为检验下一任秘书长是否成功的试金石。”

paragraphs.en: To become the next UN security general, a candidate must secure a minimum of nine affirmative votes out of the 15 security council members, and avoid a veto from the US, the UK, China, France or Russia, its permanent members.
paragraphs.zh: 要成为下一任联合国秘书长，候选人必须在安理会15个成员中获得至少9张赞成票，并且不能遭到五个常任理事国——美国、英国、中国、法国或俄罗斯——中任何一国的否决。

paragraphs.en: An informal security council poll earlier his month had ‌placed the former Costa Rican vice-president Rebeca Grynspan as the narrow frontrunner in the race. But she and all other candidates received two or more opposing votes from the permanent council members. The next straw poll could take place as soon as Friday, but the format and exact timing are still being negotiated by the diplomats.
paragraphs.zh: 本月早些时候的一次安理会非正式投票中，哥斯达黎加前副总统雷贝卡·格林斯潘以微弱优势暂居领先。但她和其他所有候选人都拿到了两个或两个以上常任理事国的反对票。下一次意向性投票最早可能在周五举行，但形式和确切时间仍由各国外交官磋商中。

paragraphs.en: At Tuesday’s briefing, Roth said: “It’s fair to say the RSF would not have been able to be nearly as successful militarily as it was and has been without that support from the UAE. And with that support, it didn’t just fight the Sudan armed forces. This wasn’t just a civil war. It committed mass atrocities.”
paragraphs.zh: 在周二的简报会上，罗斯说：“可以说，如果没有阿联酋的支持，RSF在军事上不可能达到过去和现在这样近乎成功的地步。而有了这种支持，它打击的就不只是苏丹武装部队。这不仅仅是一场内战。它犯下了大规模暴行。”

paragraphs.en: He added: “It amazes me that she’s being put forward. This is a completely unsuitable candidate.”
paragraphs.zh: 他补充说：“她竟然被推举出来，这让我感到震惊。这是一个完全不合适的候选人。”

paragraphs.en: Kate Ferguson, co-founder and co-executive director of Protection Approaches, a charity working to prevent identity-based violence, said at the briefing: “There is not, as far as I have seen, sufficient evidence that this candidate is independent from the state from which she comes. And we must not be naive nor hide behind the pretence of naivety.
paragraphs.zh: 致力于预防基于身份认同的暴力行为的慈善机构“保护途径”（Protection Approaches）联合创始人兼联合执行主任凯特·弗格森（Kate Ferguson）在简报会上说：“就我所见，没有充分证据表明这位候选人独立于她所属的国家。我们绝不能天真，也不能以假天真作掩护。”

paragraphs.en: “This is autocratic capture of our most significant multilateral institution.”
paragraphs.zh: “这是对我们最重要的多边机构的专制式劫持。”

vocab.meaning_zh: 候选资格、被提名的身份（英美报刊谈选举、任命时的常用词）
vocab.example_en: Her candidature was challenged by several member states.
vocab.example_zh: 她的候选资格受到数个成员国的质疑。

vocab.meaning_zh: 侨民群体（离开故土散居各地的族群）
vocab.example_en: The Ukrainian diaspora in Canada raised funds for relief efforts.
vocab.example_zh: 加拿大的乌克兰侨民群体为救援工作筹集了资金。

vocab.meaning_zh: 准军事的（有军事组织与武装，但不属于正规国家军队）
vocab.example_en: The paramilitary force has seized several key cities.
vocab.example_zh: 这支准军事部队已夺取数座关键城市。

vocab.meaning_zh: 暴行（尤指战争中针对平民的残暴行为）
vocab.example_en: Investigators documented atrocities committed against civilians.
vocab.example_zh: 调查人员记录下了针对平民犯下的暴行。

vocab.meaning_zh: （此处）标志、典型特征；原指金银器上的纯度印记，属熟词僻义，常见搭配 the hallmarks of sth
vocab.example_en: The report found the hallmarks of a deliberate campaign of violence.
vocab.example_zh: 报告认为其中存在有计划的暴力行动的特征。

vocab.meaning_zh: （此处）全面的、一概的、无例外的（blanket denial / blanket ban 是外刊高频搭配）
vocab.example_en: The ministry issued a blanket denial of the allegations.
vocab.example_zh: 该部门对这些指控一概否认。

vocab.meaning_zh: 颠覆、打乱（原有局面或秩序）
vocab.example_en: The late entry of a new candidate upended the race.
vocab.example_zh: 一名新候选人的迟来参选打乱了这场角逐。

vocab.meaning_zh: （此处）意向性投票、摸底投票；安理会遴选秘书长时用这种非正式投票显示各方支持与 veto 情况
vocab.example_en: The second straw poll is expected later this week.
vocab.example_zh: 第二轮意向性投票预计本周晚些时候举行。

vocab.meaning_zh: 试金石、检验标准（源自石蕊试纸）
vocab.example_en: How the agency handles this case will be a litmus test of its independence.
vocab.example_zh: 该机构如何处理这一案件，将成为检验其独立性的试金石。

vocab.meaning_zh: 问责、责任追究（指权力者须为行为负责并接受追究）
vocab.example_en: Victims’ families are demanding accountability for the killings.
vocab.example_zh: 受害者的家属要求对这些杀戮追究责任。

sentences.en: Members of the Sudanese diaspora and international human rights monitors have denounced the candidature of an Emirati diplomat for the top job at the UN, citing her denial of accusations that the United Arab Emirates is fuelling the war in Sudan by supporting the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces.
sentences.structure: 主干：Members ... and international human rights monitors（并列主语）have denounced the candidature（谓语+宾语）。修饰：of an Emirati diplomat for the top job at the UN 是层层后置的介词短语，限定 candidature；citing ... 为现在分词短语作原因状语；that the United Arab Emirates is fuelling ... 是 accusations 的同位语从句，说明指控内容；by supporting ... 在从句中作方式状语。
sentences.analysis_zh: 这句是典型的英文新闻导语：先给动作（谴责），再用分词状语交代理由，最后用同位语从句把“指控内容”一次性铺开。注意 accuse 类名词后接同位语从句时，中文习惯把从句提前说成“就……的指控”，若照英文语序直译会拗口。fuelle 本义“加燃料”，此处引申为“助燃、激化”，比 support 更带贬义判断。

sentences.en: The Sudanese pro-democracy and women’s rights activist Hala al-Karib, the regional director of the Strategic Initiative for Women in the Horn of Africa, said Nusseibeh had “no track record of acting independently of her country’s role in Sudan” and that endorsement by the security council would amount “essentially [to] a denial of the genocidal acts committed in El Fasher by the RSF”.
sentences.structure: 主干：Hala al-Karib（主语）said（谓语）+ 两个并列宾语从句。修饰：the regional director of ... 是主语的同位语，交代身份；从句一 Nusseibeh had no track record of acting independently of ...；从句二 that endorsement ... would amount to a denial of ...。committed in El Fasher by the RSF 是过去分词短语后置修饰 the genocidal acts。
sentences.analysis_zh: 这里的关键是第二个 that 不能省——两个宾语从句并列时，第二个 that 起到断句标记作用，告诉读者“这是第二个观点，不是第一个从句的延续”。amount to 意为“等于、无异于”，把“认可候选人”与“否认种族灭绝”画等号，是这段话的修辞力度所在。act independently of sth 意为“不受……左右地行事”，是评价官员独立性的固定说法。

sentences.en: “It’s fair to say the RSF would not have been able to be nearly as successful militarily as it was and has been without that support from the UAE.
sentences.structure: 主干：It’s fair to say + 宾语从句。从句内部：the RSF would not have been able to be ... successful（虚拟语气的主句）+ without that support（含蓄条件，相当于 if it had not been for that support）；nearly as successful militarily as it was and has been 为同级比较结构，it was and has been 是两个时点（过去与现在）的并列。
sentences.analysis_zh: would not have been able to 是“过去条件虚拟”，条件并未用 if 从句明说，而由 without 短语隐含——这是英文中很有力的一种归因写法：先把结论说成“理所当然”，再补一个轻描淡写的条件，把“若无阿联酋支持”变成不言自明的前提。as it was and has been 把“当时”与“至今”一并纳入，暗示支持是持续性的。

background.title: 联合国秘书长怎么选出来
background.text_zh: 按《联合国宪章》，秘书长由大会任命，但须经安理会推荐，因此真正的筛选发生在安理会。安理会15个成员中需至少9票赞成，且五个常任理事国（美、英、法、中、俄）中任何一国投反对票即构成否决。实际操作中，安理会通过一系列不公开的“意向性投票”（straw poll，文中称 informal poll）来摸底：选票上分“鼓励、不鼓励、无意见”三栏，候选人据此判断自己是否还有胜算。整个程序长期被批评为大国密室操作，发展中国家与民间组织多年来推动增加透明度（如公开候选人名单、举行候选人对话会）。

background.title: 苏丹内战、RSF与“法希尔”
background.text_zh: 快速支援部队（RSF）源自达尔富尔地区的阿拉伯民兵武装，后编入苏丹安全体系，2023年4月起与苏丹武装部队（SAF）全面开战，内战延续至今。交战期间，RSF被多个人权组织和联合国调查机制指控在达尔富尔等地对平民实施性暴力、屠杀与族群清洗。法希尔（El Fasher）是北达尔富尔州首府，长期是政府军及其盟友在达尔富尔的重要据点，2025年10月遭RSF进攻，联合国方面称相关行为带有“种族灭绝特征”。阿联酋一再被指通过乍得等渠道向RSF输送武器与物资，阿联酋政府对此一概否认——这正是本文争议的起点。

title_en: Christine Lagarde departs at a moment of peril
excerpt_en: Her successor as ECB chief will have an unenviable job

enrich.title_zh: 克里斯蒂娜·拉加德在危局之中离任
enrich.summary_zh: 本期《经济学人》以一句话提要预告了克里斯蒂娜·拉加德卸任欧洲央行行长一事。提要并未展开她离任的具体背景，只是点明时机凶险，并强调接任者将面对一份毫不令人羡慕的差事：领导欧元区货币政策的核心机构，却要在棘手局面中接手。

paragraphs.en: Her successor as ECB chief will have an unenviable job
paragraphs.zh: 接替她出任欧洲央行行长的人，将摊上一份毫不令人羡慕的差事。

vocab.meaning_zh: 离任、卸任（熟词僻义：日常义为“离开、出发”，在人事语境中指离开某个职位）
vocab.example_en: The governor departs after eight years in office.
vocab.example_zh: 这位行长在任职八年后卸任。

vocab.meaning_zh: 严重危险、危局（比 danger 更文雅、语气更重，外刊常用其来渲染局势之凶险）
vocab.example_en: The industry is in peril as demand collapses.
vocab.example_zh: 随着需求崩塌，该行业正陷入危局。

vocab.meaning_zh: 继任者、接班人（常与 as 连用，表示“作为某一职位的继任者”）
vocab.example_en: She is the front-runner to be his successor as chief executive.
vocab.example_zh: 她是接替他出任首席执行官的热门人选。

vocab.meaning_zh: 不值得羡慕的、让人头疼的（用于形容任务、处境艰难，带一点同情或揶揄）
vocab.example_en: He inherited an unenviable pile of debt.
vocab.example_zh: 他接手了一堆令人头疼的债务。

vocab.meaning_zh: 欧洲中央银行（European Central Bank）的缩写，欧元区货币政策主管机构，总部在法兰克福
vocab.example_en: The ECB raised rates for the tenth consecutive time.
vocab.example_zh: 欧洲央行连续第十次加息。

sentences.en: Her successor as ECB chief will have an unenviable job
sentences.structure: 主干：Her successor will have an unenviable job（主+谓+宾）；修饰：as ECB chief 为后置定语，紧跟在 successor 之后说明“接任的是什么职位”
sentences.analysis_zh: 这是一句标准的英文提要（standfirst）：主语 successor 后接 as 引导的介词短语作定语，把职位信息压缩在其中，避免写成 who succeeds her as ECB chief 那样的从句，从而保持句子短促有力。谓语用一般将来时 will have，语气是预判而非陈述事实；宾语中心词 job 前加 unenviable 这个带评价色彩的形容词，一个词就完成了编辑的态度表态——不直说“局面艰难”，而说“这活儿没人羡慕”，是外刊标题与提要常用的委婉修辞。

background.title: 欧洲央行与拉加德
background.text_zh: 欧洲中央银行（ECB）是欧元区的中央银行，总部位于德国法兰克福，负责制定欧元区二十国的货币政策、维护物价稳定，并监管大型银行。行长由欧洲理事会任命，任期八年、不得连任，这一设计旨在让行长不受短期政治周期干扰。克里斯蒂娜·拉加德是法国人，曾任法国财政部长和国际货币基金组织（IMF）总裁，2019 年 11 月接替马里奥·德拉吉出任欧洲央行行长，是首位担任该职的女性；按八年任期计算，她的任期至 2027 年 10 月止。她任内欧元区先后经历新冠疫情冲击、能源价格飙升带来的高通胀以及快速加息周期，因此“继任者”一词在欧洲央行语境中通常意味着接过一套尚未尘埃落定的政策框架。

title_en: The never-ending absurdity of global oil markets
excerpt_en: Despite stronger Gulf exports, Brent is near its Iran-war peak

enrich.title_zh: 全球石油市场永无止境的荒诞
enrich.summary_zh: 这篇报道以“全球石油市场永无止境的荒诞”为题，聚焦油市的反常走势：尽管海湾地区出口增加，布伦特原油价格仍接近伊朗战争期间的高点，说明供应增加并未明显压低基准油价。

paragraphs.en: Despite stronger Gulf exports, Brent is near its Iran-war peak
paragraphs.zh: 尽管海湾出口更强劲，布伦特原油仍接近其伊朗战争期间的高点。

vocab.meaning_zh: 荒诞；荒谬；荒唐之处
vocab.example_en: The absurdity of the situation made everyone laugh.
vocab.example_zh: 这种局面的荒诞让大家都笑了。

vocab.meaning_zh: 永无止境的；没完没了的
vocab.example_en: The never-ending debate has frustrated voters.
vocab.example_zh: 这场没完没了的争论让选民感到沮丧。

vocab.meaning_zh: 布伦特原油（国际原油定价的重要基准）
vocab.example_en: Brent crude rose above $80 a barrel.
vocab.example_zh: 布伦特原油升至每桶80美元以上。

vocab.meaning_zh: 高点；峰值；最高水平
vocab.example_en: Prices are still below last year’s peak.
vocab.example_zh: 价格仍低于去年的峰值。

vocab.meaning_zh: 海湾地区出口（通常指波斯湾产油国的原油出口）
vocab.example_en: Stronger Gulf exports could ease global supply concerns.
vocab.example_zh: 海湾出口增强可能缓解全球供应担忧。

sentences.en: Despite stronger Gulf exports, Brent is near its Iran-war peak
sentences.structure: 主干：Brent is near its Iran-war peak / 修饰：Despite stronger Gulf exports 为句首让步状语
sentences.analysis_zh: 这句话的主干是“Brent is near its Iran-war peak”，即布伦特原油接近其伊朗战争期间的高点。句首的 Despite 引导让步状语，后面接名词短语 stronger Gulf exports，而不是完整句子；stronger 修饰 Gulf exports，表示海湾出口更强。near 在这里是介词，its 指 Brent 的高点。作者用“出口增强”与“价格仍接近战争高点”形成反差，突出油市走势反常。

background.title: 布伦特原油与海湾出口
background.text_zh: 布伦特（Brent）是全球原油定价最重要的基准之一，原指北海布伦特油田所产原油，现常作为国际油价的参照。海湾出口通常指波斯湾产油国的原油出口；该地区的供应变化和伊朗相关冲突都会影响国际油价。“Iran-war peak”在给定材料中没有说明具体指哪一场战争，只表示布伦特原油在伊朗战争期间达到的高点。

title_en: The countries making a fortune from the US-China rivalry
excerpt_en: Critical-mineral profits could transform a lucky few

enrich.title_zh: 靠中美对抗大发横财的国家
enrich.summary_zh: 标题与提要显示，文章关注中美两国在关键矿产领域的争夺，以及这场大国竞争带来的矿产利润将流向何处。提要强调，受益者只是“幸运的少数”：少数拥有锂、镍、稀土等资源的国家可能因此获得巨额收益，经济命运被彻底改写。

paragraphs.en: Critical-mineral profits could transform a lucky few
paragraphs.zh: 关键矿产带来的利润，可能让少数幸运儿脱胎换骨。

vocab.meaning_zh: 关键矿产；战略性矿产。指对新能源、芯片、军工等产业不可或缺、且供应风险较高的矿产，如锂、钴、镍、稀土、石墨。外刊中几乎固定搭配，不说 important mineral。
vocab.example_en: The race for critical minerals has reshaped diplomacy in Africa and Southeast Asia.
vocab.example_zh: 对关键矿产的争夺已经重塑了非洲和东南亚的外交格局。

vocab.meaning_zh: 发大财，赚取巨额财富。标题中用的是 making a fortune from…，表示“靠……大发其财”。
vocab.example_en: A handful of exporting countries have made a fortune from soaring nickel prices.
vocab.example_zh: 少数出口国靠飙升的镍价大发其财。

vocab.meaning_zh: 竞争，对抗（长期性、带有敌意的较量）。US-China rivalry 是近年外刊描述中美关系的高频固定说法，比 competition 更强调对立色彩。
vocab.example_en: The US-China rivalry has split global supply chains along political lines.
vocab.example_zh: 中美对抗使全球供应链按政治阵营出现分裂。

vocab.meaning_zh: 彻底改变，使……发生根本性转变。及物动词，这里宾语是人（a lucky few），意思是“改变这些国家的命运”，而非仅仅“改善”。
vocab.example_en: Oil discoveries transformed the economies of the Gulf states within a generation.
vocab.example_zh: 石油的发现在一代人的时间里彻底改变了海湾国家的经济。

vocab.meaning_zh: 少数幸运儿。形容词加 the 或 a 构成名词性短语，是英文新闻标题的常见凝练手法；a lucky few 隐含“多数国家分不到好处”的对比意味。
vocab.example_en: Globalisation enriched a lucky few while leaving many regions behind.
vocab.example_zh: 全球化让少数幸运儿富了起来，却把许多地区甩在了后面。

sentences.en: Critical-mineral profits could transform a lucky few
sentences.structure: 主干：Critical-mineral profits（主语）+ could transform（谓语）+ a lucky few（宾语）。修饰：形容词 critical-mineral 作前置定语修饰 profits；could 为情态动词，表示可能性而非事实判断。
sentences.analysis_zh: 这是一个标准的编辑体 standfirst（提要句）：全句只有七个词，却把“变量—动作—受益者”三层信息压缩在一起。主语用名词短语 critical-mineral profits 起句，直接把话题定在“钱”上，而不是“矿产”本身，暗示文章要讲的是利益分配。谓语选了 could 而非 will，是外刊提要的典型分寸感——给出趋势判断，同时避开对未发生之事的断言。宾语 a lucky few 最见功力：形容词加 a 构成名词性短语，既省字又自带评价色彩（“幸运”），还通过“few”点出稀缺性——受益国屈指可数，多数国家只能旁观。若改写成 Only a few countries may benefit from critical minerals，意思不变，但信息重心从“利润”挪到了“国家”，力度和悬念都弱了很多，这也正是提要不写成完整说明句的原因。

background.title: 关键矿产与中美角力
background.text_zh: “关键矿产”（critical minerals）指对清洁能源、半导体、国防工业不可或缺、且供应链集中度高的矿产，如锂、钴、镍、石墨、稀土及镓、锗等。中国在稀土和多种精炼环节占据主导地位：据国际能源署等机构统计，中国约占全球稀土矿产量六成、精炼分离环节九成。美国自 2022 年起通过《通胀削减法案》为本国及自贸伙伴的电池矿物设补贴门槛，并牵头成立“矿产安全伙伴关系”（MSP），联合澳大利亚、加拿大、日本、韩国等重构供应链。2023 年起中国对镓、锗、石墨、锑等实施出口管制，被视为反制措施。与此同时，印尼（镍）、智利与阿根廷（锂）、刚果民主共和国（钴）、越南与马来西亚（稀土）等资源国成为各方争取对象，纷纷以出口禁令或本土加工要求换取投资与技术，即所谓“资源民族主义”升温。这些是讨论该话题时常见的事实背景，与本文具体论点无关。

title_en: Ignore AI and ask for that pay rise
excerpt_en: Fear of a technological revolution may be suppressing wages

enrich.title_zh: 别管什么人工智能，该谈加薪就去谈
enrich.summary_zh: 标题以略带调侃的口吻劝读者：与其被 AI 吓住，不如直接去争取加薪。提要给出理由：对「技术革命」的恐惧情绪本身，可能正在压低工资水平——也就是说，对失业的担忧会影响劳动者的议价与涨薪诉求。（该刊仅提供标题与提要，正文论证未给出。）

paragraphs.en: Fear of a technological revolution may be suppressing wages
paragraphs.zh: 对技术革命的恐惧，或许正在压低工资水平。

vocab.meaning_zh: 不理会、把……放在一边（此处是祈使语气：别被它牵着走，该谈加薪就去谈）
vocab.example_en: Ignore the noise from the markets and stick to your long-term plan.
vocab.example_zh: 别理会市场的噪音，坚持你的长期计划。

vocab.meaning_zh: 加薪（英式说法；美式英语通常说 pay raise）
vocab.example_en: She asked her boss for a pay rise after taking on two extra projects.
vocab.example_zh: 接手两个额外项目后，她向老板提出了加薪。

vocab.meaning_zh: 压制、抑制；此处指把工资水平或涨幅「压下去」，而非人为禁止
vocab.example_en: Weak union bargaining power has suppressed wage growth for a decade.
vocab.example_zh: 工会谈判力薄弱，十年来一直抑制着工资增长。

vocab.meaning_zh: 工资（通常指按小时、按周计算的报酬，常用复数 wages）
vocab.example_en: Real wages have barely moved since the financial crisis.
vocab.example_zh: 自金融危机以来，实际工资几乎没什么变化。

vocab.meaning_zh: 技术革命；外刊中常用来指以 AI、自动化为主导的新一轮产业变革
vocab.example_en: Every technological revolution has destroyed some jobs and created others.
vocab.example_zh: 每一次技术革命都会消灭一些岗位，也创造另一些岗位。

sentences.en: Fear of a technological revolution may be suppressing wages
sentences.structure: 主干：Fear（主语）+ may be suppressing（谓语，情态动词 may + 进行体）+ wages（宾语）；修饰：of a technological revolution 是后置定语，挂在 Fear 后面，说明「恐惧」的对象。
sentences.analysis_zh: 这句 standfirst 用「抽象名词作主语 + 进行体」的结构，把一件说不清主体的事写得简洁有力。主语不是「AI」，而是「恐惧」本身——编辑的巧思就在这里：真正压工资的不是技术，而是人对技术的害怕。may be suppressing 用「情态 + 进行」，语气刻意留有余地（may），同时强调这是一个正在发生的过程（进行体），比 Fear suppresses wages 更像在描述当下趋势。wages 用复数、不加冠词，是泛指「工资水平」的常规写法。整句信息压缩度很高，翻译时中文宜加「或许」和「正在」，把推测与进行两层意思都保留下来。

background.title: 「技术性失业」恐惧与工资谈判
background.text_zh: 提要中「对技术革命的恐惧」指的是公众和劳动者担心 AI、自动化取代工作岗位，这类担忧在经济学里被称为「技术性失业」（technological unemployment），凯恩斯 1930 年的文章《我们后代的经济可能性》中就用了这个说法。2022 年底 ChatGPT 发布后，生成式 AI 能否替代白领工作的讨论迅速升温，成为媒体高频话题。另一方面，英美等国在 2022—2023 年高通胀之后经历了实际工资增长乏力的问题，「加薪」成为劳资谈判的焦点。语言上，pay rise 是英式英语，美式英语说 pay raise，The Economist 使用英式拼写与用词习惯。

title_en: China’s stock markets are the great global exception
excerpt_en: If the country is winning the future, why are its investors so glum?

enrich.title_zh: 中国股市：全球独一份的例外
enrich.summary_zh: 《经济学人》以「中国股市是全球范围内的一大例外」为标题，提要只用一句反问点题：如果这个国家正在赢得未来，投资者为何还如此沮丧？这句话把中国在产业与技术上的强势叙事，同股市投资者的低迷情绪并置成一组矛盾，全篇的讨论张力正由这个反差展开——它既是编辑提出的疑问，也是理解当今中国资产定价的关键切口。

paragraphs.en: If the country is winning the future, why are its investors so glum?
paragraphs.zh: 如果这个国家正在赢得未来，那么它的投资者又为何如此愁眉不展？

vocab.meaning_zh: 愁眉不展的、情绪低落的；形容市场人气时，可指「低迷、没人愿意买」，是外刊写行情气氛的高频词
vocab.example_en: Fund managers sound glum about the year ahead.
vocab.example_zh: 基金经理们对来年并不乐观，谈起时语气低落。

vocab.meaning_zh: 赢得未来。原为美国政治话语（如奥巴马国情咨文）中的说法，指在长期技术、产业和教育竞争中占据上风；此处借指「中国在长期竞争中领先」，带修辞色彩
vocab.example_en: Policymakers keep saying that whoever leads in clean tech will win the future.
vocab.example_zh: 政策制定者反复强调，谁在清洁技术上领先，谁就赢得未来。

vocab.meaning_zh: 例外。the great exception 指「唯一的大例外、与众不同的那一个」，标题用它与「全球普遍上涨」形成对照
vocab.example_en: Every rule has its exceptions, and this market has been a big one.
vocab.example_zh: 凡规则皆有例外，而这个市场就是个大例外。

vocab.meaning_zh: 投资者、投资人；此处特指二级市场参与者（散户与机构），而非外商直接投资
vocab.example_en: Retail investors have been pulling money out of equity funds.
vocab.example_zh: 散户投资者一直在从股票基金中撤资。

sentences.en: If the country is winning the future, why are its investors so glum?
sentences.structure: 主干：why are its investors so glum?（特殊疑问句，语序为「疑问词 + be + 主语 + 表语」）/ 修饰：if 引导条件状语从句，作全句的前提；the country 以定冠词借指中国；winning the future 用现在进行时，强调「正在赢」的过程感
sentences.analysis_zh: 这是一个「假设—反问」结构：先以 if 从句把「这个国家正在赢得未来」设为读者大致接受的前提（它来自当时关于中国制造业与科技实力的流行说法），再用反问句逼出反差。用疑问句而非陈述句，是《经济学人》提要的典型手法——不直接下结论，而是让读者自己感到矛盾，从而愿意往下读。注意 the country、its investors 都用代词或定冠词回指，句子里一次也没出现 China，却不会歧义，这是标题页已知主题时的省略技巧。

background.title: 「赢得未来」与「股市不涨」之间的现实落差
background.text_zh: 这句提要点到的反差有具体的现实来源。一方面，2020 年代以来中国在电动汽车、动力电池、光伏、造船以及人工智能（如 2025 年初的 DeepSeek）等领域表现抢眼，出口结构升级，「中国制造」在多个赛道被认为取得长期优势，这正是 winning the future 所指的说法。另一方面，中国内地与香港股市在 2021 年见顶后长期走弱：上证综指多年在 3000 点附近反复拉锯，2024 年初一度跌破 2700 点，恒生指数跌幅更大；监管层先后下调印花税、收紧减持规则、限制融券，中央汇金等「国家队」多次增持 ETF 托市，外资一度持续流出。房地产深度调整、通缩压力与消费疲软被视为压制估值的主因。理解这层背景，才能体会编辑那句反问的分量：产业竞争力属于「未来」，而股价反映的是当下企业盈利、股东回报与投资者信心。

title_en: Egypt fines prominent editor Lina Attalah and shuts independent news outlet Mada Masr
excerpt_en: Warnings of escalating clampdown on press freedom come after Cairo court convicts Attalah of managing an unlicensed website
body_en: Lina Attalah, a prominent Egyptian journalist and the editor-in-chief of the news outlet Mada Masr, has been released from detention by Egypt’s authorities and had her website ordered to be shut down by a court amid an intensifying crackdown on independent media in the country.
Attalah was taken briefly into custody after a Cairo court convicted her of managing an unlicensed website, prompting fresh international concerns over press freedom in Egypt.
According to Mada Masr, Attalah was released after the news outlet had paid a fine of 3m Egyptian pounds ($53,500; £40,100), prompting statements of support from global human rights groups.

“Lina Attalah was released after we paid the said fine,” said her lawyer Hassan al-Azhari. “In the process, we discovered that she had been sentenced in absentia in 2024 to a year in prison, as well as a fine of 20,000 Egyptian pounds,” he told AFP.
Attalah’s defence team had appealed that sentence, and a new court hearing was scheduled for 11 November, Azhari added.
Related: The news website that’s keeping press freedom alive in Egypt | Leslie T Chang
Attalah founded Mada Masr in 2013, after coming to international prominence in 2011 during the Arab spring. An advocate for press freedom, she has been arrested on a number of occasions.

Attalah’s detention, and the ordered closure of Mada Masr – which says it had applied for a licence to operate three years ago and had no reply from Egyptian authorities – follows the arrest of the entire six-person team at the independent factchecking platform Matsadaash, who were charged with belonging to the outlawed Muslim Brotherhood.
Attalah’s legal team suggested she had been, in effect, ambushed during a court appearance, with a judge appointing a defence lawyer for her before security personnel detained her in the courtroom.

The crackdown “can only mean that Egypt’s security agencies are moving from years of harassing independent media to wiping them out completely”, said Hossam Bahgat, the head of the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights (EIPR), who attended the court hearing.

“This escalation validates our fears that the arrest and continued detention of the six Matsadaash journalists would signal a crackdown of unprecedented magnitude,” said Bahgat. “It risks fully eviscerating the narrow margin of press freedoms that have been carefully maintained in Egypt over the past decade, albeit amid great personal sacrifice – a margin that had allowed the continued operation of a handful of news outlets and human rights organisations despite frequent harassment, including through legal avenues.”

According to EIPR, the recent moves against independent media follow an increasing frequency of statements from the Egyptian president, Abdel Fatah al-Sisi , since August claiming a conspiracy to destabilise the country. He has said he intended to remain in power until 2030 to protect Egypt from “traitors, criminals, and saboteurs”.

Reporters Without Borders said the court’s decision was “outrageous” and “shameful”, urging authorities to release Attalah “at once”. The Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) also condemned the verdict. Amnesty International said the verdict represented “a crushing blow to press freedom”.

Egypt is among the top jailers of journalists globally, with 25 currently behind bars, according to the CPJ. Attalah’s lawyers took steps to challenge the ruling, with a hearing in a retrial of the case scheduled for 11 November.
Underlining concerns over the crackdown, Pen International issued a statement with several dozen civil society organisations condemning the moves.

“Though this is the sixth case brought against Mada Masr in six years, this is the first time that a case of this nature has been referred to trial,” the writers’ association said. “For years, Egyptian authorities have leveraged their repressive and restrictive tactics against independent media outlets to harass journalists, restrict their operations and chill freedom of expression. To escalate to the step of referral to trial must be read as a clear intent to entirely shutter the independent media space, and to permanently close what remains.”

enrich.title_zh: 埃及法院对知名主编莉娜·阿塔拉处以罚款并下令关闭独立新闻网站 Mada Masr
enrich.summary_zh: 埃及知名记者、Mada Masr 主编莉娜·阿塔拉因“经营无证网站”被判罪，缴清300万埃及镑罚款后获释，法院同时下令关闭该网站；她此前还被缺席判处一年监禁。此事紧随独立事实核查平台 Matsadaash 六名记者被捕之后，多家人权与新闻自由组织谴责这是对埃及独立媒体的全面清剿。

paragraphs.en: Lina Attalah, a prominent Egyptian journalist and the editor-in-chief of the news outlet Mada Masr, has been released from detention by Egypt’s authorities and had her website ordered to be shut down by a court amid an intensifying crackdown on independent media in the country.
paragraphs.zh: 埃及知名记者、新闻网站 Mada Masr 主编莉娜·阿塔拉已被埃及当局释放，但同时一家法院下令关闭她的网站。此举发生在该国对独立媒体的打压不断升级之际。

paragraphs.en: Attalah was taken briefly into custody after a Cairo court convicted her of managing an unlicensed website, prompting fresh international concerns over press freedom in Egypt.
paragraphs.zh: 开罗一家法院裁定阿塔拉经营未获许可的网站罪名成立，她因此被短暂羁押，这引发了国际社会对埃及新闻自由的新一轮担忧。

paragraphs.en: According to Mada Masr, Attalah was released after the news outlet had paid a fine of 3m Egyptian pounds ($53,500; £40,100), prompting statements of support from global human rights groups.
paragraphs.zh: 据 Mada Masr 报道，该新闻网站缴纳了300万埃及镑（约合5.35万美元、4.01万英镑）的罚款后，阿塔拉获释，多个人权组织随即发表声明表示声援。

paragraphs.en: “Lina Attalah was released after we paid the said fine,” said her lawyer Hassan al-Azhari. “In the process, we discovered that she had been sentenced in absentia in 2024 to a year in prison, as well as a fine of 20,000 Egyptian pounds,” he told AFP.
paragraphs.zh: “在我们缴纳上述罚款后，莉娜·阿塔拉获释了，”她的律师哈桑·阿兹哈里说。“在此过程中我们发现，她已于2024年被缺席判处一年监禁，并处罚金2万埃及镑，”他向法新社表示。

paragraphs.en: Attalah’s defence team had appealed that sentence, and a new court hearing was scheduled for 11 November, Azhari added.
paragraphs.zh: 阿兹哈里补充说，阿塔拉的辩护团队已对该判决提出上诉，新的庭审定于11月11日举行。

paragraphs.en: Related: The news website that’s keeping press freedom alive in Egypt | Leslie T Chang
paragraphs.zh: 相关阅读：在埃及守护新闻自由的这家新闻网站 | 莱斯莉·T·张

paragraphs.en: Attalah founded Mada Masr in 2013, after coming to international prominence in 2011 during the Arab spring. An advocate for press freedom, she has been arrested on a number of occasions.
paragraphs.zh: 阿塔拉于2013年创办 Mada Masr，此前她在2011年“阿拉伯之春”期间已蜚声国际。作为新闻自由的倡导者，她曾多次被捕。

paragraphs.en: Attalah’s detention, and the ordered closure of Mada Masr – which says it had applied for a licence to operate three years ago and had no reply from Egyptian authorities – follows the arrest of the entire six-person team at the independent factchecking platform Matsadaash, who were charged with belonging to the outlawed Muslim Brotherhood.
paragraphs.zh: 阿塔拉被拘押、Mada Masr 被勒令关闭——该网站称三年前就已申请运营执照，但埃及当局始终未予答复——而在此之前，独立事实核查平台 Matsadaash 的全部六名成员被捕，他们被控从属被取缔的穆斯林兄弟会。

paragraphs.en: Attalah’s legal team suggested she had been, in effect, ambushed during a court appearance, with a judge appointing a defence lawyer for her before security personnel detained her in the courtroom.
paragraphs.zh: 阿塔拉的律师团队认为，她实际上是在出庭时遭到“突袭”：法官先为她指定了一名辩护律师，随后安保人员就在法庭内将她拘留。

paragraphs.en: The crackdown “can only mean that Egypt’s security agencies are moving from years of harassing independent media to wiping them out completely”, said Hossam Bahgat, the head of the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights (EIPR), who attended the court hearing.
paragraphs.zh: 出席庭审的埃及个人权利倡议组织（EIPR）负责人胡萨姆·巴赫加特说，这场打压“只能说明埃及安全机构正从多年的骚扰独立媒体，转向将它们彻底清除”。

paragraphs.en: “This escalation validates our fears that the arrest and continued detention of the six Matsadaash journalists would signal a crackdown of unprecedented magnitude,” said Bahgat. “It risks fully eviscerating the narrow margin of press freedoms that have been carefully maintained in Egypt over the past decade, albeit amid great personal sacrifice – a margin that had allowed the continued operation of a handful of news outlets and human rights organisations despite frequent harassment, including through legal avenues.”
paragraphs.zh: “这一升级印证了我们的担忧：六名 Matsadaash 记者被捕并持续被羁押，预示着一场规模空前的打压，”巴赫加特说。“它有可能彻底掏空过去十年来埃及小心维持的那一线狭窄的新闻自由空间——尽管这背后是巨大的个人牺牲。正是这一线空间，让少数几家新闻媒体和人权组织得以在频繁骚扰（包括通过法律途径的骚扰）之下继续运作。”

paragraphs.en: According to EIPR, the recent moves against independent media follow an increasing frequency of statements from the Egyptian president, Abdel Fatah al-Sisi , since August claiming a conspiracy to destabilise the country. He has said he intended to remain in power until 2030 to protect Egypt from “traitors, criminals, and saboteurs”.
paragraphs.zh: 据 EIPR 称，近期针对独立媒体的行动，发生在埃及总统阿卜杜勒-法塔赫·塞西自8月以来愈发频繁地声称存在破坏国家稳定的阴谋之后。他曾表示打算执政至2030年，以保护埃及免受“叛徒、罪犯和破坏分子”之害。

paragraphs.en: Reporters Without Borders said the court’s decision was “outrageous” and “shameful”, urging authorities to release Attalah “at once”. The Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) also condemned the verdict. Amnesty International said the verdict represented “a crushing blow to press freedom”.
paragraphs.zh: 无国界记者组织称法院的裁决“令人愤慨”“可耻”，并敦促当局“立即”释放阿塔拉。保护记者委员会（CPJ）也谴责了这一判决。国际特赦组织表示，该判决是“对新闻自由的一记毁灭性打击”。

paragraphs.en: Egypt is among the top jailers of journalists globally, with 25 currently behind bars, according to the CPJ. Attalah’s lawyers took steps to challenge the ruling, with a hearing in a retrial of the case scheduled for 11 November.
paragraphs.zh: 据 CPJ 统计，埃及是全球关押记者最多的国家之一，目前有25名记者在押。阿塔拉的律师已采取措施挑战这一裁决，案件重审的听证会定于11月11日举行。

paragraphs.en: Underlining concerns over the crackdown, Pen International issued a statement with several dozen civil society organisations condemning the moves.
paragraphs.zh: 国际笔会与数十家公民社会组织联合发表声明谴责这些行动，进一步凸显了外界对这场打压的担忧。

paragraphs.en: “Though this is the sixth case brought against Mada Masr in six years, this is the first time that a case of this nature has been referred to trial,” the writers’ association said. “For years, Egyptian authorities have leveraged their repressive and restrictive tactics against independent media outlets to harass journalists, restrict their operations and chill freedom of expression. To escalate to the step of referral to trial must be read as a clear intent to entirely shutter the independent media space, and to permanently close what remains.”
paragraphs.zh: “尽管这是六年来针对 Mada Masr 的第六起案件，但此类案件被移交审判还是第一次，”该作家协会表示。“多年来，埃及当局一直对独立媒体动用其压制性和限制性手段，骚扰记者、限制其运作、压制言论自由。如今升级到移交审判这一步，只能被解读为一个明确的意图：彻底关闭独立媒体空间，并永久封死仅存的一切。”

vocab.meaning_zh: 主编；总编辑
vocab.example_en: She was promoted to editor-in-chief of the magazine last year.
vocab.example_zh: 她去年被提升为该杂志的主编。

vocab.meaning_zh: （当局的）严厉打击，镇压；常与 on 连用
vocab.example_en: The government launched a crackdown on illegal online gambling.
vocab.example_zh: 政府展开了一场对非法网络赌博的严厉打击。

vocab.meaning_zh: 缺席地（多指缺席审判）
vocab.example_en: He was sentenced in absentia to five years in prison.
vocab.example_zh: 他被缺席判处五年监禁。

vocab.meaning_zh: 事实核查（的）；核对信息真伪的工作
vocab.example_en: The outlet runs a factchecking desk that verifies viral claims.
vocab.example_zh: 该媒体设有一个事实核查部门，专门核实网络热传的说法。

vocab.meaning_zh: 伏击，突袭；此处引申为（在毫无防备时）突然下手
vocab.example_en: Critics say the committee ambushed her with questions she had no chance to prepare for.
vocab.example_zh: 批评者说，委员会用她根本来不及准备的问题突袭了她。

vocab.meaning_zh: 本义“取出内脏”，引申为抽空实质内容、使形同虚设
vocab.example_en: The amendment would eviscerate the law’s protections for whistleblowers.
vocab.example_zh: 这项修正案将掏空该法对举报人的保护。

vocab.meaning_zh: 尽管，虽然（引导让步成分，书面语，后接短语而非完整从句）
vocab.example_en: The reforms were adopted, albeit with little public debate.
vocab.example_zh: 改革方案获得了通过，尽管几乎没有公开辩论。

vocab.meaning_zh: 利用（资源、规则、优势）以达到目的
vocab.example_en: The company leveraged its legal team to wear down smaller rivals.
vocab.example_zh: 该公司利用其法务团队拖垮较小的竞争对手。

vocab.meaning_zh: （熟词僻义）使冷却、抑制；chill freedom of expression 即“使言论自由寒蝉化”
vocab.example_en: Surveillance laws can chill legitimate political speech.
vocab.example_zh: 监控法律可能会抑制正当的政治言论。

vocab.meaning_zh: （熟词僻义）永久关闭（企业、机构、场所）
vocab.example_en: The newspaper was shuttered after 40 years in print.
vocab.example_zh: 这家报纸在发行四十年后被关停。

sentences.en: Lina Attalah, a prominent Egyptian journalist and the editor-in-chief of the news outlet Mada Masr, has been released from detention by Egypt’s authorities and had her website ordered to be shut down by a court amid an intensifying crackdown on independent media in the country.
sentences.structure: 主干：Lina Attalah has been released ... and had her website ordered to be shut down ...；修饰：同位语 a prominent Egyptian journalist and the editor-in-chief ... 说明身份；介词短语 amid an intensifying crackdown on independent media 作背景状语。
sentences.analysis_zh: 这句兼有两个谓语结构：第一个是被动语态的 has been released（已获释），第二个是 have sth done 结构的 had her website ordered to be shut down（网站被下令关闭），后者暗示这是外部强加于她的、与她意愿相违的结果，语气上带有“遭受”意味。句末 amid 引导的背景状语把“获释+关站”这对矛盾并置，正是全文的核心张力。

sentences.en: Attalah’s detention, and the ordered closure of Mada Masr – which says it had applied for a licence to operate three years ago and had no reply from Egyptian authorities – follows the arrest of the entire six-person team at the independent factchecking platform Matsadaash, who were charged with belonging to the outlawed Muslim Brotherhood.
sentences.structure: 主干：Attalah’s detention, and the ordered closure of Mada Masr ... follows the arrest ...；修饰：破折号内 which 定语从句修饰 Mada Masr；the entire six-person team 后接 who 定语从句修饰 team。
sentences.analysis_zh: 主语很长（并列的两件事），谓语却只有一个一般现在时的 follows，直译是“（这两件事）都发生在……之后”，作者用这种“长主语+紧跟谓语”的笔法把两起事件串成一条时间链，暗示打压是有步骤升级的。破折号内的 which 从句是网站方的辩解（三年前已申请执照、当局不回复），在新闻写作里用来交代当事方说法，保持中立；句末 who 从句则点明前案的罪名，说明两案用的是两套不同指控。

sentences.en: “It risks fully eviscerating the narrow margin of press freedoms that have been carefully maintained in Egypt over the past decade, albeit amid great personal sacrifice – a margin that had allowed the continued operation of a handful of news outlets and human rights organisations despite frequent harassment, including through legal avenues.”
sentences.structure: 主干：It risks fully eviscerating the narrow margin of press freedoms；修饰：that have been carefully maintained ... 定语从句修饰 margin；albeit amid great personal sacrifice 让步短语；破折号后 a margin that had allowed ... 为同位语，再次带定语从句。
sentences.analysis_zh: It 指上一句的“这轮打压升级”。risk doing 表示“有……之虞”。句中 margin（余量、空间）出现了两次，第一次用完成时 have been maintained 强调十年来的持续维护，破折号后的同位语换用过去完成时 had allowed，把这一空间写成“原本还能让几家媒体运转”的最后余地——时态后移暗示这份余地如今即将失效。albeit 后接介词短语而非从句，是外刊典型的紧凑让步写法；despite frequent harassment 又进一步说明这种空间是在骚扰中勉强保住的最低限度。

sentences.en: “To escalate to the step of referral to trial must be read as a clear intent to entirely shutter the independent media space, and to permanently close what remains.”
sentences.structure: 主干：To escalate ... must be read as a clear intent ...；修饰：两个不定式 to entirely shutter ... 和 to (permanently) close ... 作 intent 的同位成分；what remains 作 close 的宾语从句。
sentences.analysis_zh: 以不定式短语 To escalate ... 作主语，是正式声明中的常见句式，语气冷静而强硬。must be read as（必须被解读为）把判断权交给“读者”，比直接说 is 更具控诉意味。shutter 这里由名词“百叶窗”转为动词“永久关停”，与句末 close what remains（封死仅存的一切）形成递进。

background.title: Mada Masr：埃及仅存的独立新闻网站之一
background.text_zh: Mada Masr 于2013年由一群埃及记者创办，以阿拉伯语和英语双语运营，长期报道埃及国内政治、人权与司法议题，在埃及本地读者之外也有相当的国际读者。自2017年起，其主站在埃及境内被封锁，读者需借助镜像站或翻墙访问；网站主要靠非营利模式和海外资助维持。埃及法律要求新闻网站向最高媒体监管机构（Supreme Council for Media Regulation）申领执照，而许多独立媒体称申请长期石沉大海，随后又在“无证运营”罪名下被起诉——这也是本案的由来。

background.title: 穆斯林兄弟会与被取缔的标签
background.text_zh: 穆斯林兄弟会（Muslim Brotherhood）是1928年成立于埃及的伊斯兰主义组织，长期在埃及社会拥有广泛基层网络。2013年穆尔西被军方罢黜后，埃及当局将穆兄会列为恐怖组织并大规模抓捕其成员。由于这一标签的适用范围在实践中相当宽泛，在埃及，只要被指控“加入穆兄会”，就足以成为羁押独立记者和活动人士的理由，人权组织多次批评此种做法被用于打压异见，而非针对具体暴力行为。

title_en: Africa’s ‘unprecedented’ Ebola outbreak could reach UK, says top health official
excerpt_en: Jean Kaseya, of the Africa CDC, warns of the illness spreading like Covid unless more funding is secured to increase preparedness and possible treatment
body_en: The “unprecedented” spread of the Ebola outbreak means it could reach the UK and other countries, according to one of Africa’s top health officials.

As the current outbreak reached 10,000 cases, with almost 5,000 deaths , Dr Jean Kaseya, director general of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), compared the outbreak to the Covid pandemic, which first took hold in China before spreading to countries across the world, claiming millions of lives, and ravaging health systems and economies.
“We want all countries to know that they are not safe if they don’t take appropriate measures,” he said.
“Each country, not only in the African region, but all continents, must now increase the preparedness level and the possibility for treatment.
“It is the first time three African regions have been affected [by Ebola]. The geographic extension of this outbreak is unprecedented,” he said.

Kaseya said leaders around the world should realise that although the brunt of the health crisis is affecting Africa at the moment, the situation could change. “We shouldn’t forget that at the beginning of Covid, many countries said there was zero risk of being affected, but a few months later, they became the hotspot,” he said. “We don’t want to see the UK and other countries become the hotspot.”
This outbreak, the 17th in the Democratic Republic of the Congo since Ebola was identified, was caused by the Bundibugyo virus and has become the largest and deadliest in the country’s history.

Ebola is a highly contagious, severe, and often fatal illness . It is spread through direct contact with body fluids such as the blood or vomit of infected people, or dead bodies, such as during funeral preparations.

On 15 May, DR Congo’s health ministry declared an outbreak in Ituri province, though sequencing shows it had begun in February. It has now spread to Kenya and Uganda in east Africa, while last week, in west Africa, Nigeria confirmed a case in the capital, Abuja , after a woman who arrived from Uganda tested positive for the virus.
France is the only non-African country to have confirmed a case of Ebola so far – a doctor who had returned from DR Congo – in June.
The Bundibugyo virus has no approved treatment, though vaccine trials are under way . The results should be available in three to six months, said Kaseya.
Of the total 10,091 cases, 10,060 have occurred in DR Congo, with 4,887 deaths. Two people have died in Uganda, and two in Kenya.

The response to the crisis has been hampered by inadequate protective equipment and unpaid health worker wages , leading to strikes. Conflict in DR Congo as well as mistrust towards officials in affected areas, misinformation and global aid cuts have further complicated the situation.

Kaseya will convene a meeting of African health ministers on Wednesday to urge greater cross-border cooperation. He wants governments to introduce screening and testing for people coming from affected regions at points of entry and exit.
“The main message to ministers is that they have to understand they could be affected, and we don’t want them to be surprised by what could happen,” he said.

At a meeting in November with African heads of state, Kaseya will call for a “corridor of peace” in conflict areas. “Currently, we have colleagues in Ituri who want to go and support the population, but they cannot because of insecurity,” he said. “I have to say to leaders, this outbreak is not for rebels, it’s not for the official army, it’s for everyone. Ebola can affect everyone … We need to come together to have a kind of agreement on how to protect each other.”

Kaseya called for a global effort to fund the response. He said governments had pledged $3bn (£2.3bn), but that more than $2bn was still outstanding. African countries had committed $120m, he said, while the rest is meant to come from international donors including the US, the UK and the EU.

“We need this money now,” he said. “We must understand that failure to provide funding now to African countries [will result in more being spent] because the outbreak will continue to move. If we have other countries affected we’ll be talking about trillions of dollars because it will require a lot of support to stop this outbreak.”

enrich.title_zh: 非洲疾控中心主任警告：埃博拉疫情“前所未有”，或蔓延至英国
enrich.summary_zh: 非洲疾控中心主任让·卡塞亚警告，本轮埃博拉疫情已波及三个非洲区域、累计超过1万例、近5000人死亡，地理扩散范围前所未有。他要求各国提高防范等级，呼吁跨境合作、筛查入境人员、设立“和平走廊”，并敦促国际社会尽快兑现30亿美元援助承诺，否则疫情将继续外溢、代价更高。

paragraphs.en: The “unprecedented” spread of the Ebola outbreak means it could reach the UK and other countries, according to one of Africa’s top health officials.
paragraphs.zh: 非洲一位高级卫生官员表示，本轮埃博拉疫情的扩散“前所未有”，这意味着它可能波及英国及其他国家。

paragraphs.en: As the current outbreak reached 10,000 cases, with almost 5,000 deaths , Dr Jean Kaseya, director general of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), compared the outbreak to the Covid pandemic, which first took hold in China before spreading to countries across the world, claiming millions of lives, and ravaging health systems and economies.
paragraphs.zh: 随着本轮疫情病例数达到1万例、死亡近5000人，非洲疾病控制与预防中心（CDC）总干事让·卡塞亚博士将此次疫情与新冠大流行相提并论——新冠最初在中国暴发，随后蔓延至世界各国，夺去数百万人的生命，重创各国卫生体系与经济。

paragraphs.en: “We want all countries to know that they are not safe if they don’t take appropriate measures,” he said.
paragraphs.zh: 他说：“我们希望所有国家都明白，如果不采取适当措施，就没有哪个国家是安全的。”

paragraphs.en: “Each country, not only in the African region, but all continents, must now increase the preparedness level and the possibility for treatment.
paragraphs.zh: “每个国家，不仅是非洲地区，而是所有大洲，现在都必须提高防范级别和收治能力。

paragraphs.en: “It is the first time three African regions have been affected [by Ebola]. The geographic extension of this outbreak is unprecedented,” he said.
paragraphs.zh: 他说：“这是首次有三个非洲地区同时受到（埃博拉）疫情影响。此次疫情在地理上的扩散范围是前所未有的。”

paragraphs.en: Kaseya said leaders around the world should realise that although the brunt of the health crisis is affecting Africa at the moment, the situation could change. “We shouldn’t forget that at the beginning of Covid, many countries said there was zero risk of being affected, but a few months later, they became the hotspot,” he said. “We don’t want to see the UK and other countries become the hotspot.”
paragraphs.zh: 卡塞亚表示，世界各国领导人应当认识到，尽管目前这场卫生危机的主要冲击落在非洲，但形势可能发生变化。他说：“我们不应忘记，新冠疫情初期，许多国家都说自己被波及的风险为零，可几个月后，它们自己就成了疫情热点地区。我们不希望看到英国和其他国家成为热点地区。”

paragraphs.en: This outbreak, the 17th in the Democratic Republic of the Congo since Ebola was identified, was caused by the Bundibugyo virus and has become the largest and deadliest in the country’s history.
paragraphs.zh: 这是自埃博拉被发现以来，刚果民主共和国发生的第17次疫情。此次疫情由本迪布焦（Bundibugyo）病毒引起，已成为该国历史上规模最大、致死人数最多的一次。

paragraphs.en: Ebola is a highly contagious, severe, and often fatal illness . It is spread through direct contact with body fluids such as the blood or vomit of infected people, or dead bodies, such as during funeral preparations.
paragraphs.zh: 埃博拉是一种传染性极强、病情严重且往往致命的疾病。它通过直接接触体液传播，例如感染者的血液、呕吐物，或死者的遗体——比如在筹备葬礼的过程中。

paragraphs.en: On 15 May, DR Congo’s health ministry declared an outbreak in Ituri province, though sequencing shows it had begun in February. It has now spread to Kenya and Uganda in east Africa, while last week, in west Africa, Nigeria confirmed a case in the capital, Abuja , after a woman who arrived from Uganda tested positive for the virus.
paragraphs.zh: 5月15日，刚果（金）卫生部宣布伊图里省发生疫情，但基因测序显示疫情早在2月就已开始。目前疫情已蔓延至东非的肯尼亚和乌干达；上周，西非的尼日利亚确认首都阿布贾出现一例病例，患者是一名从乌干达抵达的女性，其病毒检测呈阳性。

paragraphs.en: France is the only non-African country to have confirmed a case of Ebola so far – a doctor who had returned from DR Congo – in June.
paragraphs.zh: 法国是目前唯一确认出现埃博拉病例的非洲以外国家——6月，一名从刚果（金）返回的医生被确诊。

paragraphs.en: The Bundibugyo virus has no approved treatment, though vaccine trials are under way . The results should be available in three to six months, said Kaseya.
paragraphs.zh: 本迪布焦病毒目前尚无获批的治疗方法，不过疫苗试验正在进行。卡塞亚表示，试验结果预计在3至6个月内出炉。

paragraphs.en: Of the total 10,091 cases, 10,060 have occurred in DR Congo, with 4,887 deaths. Two people have died in Uganda, and two in Kenya.
paragraphs.zh: 在总计10091例病例中，10060例发生在刚果（金），其中4887人死亡。乌干达有2人死亡，肯尼亚有2人死亡。

paragraphs.en: The response to the crisis has been hampered by inadequate protective equipment and unpaid health worker wages , leading to strikes. Conflict in DR Congo as well as mistrust towards officials in affected areas, misinformation and global aid cuts have further complicated the situation.
paragraphs.zh: 应对这场危机的行动受到防护装备不足、医护人员工资拖欠的拖累，后者还引发了罢工。刚果（金）的冲突、疫区民众对官员的不信任、虚假信息以及全球援助削减，都使局势更加复杂。

paragraphs.en: Kaseya will convene a meeting of African health ministers on Wednesday to urge greater cross-border cooperation. He wants governments to introduce screening and testing for people coming from affected regions at points of entry and exit.
paragraphs.zh: 卡塞亚将于周三召集非洲各国卫生部长开会，敦促加强跨境合作。他希望各国政府在出入境口岸对来自疫区的人员进行筛查和检测。

paragraphs.en: “The main message to ministers is that they have to understand they could be affected, and we don’t want them to be surprised by what could happen,” he said.
paragraphs.zh: 他说：“我要向部长们传达的核心信息是：他们必须明白自己也可能被波及，我们不希望他们对可能发生的情况措手不及。”

paragraphs.en: At a meeting in November with African heads of state, Kaseya will call for a “corridor of peace” in conflict areas. “Currently, we have colleagues in Ituri who want to go and support the population, but they cannot because of insecurity,” he said. “I have to say to leaders, this outbreak is not for rebels, it’s not for the official army, it’s for everyone. Ebola can affect everyone … We need to come together to have a kind of agreement on how to protect each other.”
paragraphs.zh: 在11月与非洲国家元首的会议上，卡塞亚将呼吁在冲突地区建立“和平走廊”。他说：“目前我们在伊图里省的同事想去支援当地民众，但因安全局势无法前往。我必须对领导人说，这场疫情不属于反叛武装，也不属于政府军，它关乎每一个人。埃博拉可能感染任何人……我们需要团结起来，就如何相互保护达成某种协议。”

paragraphs.en: Kaseya called for a global effort to fund the response. He said governments had pledged $3bn (£2.3bn), but that more than $2bn was still outstanding. African countries had committed $120m, he said, while the rest is meant to come from international donors including the US, the UK and the EU.
paragraphs.zh: 卡塞亚呼吁全球共同努力为应对行动提供资金。他说，各国政府已承诺提供30亿美元（约23亿英镑），但仍有超过20亿美元尚未到位。他表示，非洲国家已承诺出资1.2亿美元，其余资金应来自美国、英国和欧盟等国际捐助方。

paragraphs.en: “We need this money now,” he said. “We must understand that failure to provide funding now to African countries [will result in more being spent] because the outbreak will continue to move. If we have other countries affected we’ll be talking about trillions of dollars because it will require a lot of support to stop this outbreak.”
paragraphs.zh: 他说：“我们现在就需要这笔钱。我们必须明白，现在不向非洲国家提供资金（将导致日后花费更多），因为疫情会继续扩散。如果再有其他国家被波及，我们要谈的就是数万亿美元了，因为遏制这场疫情需要大量支持。”

vocab.meaning_zh: 前所未有的；空前的
vocab.example_en: The speed of the virus's spread is unprecedented.
vocab.example_zh: 这种病毒的传播速度是前所未有的。

vocab.meaning_zh: 严重破坏；摧残（外刊常用来形容疾病、战争对经济与体系的冲击）
vocab.example_en: The pandemic ravaged health systems around the world.
vocab.example_zh: 这场大流行重创了世界各国的卫生体系。

vocab.meaning_zh: 开始扎根；开始盛行（指疫情、观念等开始形成并扩散）
vocab.example_en: The infection took hold in crowded cities before spreading nationwide.
vocab.example_zh: 这种传染病先在拥挤的城市蔓延开来，随后扩散至全国。

vocab.meaning_zh: （冲击的）主要部分；首当其冲（bear/take the brunt of）
vocab.example_en: Poorer countries are bearing the brunt of the climate crisis.
vocab.example_zh: 较贫穷的国家正承受气候危机的主要冲击。

vocab.meaning_zh: 热点地区；（疫情）高发地
vocab.example_en: The city quickly became a hotspot for the virus.
vocab.example_zh: 这座城市很快成了病毒的高发地。

vocab.meaning_zh: 传染性的；有传染力的
vocab.example_en: Measles is highly contagious.
vocab.example_zh: 麻疹传染性极强。

vocab.meaning_zh: 正在进行中（外刊高频：talks/trials are under way）
vocab.example_en: Large-scale vaccine trials are under way.
vocab.example_zh: 大规模疫苗试验正在进行。

vocab.meaning_zh: 妨碍；阻碍（常见于被动：be hampered by）
vocab.example_en: Relief efforts were hampered by heavy rain.
vocab.example_zh: 救援工作受到暴雨阻碍。

vocab.meaning_zh: （款项）尚未支付/尚未落实的（熟词僻义，此处不是“杰出的”）
vocab.example_en: More than $2bn in pledged aid is still outstanding.
vocab.example_zh: 仍有超过20亿美元的承诺援助尚未到位。

vocab.meaning_zh: 召集（会议）；召开
vocab.example_en: The director will convene a meeting of health ministers.
vocab.example_zh: 这位主任将召集各国卫生部长开会。

sentences.en: As the current outbreak reached 10,000 cases, with almost 5,000 deaths , Dr Jean Kaseya, director general of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), compared the outbreak to the Covid pandemic, which first took hold in China before spreading to countries across the world, claiming millions of lives, and ravaging health systems and economies.
sentences.structure: 主干：Dr Jean Kaseya compared the outbreak to the Covid pandemic。修饰：句首 As... 为时间状语从句；with almost 5,000 deaths 为 with 复合结构作伴随；director general of the Africa CDC 为同位语，解释人物身份；which... 引导非限制性定语从句修饰 the Covid pandemic，从句内三个并列谓语 took hold / claiming / ravaging 中后两个为现在分词，表示结果与伴随。
sentences.analysis_zh: 这句信息密度极高，一句话交代了时间背景、人物身份、核心判断与对比依据。写作上值得学习的是：把最重的主干（compare A to B）放在中间，用同位语补身份，用非限制性定语从句展开对比对象的历史，从而使读者无须另起一句就理解“为什么拿新冠作比”。翻译时不宜按英文语序硬搬，应把 as 状语前置、同位语融入人名之后。

sentences.en: It has now spread to Kenya and Uganda in east Africa, while last week, in west Africa, Nigeria confirmed a case in the capital, Abuja , after a woman who arrived from Uganda tested positive for the virus.
sentences.structure: 主干：It has now spread to Kenya and Uganda。修饰：while 引导对比并列分句（尼日利亚的情况）；in west Africa 为插入的地点状语；after a woman... 为时间状语从句，其中 who arrived from Uganda 为定语从句修饰 a woman。
sentences.analysis_zh: while 在这里不是“当……时”，而是表示对照的连词“而、与此同时”，这是外刊中极常见的用法。句子按地理顺序展开：东非（肯尼亚、乌干达）——西非（尼日利亚），最后用 after 从句交代传入链条，形成“扩散路径”的叙事逻辑，而不是简单罗列。

sentences.en: “We must understand that failure to provide funding now to African countries [will result in more being spent] because the outbreak will continue to move. If we have other countries affected we’ll be talking about trillions of dollars because it will require a lot of support to stop this outbreak.”
sentences.structure: 主干：We must understand that...。that 引导宾语从句，从句主语是 failure to provide funding now to African countries（动名词化的名词短语作主语），谓语 will result in，宾语 more being spent；because 引导原因状语从句。第二句为 If 条件句 + 主句 we'll be talking about trillions，后接 because 从句说明原因。方括号内为原文编辑后的补足成分。
sentences.analysis_zh: 这段的修辞核心是“现在省钱＝以后多花钱”的成本论证。注意 failure to do 是名词化表达，比 if we don't provide 更正式、更有力；will be talking about trillions 用将来进行时，语气上刻意轻描淡写，反而凸显数额之巨。

background.title: 非洲疾控中心（Africa CDC）
background.text_zh: 非洲疾病控制与预防中心是非洲联盟于2016年正式启动的公共卫生机构，总部设在埃塞俄比亚首都亚的斯亚贝巴，职能类似欧洲疾控中心，负责疫情监测、协调成员国应急响应与公共卫生能力建设。其总干事由非盟任命，在跨国疫情中被视为非洲卫生外交的主要发声者。它与世界卫生组织（WHO）并非同一机构，两者常被中文读者混淆。

background.title: 埃博拉与本迪布焦毒株
background.text_zh: 埃博拉病毒于1976年在刚果（金）首次被识别（因附近埃博拉河得名），此后该国已多次暴发疫情，故文中称此次为“第17次”。病毒分多个型别，扎伊尔型致死率最高、疫苗与药物相对成熟；本迪布焦型（Bundibugyo）1977年在乌干达首次发现，目前尚无获批的疫苗或特效药，这正是文中强调“疫苗试验正在进行”的分量所在。埃博拉的传播依赖直接接触体液，因此 funeral preparations（葬礼清洗遗体）是西非2014年大暴发的关键传播环节。

background.title: “和平走廊”与冲突中的防疫
background.text_zh: “走廊”在公共卫生语境中通常指为人员和物资通行划定的安全通道（如疫苗“冷链走廊”）。卡塞亚提出“和平走廊”，是希望在刚果（金）东部武装冲突地区促成交战方临时停火或通行默契，让防疫人员能够进入。刚果（金）东部长期活跃着多支反叛武装，伊图里省尤为动荡，这直接解释了文中“同事想去支援却因不安全无法前往”一句。

title_en: UK sanctions Sudanese military leaders implicated in El Fasher ‘campaign of rape’
excerpt_en: Commanders suspected of sexual violence during the largest and fastest slaughter of civilians in more than 30 years have been subjected to travel ban and asset freeze
body_en: Senior Sudanese commanders implicated in a “campaign of rape” have been targeted by the UK on the first anniversary of a mass atrocity that saw tens of thousands of civilians killed over several days.

A year after the fall of El Fasher , the British government said it had sanctioned military leaders from both sides in the country’s ongoing conflict whom it suspected of sexual violence during the siege of the city.
A total of 15 commanders from the military groups – the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) – have been subjected to a travel ban and an asset freeze .
The Foreign Office said it hoped the action would ensure “the horrors that took place at El Fasher will be known to the world”.

During the RSF’s takeover of the city, up to 10,000 men, women and children are believed to have been slaughtered over two days – the fastest and largest massacre of civilians this century . Another 40,000 remain unaccounted for.
The killings came at the end of an 18-month starvation siege by the RSF, which was allegedly backed by the United Arab Emirates (UAE). The UAE continues to deny supporting the RSF.

Fewer than 70,000 people are believed to remain in El Fasher, compared with a prewar population of more than 1 million. Life inside the city continues to be horrendous, with testimony indicating routine detention, torture and unlawful killings.

Individuals targeted by the UK’s latest sanctions include Hussein Abu Jalak, an RSF colonel linked to atrocities during the siege, which forced hundreds of thousands of civilians to live off animal feed.
Another is Al-Nour Ahmed Adam – also known as “Al-Qubba” – who was identified as playing a prominent role in the attack on the city.
A Guardian investigation earlier this year revealed internal US and UK warnings were sidelined in the run-up to the RSF attack on El Fasher, and that action that might have saved lives was not taken.

A statement to mark the anniversary of the massacre from the Coalition on Atrocity Prevention and Justice for Sudan said: “The victims will not be forgotten, survivors will be heard, and we will continue to pursue accountability for those responsible.”
During the 12 months since the fall of El Fasher, Sudan’s ruinous conflict – which has forced 14 million people to flee their homes – has developed increasingly into a drone war.
The latest strikes saw the RSF causing mass power outages across east Sudan after targeting power stations with a coordinated drone attack.

enrich.title_zh: 英国制裁卷入法希尔“强奸运动”的苏丹军事领导人
enrich.summary_zh: 在法希尔陷落一周年之际，英国对苏丹冲突双方的15名指挥官实施旅行禁令和资产冻结，指其涉嫌围城期间犯下性暴力。文章回顾了RSF长达18个月的围困、两天内多达万人被屠杀的暴行以及城内的人道惨状，并指出苏丹的毁灭性冲突正日益演变为无人机战争。

paragraphs.en: Senior Sudanese commanders implicated in a “campaign of rape” have been targeted by the UK on the first anniversary of a mass atrocity that saw tens of thousands of civilians killed over several days.
paragraphs.zh: 在一场数日内导致数万平民丧生的重大暴行发生一周年之际，英国将矛头对准了涉嫌参与“强奸运动”的苏丹高级指挥官，对其采取制裁措施。

paragraphs.en: A year after the fall of El Fasher , the British government said it had sanctioned military leaders from both sides in the country’s ongoing conflict whom it suspected of sexual violence during the siege of the city.
paragraphs.zh: 法希尔（El Fasher）陷落一年后，英国政府表示，已对苏丹持续冲突中双方的军事领导人实施制裁，这些人涉嫌在这座城市被围困期间实施性暴力。

paragraphs.en: A total of 15 commanders from the military groups – the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) – have been subjected to a travel ban and an asset freeze .
paragraphs.zh: 来自两个军事团体——快速支援部队（RSF）和苏丹武装部队（SAF）——的共15名指挥官被实施旅行禁令和资产冻结。

paragraphs.en: The Foreign Office said it hoped the action would ensure “the horrors that took place at El Fasher will be known to the world”.
paragraphs.zh: 英国外交部表示，希望这一行动能确保“法希尔发生的恐怖暴行被世界所知”。

paragraphs.en: During the RSF’s takeover of the city, up to 10,000 men, women and children are believed to have been slaughtered over two days – the fastest and largest massacre of civilians this century . Another 40,000 remain unaccounted for.
paragraphs.zh: 在RSF攻占该城期间，据信两天内有多达1万名男女老幼惨遭屠杀——这是本世纪速度最快、规模最大的一起平民屠杀。另有4万人至今下落不明。

paragraphs.en: The killings came at the end of an 18-month starvation siege by the RSF, which was allegedly backed by the United Arab Emirates (UAE). The UAE continues to deny supporting the RSF.
paragraphs.zh: 这些杀戮发生在RSF长达18个月的“饥饿围城”末期。据指称，RSF背后有阿拉伯联合酋长国（UAE）的支持。阿联酋则一直否认支持RSF。

paragraphs.en: Fewer than 70,000 people are believed to remain in El Fasher, compared with a prewar population of more than 1 million. Life inside the city continues to be horrendous, with testimony indicating routine detention, torture and unlawful killings.
paragraphs.zh: 据信法希尔城内目前仅剩不到7万人，而战前人口超过100万。城中生活依旧骇人，有证词显示，拘押、酷刑和非法杀戮已成常态。

paragraphs.en: Individuals targeted by the UK’s latest sanctions include Hussein Abu Jalak, an RSF colonel linked to atrocities during the siege, which forced hundreds of thousands of civilians to live off animal feed.
paragraphs.zh: 英国最新制裁的对象包括侯赛因·阿布·贾拉克（Hussein Abu Jalak），他是一名RSF上校，与围城期间的暴行有关；那场围城迫使数十万平民靠牲畜饲料活命。

paragraphs.en: Another is Al-Nour Ahmed Adam – also known as “Al-Qubba” – who was identified as playing a prominent role in the attack on the city.
paragraphs.zh: 另一人是努尔·艾哈迈德·阿丹（Al-Nour Ahmed Adam），又名“阿尔-库巴”（Al-Qubba），他被认定在攻打该城的行动中扮演了重要角色。

paragraphs.en: A Guardian investigation earlier this year revealed internal US and UK warnings were sidelined in the run-up to the RSF attack on El Fasher, and that action that might have saved lives was not taken.
paragraphs.zh: 《卫报》今年早些时候的一项调查披露，在RSF进攻法希尔之前，美国和英国政府内部的警告被搁置一旁，本可能挽救生命的行动也没有被采取。

paragraphs.en: A statement to mark the anniversary of the massacre from the Coalition on Atrocity Prevention and Justice for Sudan said: “The victims will not be forgotten, survivors will be heard, and we will continue to pursue accountability for those responsible.”
paragraphs.zh: “防止暴行与为苏丹伸张正义联盟”（Coalition on Atrocity Prevention and Justice for Sudan）在纪念这场大屠杀一周年的声明中说：“受害者不会被遗忘，幸存者的声音将被听见，我们将继续追究责任人的罪责。”

paragraphs.en: During the 12 months since the fall of El Fasher, Sudan’s ruinous conflict – which has forced 14 million people to flee their homes – has developed increasingly into a drone war.
paragraphs.zh: 法希尔陷落后的这12个月里，苏丹这场毁灭性的冲突——已迫使1400万人逃离家园——日益演变为一场无人机战争。

paragraphs.en: The latest strikes saw the RSF causing mass power outages across east Sudan after targeting power stations with a coordinated drone attack.
paragraphs.zh: 在最近的袭击中，RSF以协同的无人机攻击打击多座发电站，造成苏丹东部大面积停电。

vocab.meaning_zh: 涉嫌参与（犯罪或不当行为）的，有牵连的；常与 in 连用
vocab.example_en: Several officers were implicated in the cover-up of the killings.
vocab.example_zh: 几名警官涉嫌参与掩盖这些杀戮事件。

vocab.meaning_zh: 暴行，残暴行为（尤指战争中对平民的暴行）
vocab.example_en: The UN documented atrocities committed against civilians in the region.
vocab.example_zh: 联合国记录了该地区针对平民实施的暴行。

vocab.meaning_zh: 围攻，围困（切断物资与人员进出的军事行动）
vocab.example_en: The city has been under siege for more than a year.
vocab.example_zh: 这座城市已被围困一年有余。

vocab.meaning_zh: 对……实施制裁（名词 sanctions 指制裁措施，此处作动词；注意与“批准、认可”义区分）
vocab.example_en: The government sanctioned three officials linked to the crackdown.
vocab.example_zh: 政府对三名与镇压有关的官员实施了制裁。

vocab.meaning_zh: 下落不明的，未被计入的（人）
vocab.example_en: Thousands of people are still unaccounted for after the earthquake.
vocab.example_zh: 地震过后仍有数千人下落不明。

vocab.meaning_zh: 屠杀，残杀（大量杀人，也可指宰杀牲畜）
vocab.example_en: Hundreds of villagers were slaughtered in the raid.
vocab.example_zh: 数百名村民在这次袭击中被屠杀。

vocab.meaning_zh: 靠……为生，以……为食（此处指被迫以牲畜饲料果腹）
vocab.example_en: Families were left to live off leaves and animal feed.
vocab.example_zh: 许多家庭只能靠树叶和牲畜饲料活命。

vocab.meaning_zh: 被搁置，被排挤到一边，未获重视（熟词僻义：原义“使退出比赛”）
vocab.example_en: Experts warn that the warnings were sidelined for political reasons.
vocab.example_zh: 专家警告说，这些警告因政治原因被搁置一旁。

vocab.meaning_zh: 在……之前的一段时间里，在……的筹备/前奏阶段（外刊高频表达）
vocab.example_en: In the run-up to the election, tensions rose sharply.
vocab.example_zh: 选举前夕，紧张局势急剧升级。

vocab.meaning_zh: 协同的，协调一致的（多方配合行动）
vocab.example_en: The attack was a coordinated assault on three power stations.
vocab.example_zh: 这次袭击是对三座发电站的协同攻击。

sentences.en: Senior Sudanese commanders implicated in a “campaign of rape” have been targeted by the UK on the first anniversary of a mass atrocity that saw tens of thousands of civilians killed over several days.
sentences.structure: 主干：Senior Sudanese commanders ... have been targeted by the UK（主语+被动谓语+施动者）。修饰：implicated in a “campaign of rape” 为过去分词短语后置修饰 commanders；on the first anniversary of a mass atrocity 为时间状语；that saw tens of thousands of civilians killed over several days 为定语从句修饰 atrocity，其中 see 为“见证、发生”义，killed 为宾语补足语。
sentences.analysis_zh: 新闻导语常用“被动+长定语”把最重要的受制裁对象放在句首。注意 see 的拟人化用法：以“事件/时间”作主语表示“发生、见证”，比 there be 更有画面感；tens of thousands of 表约数，避免给出精确数字，符合报道对未核实伤亡的谨慎表述。

sentences.en: Individuals targeted by the UK’s latest sanctions include Hussein Abu Jalak, an RSF colonel linked to atrocities during the siege, which forced hundreds of thousands of civilians to live off animal feed.
sentences.structure: 主干：Individuals ... include Hussein Abu Jalak。修饰：targeted by the UK’s latest sanctions 为过去分词短语修饰 individuals；an RSF colonel ... 为同位语解释人名身份；linked to atrocities during the siege 为过去分词短语修饰 colonel；which forced ... 为非限制性定语从句，先行词是 the siege（不是 atrocities）。
sentences.analysis_zh: 这一句最易错的是 which 的先行词：从语义与搭配看，forced civilians to live off animal feed 的主语只能是“围城”而非“暴行”。写作上，同位语（an RSF colonel）先交代身份，再用分词与从句层层补充，是英文人物指认句的典型结构，中文翻译时宜拆成短句避免“一逗到底”。

sentences.en: A Guardian investigation earlier this year revealed internal US and UK warnings were sidelined in the run-up to the RSF attack on El Fasher, and that action that might have saved lives was not taken.
sentences.structure: 主干：A Guardian investigation ... revealed + 两个宾语从句。宾语从句一：internal US and UK warnings were sidelined in the run-up to the RSF attack on El Fasher；宾语从句二：that action that might have saved lives was not taken —— 第一个 that 引导从句，第二个 that 引导定语从句修饰 action，主句谓语是 was not taken。
sentences.analysis_zh: revealed 后接两个并列宾语从句，第二个从句前保留 that 是为了避免与前面的 and 连读时界限不清。第二个从句中出现了“that ... that ...”连续结构：第一个 that 是从句引导词，第二个 that 才是关系代词，阅读时须先抓主干 action was not taken，再回填定语 might have saved lives。'might have saved' 用虚拟语气，暗示“本可挽救却未挽救”的追责意味。

background.title: 苏丹内战与法希尔
background.text_zh: 2023年4月，苏丹武装部队（SAF）与快速支援部队（RSF）爆发全面内战，起因是双方围绕权力整合与武装改编的分歧。法希尔是北达尔富尔州首府，也是达尔富尔地区最后一个由政府军控制的城市，收容了大量流离失所者。2025年该城被RSF攻陷，被视为战争的转折点，此后针对平民的大规模暴行报道不断。达尔富尔在2003年前后曾发生被外界称为“种族灭绝”的冲突，RSF的前身金戈威德民兵即源于那段历史。

background.title: 阿联酋被指支持RSF与英国制裁机制
background.text_zh: 多份联合国专家报告与媒体调查指称，阿联酋通过乍得等渠道向RSF提供武器与后勤支持，阿联酋对此一贯否认。英国使用的是“全球人权制裁”制度（即所谓“马格尼茨基式”制裁），可对个人实施旅行禁令和资产冻结，但这类措施的实际执行力有限，主要起政治表态与声誉施压作用。
